"optimistic" ko meaning k ho
"optimistic" bhaneko asawadi, arthat ramro hunchha bhanera bishwas garne. jastai: "She is optimistic about her result."
"between" ra "among" kahile use garne?
duita manchhe ya chij ko bich ma "between" ra tin ya tyo bhanda badhi ko bich ma "among" prayog garinchha. jastai: "between Ram and Hari", "among the students".
what is a synonym for "big"?
Some synonyms for "big" are large, huge, enormous and giant.
opposite of "generous"
The opposite of "generous" is "selfish" or "mean" (not wanting to share).
antonym of "temporary"?
The antonym of "temporary" is "permanent", which means lasting for a very long time or forever.
opposite of optimistic
The opposite of "optimistic" is "pessimistic".
is it correct to say "i am having a car"?
It is better to say "I have a car." "Have" for owning things is a state, so we usually don't use the "-ing" form. But "I am having lunch" is fine, because there "have" means "eat".
"He is more taller than me" - right or wrong?
Wrong. Say "He is taller than me." Don't use "more" with a word that already has "-er".
Correct it: "Yesterday I buyed a new shirt."
Correct: "Yesterday I bought a new shirt." "Buy" is irregular, so its past tense is "bought".
is "less people" wrong?
In careful English, say "fewer people", because people can be counted. Use "less" with things you can't count, like "less noise".
is "I didn't went" correct?
No. After "didn't", use the base form of the verb: "I didn't go." The "did" already shows the past.
correct: "She can sings well."
Correct: "She can sing well." After modal verbs like "can", the verb stays in its base form.
correct the sentence - "Their is a cat on the roof."
Correct: "There is a cat on the roof." "There" is used to say something exists; "their" means "belonging to them".
is it "a hour" or "an hour"?
It is "an hour". The "h" is silent, so the word starts with a vowel sound.
what's the plural of "fish"?
The plural of "fish" is usually "fish": "I caught three fish." "Fishes" is used only when talking about different kinds of fish.
what's the past of "catch"
The past tense of "catch" is "caught", and the past participle is also "caught".
Is "funner" a real word?
"Funner" is used in casual speech, but in standard English we say "more fun": "This game is more fun than that one."
what is a noun phrase
A noun phrase is a group of words built around a noun. In "the tall old tree", the whole phrase works like one noun, with "tree" as the main word.
what are the 3 forms of the verb "speak"?
The three forms of "speak" are: speak, spoke, spoken. Example: "She has spoken to the teacher."
three forms of "begin"
The three forms of "begin" are: begin, began, begun. Example: "The class has begun."
forms of "drink"
The forms of "drink" are: drink, drank, drunk. Example: "I drank tea." / "I have drunk two cups."
forms of "choose"?
The forms of "choose" are: choose, chose, chosen. Example: "She has chosen the red dress."
what's the past tense of "fly"?
The past tense of "fly" is "flew", and the past participle is "flown": "The bird flew away." / "I have never flown in a plane."
why do leaves change colour in autumn?

Leaves are green because of chlorophyll. In autumn the days get shorter and colder, so trees stop making chlorophyll. The green fades and the yellow and orange colours that were hidden in the leaf start to show.
how do plants drink water?
Plants take in water through their roots. The water moves up through tiny tubes in the stem to the leaves, and some of it escapes from the leaves as vapour.
Why does ice float on water?
Ice floats because it is less dense than liquid water. When water freezes, its molecules spread out into a pattern with more space, so ice is lighter for the same size.
what is evaporation
Evaporation is when a liquid slowly turns into a gas. Wet clothes dry in the sun because the water in them evaporates into the air.
what is a food chain?
A food chain shows who eats whom in nature. For example: grass is eaten by a deer, and the deer is eaten by a tiger. Energy passes from one living thing to the next.
what is a herbivore
A herbivore is an animal that eats only plants. Cows, goats, deer and rabbits are herbivores.
carnivore and omnivore meaning?
A carnivore eats mainly meat, like a tiger or a lion. An omnivore eats both plants and meat, like humans, bears and crows.
What is a habitat?
A habitat is the natural home of a plant or animal, where it finds food, water and shelter. A fish's habitat is water, and a snow leopard's habitat is the high, rocky mountains.
how do bees make honey
Bees collect sweet nectar from flowers and store it in their bodies. Back in the hive, they pass it to other bees and fan it with their wings so the water dries out. The thick nectar becomes honey.
can cats see in complete darkness?
No, cats cannot see in total darkness, but they see much better than us in dim light. A special layer at the back of their eyes reflects light, which is why their eyes shine at night.
how do fish breathe underwater
Fish breathe with gills. Water goes in through the mouth and passes over the gills, which take oxygen from the water and send it into the blood.
why do we have bones?
Bones give our body shape and support, protect organs like the brain and heart, and help us move with our muscles. They also store calcium and make blood cells.
What does the heart do?
The heart is a muscle that pumps blood all around the body. The blood carries oxygen and food to every part, and brings waste back.
what do the lungs do
The lungs help us breathe. They take oxygen from the air into the blood and remove carbon dioxide, which we breathe out.
why should we eat vegetables?
Vegetables give us vitamins, minerals and fibre. They help the body fight illness, keep digestion healthy and give long-lasting energy. Try to eat different colours of vegetables each day.
what is protein and why do we need it
Protein is a nutrient that builds and repairs the body, like muscles, skin and hair. Good sources are dal, beans, eggs, milk, fish and meat.
How many teeth does an adult have?
An adult usually has 32 teeth, including the 4 wisdom teeth. Children have 20 milk teeth.
what is the largest organ of the human body
The skin is the largest organ of the human body. It protects us from germs, heat and injury.
what is a fever
A fever is when the body temperature goes higher than normal, usually above about 38 degrees Celsius. It is often the body's way of fighting an infection.
Which is the longest river in the world?
The Nile in Africa is usually called the longest river in the world, at about 6650 km. Some experts say the Amazon may be slightly longer, but the Nile is the common answer.
what is the largest hot desert
The Sahara in northern Africa is the largest hot desert in the world. If cold deserts are included, Antarctica is the largest desert.
What is the largest country in the world?
Russia is the largest country by area. It covers parts of both Europe and Asia.
smallest country in the world?
Vatican City is the smallest country in the world. It is inside the city of Rome in Italy.
which country has the most people
India has the most people in the world. It passed China in 2023.
What is the equator?
The equator is an imaginary line around the middle of the Earth. It divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres, and places near it are hot all year.
Which hemisphere is Nepal in?
Nepal is in the Northern Hemisphere, because it is north of the equator. It is also in the Eastern Hemisphere.
what is a peninsula
A peninsula is land that is surrounded by water on three sides. India is a large peninsula, with the sea on the east, west and south.
what is an island
An island is a piece of land with water all around it. Sri Lanka and Japan are island countries.
what is a river delta?
A delta is flat land formed where a river meets the sea and drops the soil it carries. The Ganges delta in Bangladesh and India is one of the largest in the world.
what is a volcano
A volcano is an opening in the Earth's surface where hot melted rock, called lava, ash and gases come out from deep inside the Earth.
what causes a tsunami?
A tsunami is a series of huge sea waves, usually caused by a strong earthquake under the sea. The sudden movement of the sea floor pushes a large amount of water.
what is a monsoon
A monsoon is a seasonal wind that brings heavy rain. In Nepal, the monsoon usually comes from June to September and brings most of the year's rain.
Which is the biggest continent?
Asia is the biggest continent, both in area and in population. Nepal is in Asia.
smallest continent?
Australia (often called Oceania with nearby islands) is the smallest continent.
what is the highest mountain in africa
Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is the highest mountain in Africa, at about 5895 meters.
where is mount fuji
Mount Fuji is in Japan. It is Japan's highest mountain and a famous volcano.
What is the Amazon?
The Amazon is a huge river and the world's largest tropical rainforest, mostly in Brazil in South America. It is home to a very large number of plants and animals.
who invented the light bulb
Thomas Edison made the first practical, long-lasting light bulb in 1879. Other inventors had worked on electric lights before him.
who made the first airplane?
The Wright brothers, Orville and Wilbur, made the first powered airplane flight in 1903 in the United States.
who invented the printing press
Johannes Gutenberg of Germany built the printing press with movable metal type around 1440. It made books much cheaper and faster to produce.
Who discovered penicillin?
Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928. It was the first antibiotic and has saved millions of lives.
who created the world wide web
Tim Berners-Lee created the World Wide Web in 1989. The internet already existed, but the web made it easy to share pages with links.
Who invented the radio?
Guglielmo Marconi from Italy is known for developing the radio in the 1890s, sending signals without wires.
who discovered x-rays
Wilhelm Roentgen, a German scientist, discovered X-rays in 1895. Doctors use X-rays to see bones inside the body.
what is Einstein famous for?
Albert Einstein is famous for his theory of relativity and the equation E = mc squared, which shows that mass and energy are related.
what did isaac newton discover
Isaac Newton described the laws of motion and the law of gravity. The story says a falling apple made him think about why things fall.
who was marie curie
Marie Curie was a scientist who studied radioactivity. She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize and the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences, physics and chemistry.
who is called the first computer programmer?
Ada Lovelace is often called the first computer programmer. In the 1840s, she wrote steps for Charles Babbage's planned machine to calculate numbers.
Who was Mahatma Gandhi?
Mahatma Gandhi was a leader of India's independence movement. He used peaceful protest and non-violence to fight British rule.
who was nelson mandela
Nelson Mandela fought against apartheid (racial separation) in South Africa. After 27 years in prison, he became the country's first Black president in 1994.
what does a pharmacist do?
A pharmacist prepares and gives out medicines and explains how to take them safely. They can also advise on side effects.
What does an architect do?
An architect designs buildings. They plan how a house, school or office will look and make drawings for builders to follow.
what's the job of an accountant
An accountant keeps and checks financial records, like income, spending and taxes, for people or companies.
what does a journalist do
A journalist collects news, checks facts and writes or reports stories for newspapers, TV, radio or websites.
plumber means what?
A plumber is a person who fits and repairs water pipes, taps, toilets and drains.
what is an electrician
An electrician is a person who installs and repairs electric wires, switches, lights and other electrical things.
what does jealous mean
"Jealous" means feeling unhappy because someone else has something you want, or being afraid of losing someone's love to another person.
meaning of embarrassed
"Embarrassed" means feeling shy, silly or uncomfortable because of something you did in front of others. Example: "I was embarrassed when I fell on the stage."
What does proud mean?
"Proud" means feeling pleased about something you or someone close to you did. Example: "My parents were proud of my result."
lonely and alone, same?
Not exactly. "Alone" means without other people, and you can be happy alone. "Lonely" means feeling sad because you want company.
a person who writes books is called?
A person who writes books is called an author or a writer.
one word for a place where books are kept
A place where books are kept for reading or borrowing is a library.
what do you call a doctor who treats teeth
A doctor who treats teeth is called a dentist.
what is a person who travels to work every day called?
A person who travels some distance to work or school every day is called a commuter.
one word: a person who can speak two languages
A person who can speak two languages is bilingual.
what is a baby cow called
A baby cow is called a calf. The plural is "calves".
baby dog name?
A baby dog is called a puppy.
what do you call a baby cat
A baby cat is called a kitten.
What is a young lion called?
A young lion is called a cub. Baby bears and tigers are also called cubs.
baby horse is called?
A baby horse is called a foal.
what is a baby sheep called
A baby sheep is called a lamb.
what is a baby goat called
A baby goat is called a kid.
What sound does a horse make?
A horse neighs.
what sound does a donkey make
A donkey brays.
lion sound in english?
A lion roars.
what do we say for the sound a snake makes
A snake hisses.
what is a dog's house called?
A dog's house is called a kennel.
where does a bee live
Bees live in a hive.
what's a lion's home called
A lion's home is called a den.
where does a horse live?
A horse lives in a stable.
feminine of actor
The feminine of "actor" is "actress", though many people now use "actor" for both men and women.
What is the female of lion?
The female of "lion" is "lioness".
opposite gender of nephew
The female form of "nephew" is "niece".
masculine of queen?
The masculine of "queen" is "king".
what is the feminine of host
The feminine of "host" is "hostess", but "host" is also used for everyone today.
collective noun for lions
A group of lions is called a pride.
what do you call a group of bees?
A group of bees is called a swarm.
group of fish is called?
A group of fish is called a school (or a shoal).
what's a group of wolves called
A group of wolves is called a pack.
collective noun of ships?
A group of ships is called a fleet.
I bought a notebook for 85 rupees and gave 100. How much change should I get?
You should get 15 rupees back.
It is 10:00 in Kathmandu. What time is it in Delhi?
It is 9:45 in Delhi.
messages.think: Nepal is 15 minutes ahead of India. 10:00 minus 15 minutes is 9:45.

messages.content: 4 friends share 1000 rupees equally. How much does each get?
Each friend gets 250 rupees.
A box has 24 pencils. How many pencils are in 7 boxes?
There are 168 pencils in 7 boxes.
Pokhara is 200 km from Kathmandu. A car goes at 40 km per hour. How long will it take?
It will take 5 hours.
30 out of 40 students passed. What percent passed?
75% of the students passed.
If I save 1500 rupees every month, how much will I save in a year?
You will save 18000 rupees in a year.
A garden is 15 m long and 9 m wide. What is its area?
The area of the garden is 135 square meters.
how many days are in january, february and march together in a normal year?
In a normal year, January, February and March have 90 days together.
A field is 50 m by 30 m. How long is a fence around it?
The fence must be 160 meters long.
In a class of 36, the ratio of boys to girls is 4:5. How many girls are there?
There are 20 girls in the class (and 16 boys).
What is two-thirds of 90?
Two-thirds of 90 is 60.
How many milliliters are in 2.5 liters?
2.5 liters is 2500 milliliters.
In the morning it was 8 degrees and in the afternoon 21 degrees. How much did it rise?
The temperature rose by 13 degrees.
Ram is 12 and his father is 3 times as old. What is the sum of their ages?
Ram's father is 36, so together their ages add up to 48.
A shirt costs 1200 rupees. There is 13% tax. How much tax is that?
The tax is 156 rupees, so the total is 1356 rupees.
A train has 8 coaches with 72 seats each. How many seats in all?
The train has 576 seats in all.
A tank holds 500 liters. 120 liters are used in the morning and 95 in the evening. How much is left?
285 liters are left in the tank.
What is 1/4 of 2 hours in minutes?
One quarter of 2 hours is 30 minutes.
I read 15 pages a day. How many days to finish a 240-page book?
You will finish the book in 16 days.
How do I start learning to type fast?
Learn the home row first: put your fingers on A S D F and J K L ;. Look at the screen, not the keys, and practise 10 to 15 minutes daily with a free typing tutor. Accuracy first, speed comes later.
how do I make a simple monthly budget?

Write your total monthly income first. List fixed costs like rent, food and travel, then set an amount to save. Whatever is left is for other spending. Track your spending each week and adjust next month.
I had a fight with my best friend. What should I do?

Give it a little time to cool down, then talk calmly and in private. Say how you felt without blaming, for example "I felt hurt when...", and listen to their side too. A sincere sorry from either side often fixes a lot.
how do I keep a house plant alive?

Put it where it gets the right light for its type, usually bright but not direct hot sun. Water only when the top of the soil feels dry, and make sure the pot has a drainage hole. Too much water kills more plants than too little.
tips for a long bus trip in nepal

Carry water, light snacks and a small bag for rubbish. If you get motion sickness, sit near the front, look out of the window and eat lightly before the trip. Keep your phone charged, and wear comfortable layers since the weather changes with altitude.
What should I do during an earthquake?

Drop down, cover your head and neck under a strong table, and hold on until the shaking stops. Stay away from windows and heavy things that can fall. If you are outside, move to an open space away from buildings and wires.
how to treat a small burn at home

Cool the burn under clean running water for about 20 minutes. Do not put ice, toothpaste or oil on it. Cover it loosely with a clean cloth. If the burn is large, deep or on the face, see a doctor quickly.
what to do for a nosebleed?

Sit up and lean slightly forward, not back. Pinch the soft part of your nose for about 10 minutes and breathe through your mouth. If it does not stop after 20 minutes or happened after an injury, see a doctor.
how can I clean my phone screen safely?
Switch the phone off and wipe the screen with a soft, slightly damp microfibre cloth. Don't spray water directly on it, and avoid strong cleaners. Dry it gently afterwards.
how do I back up my photos?
Copy them to at least one other place, like a computer, an external drive or a cloud service. Doing it regularly, for example once a month, means you won't lose them if your phone breaks.
how to avoid mosquito bites
Sleep under a mosquito net, use repellent cream, and wear long sleeves in the evening. Don't let water collect in pots, tyres or buckets, because mosquitoes breed in still water.
today is my birthday!
Happy birthday! I hope your day is full of good food, laughter and people you love. Any special plans?
it's raining all day here
Rainy days can be cosy. A good day for hot tea and something to read! Are you staying indoors today?
happy dashain!
Happy Dashain to you too! May this festival bring you blessings, good health and lots of happiness with your family.
happy tihar to you
Thank you, and a very happy Tihar to you and your family! May your home be filled with light and joy.
i'm hungry
Time for a snack! Maybe some fruit, roasted chana, or a boiled egg if you want something quick. Or is it almost time for a full meal?
will you be my friend?
Of course! I'm happy to chat with you anytime. What would you like to talk about?
I got a new job today!
Congratulations! That's fantastic news. What kind of work will you be doing?
my exam went badly
I'm sorry, that feels awful. One exam doesn't decide your future. Think about what was hardest, and we can make a plan so the next one goes better.
i miss my family, i'm working abroad
That must be really hard. Missing them shows how much you love them. Try to set a regular time to call them, and keep some photos close. Is there someone near you that you can talk to?
tell me something interesting
Here's one: octopuses have three hearts and blue blood. Two hearts pump blood to the gills, and one pumps it to the rest of the body.
good night, talk tomorrow
Good night! Sleep well, and I'll be here when you want to chat again.
"embarrassed" ko matlab k ho?
"embarrassed" bhaneko aru ko agadi lajjit ya asahaj mahasus garnu ho. jastai: "I was embarrassed when I forgot my lines."
proud bhaneko k ho nepali ma?
"proud" bhaneko garva garne. jastai: "I am proud of my sister" bhaneko malai mero bahini prati garva chha.
lonely ra alone ma farak bhana na
"alone" bhaneko eklai hunu ho, jasma dukha nahuna pani sakchha. "lonely" bhaneko eklopan le dukhi mahasus garnu ho.
pharmacist le k kaam garchha?
"pharmacist" le aushadhi tayar garne, dine ra kasari khane bhanera bujhaune kaam garchha. nepali ma yaslai aushadhi bigyan ko bigya bhanna sakinchha.
"puppy" bhaneko k ho?
"puppy" bhaneko kukur ko chhauna ho. biralo ko bachcha lai "kitten" bhaninchha.
library lai nepali ma k bhanchha?
"library" lai nepali ma pustakalaya bhaninchha, jaha padhna ra saparna kitab rakhinchha.
"commuter" ko arth bhannus
"commuter" bhaneko din dinai ghar bata kaam ya padhai garne thau samma aawatjawat garne manchhe ho.
"drop, cover and hold on" bhaneko k ho?
yo bhukampa ko bela garne surakshya ko tarika ho: "drop" bhaneko tala basnu, "cover" bhaneko baliyo table muni tauko chhopnu, ra "hold on" bhaneko hallaai nasakinjel samatirahanu.
"kitten" ko nepali?
"kitten" bhaneko biralo ko bachcha ho.
"jealous" ko arth k hunchha?
"jealous" bhaneko irshya garne, arthat arko sanga bhayeko kura aafu sanga nabhayera dukhi hune. jastai: "He was jealous of his friend's new bike."
"bilingual" bhaneko k ho?
"bilingual" bhaneko duita bhasa bolna sakne manchhe. jastai nepali ra english dubai bolne manchhe bilingual ho.
"swarm" kun shabda ho?
"swarm" bhaneko maha ya kira ko thulo jhund ho. jastai: "a swarm of bees" bhaneko maha ko jhund.
what is the opposite of "ancient" and "noisy"?
The opposite of "ancient" is "modern", and the opposite of "noisy" is "quiet".
opposite of "accept"
The opposite of "accept" is "refuse" or "reject".
what is the opposite of "rich"?
The opposite of "rich" is "poor".
Give the opposite of "victory".
The opposite of "victory" is "defeat".
opposite of "increase"
The opposite of "increase" is "decrease".
antonym of "early"?
The antonym of "early" is "late".
synonym for "tired"
Some synonyms for "tired" are exhausted, sleepy and worn out.
another word for "smart"
Other words for "smart" are clever, intelligent, bright and wise.
give me a synonym of "begin"
Synonyms of "begin" are start and commence.
what's a synonym for "angry"?
Synonyms for "angry" include mad, upset, annoyed and furious (very angry).
what is a compound word
A compound word is made by joining two words: "sun" + "flower" = "sunflower", "foot" + "ball" = "football".
what is a silent letter? examples
A silent letter is written but not spoken. Examples: the "k" in "knife", the "w" in "write", the "b" in "thumb" and the "h" in "hour".
what is alliteration
Alliteration is when nearby words start with the same sound, like "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers". It is often used in poems and slogans.
what is a simile?
A simile compares two things using "like" or "as". Examples: "as brave as a lion", "she sings like a bird".
what is a metaphor
A metaphor compares two things by saying one thing is another, without "like" or "as". Example: "Time is money" or "My brother is a lazy cat on Sundays."
What is a rhyme?
Words rhyme when their endings sound the same, like "cat" and "hat", or "light" and "night". Many poems and songs use rhyme.
what is a vowel sound vs a vowel letter?
Vowel letters are a, e, i, o, u. A vowel sound is what we hear. "Hour" starts with the letter h but a vowel sound, so we say "an hour".
what's the difference between "lie" and "lay"?
"Lie" means to rest your body flat: "I lie on the bed." "Lay" means to put something down: "Lay the book on the table." The past tense of "lie" is "lay", which is why it gets confusing.
"Each students has a book" - correct it
Correct: "Each student has a book." After "each", use a singular noun.
is this right: "I am living in Kathmandu since 2019"?
Better: "I have been living in Kathmandu since 2019" or "I have lived in Kathmandu since 2019." With "since", we use the present perfect.
correct: "The news are good."
Correct: "The news is good." "News" is uncountable and takes a singular verb, even though it ends in "s".
correct: "He is elder than me."
Correct: "He is older than me." We use "older" with "than"; "elder" is used before a noun, like "my elder brother".
correct this: "I prefer tea than coffee."
Correct: "I prefer tea to coffee." With "prefer", we use "to", not "than".
which is right, "discuss about" or "discuss"?
Just "discuss": "We discussed the plan." "Discuss" already includes the meaning of "about". But you can say "a discussion about the plan".
"Return back" thik ho?
"return back" ma dohoro arth hunchha, kinabhane "return" ko arth nai farkinu ho. "I will return tomorrow" matra lekhda pugchha.
"cousin brother" english ma sahi ho?
english ma "cousin" matra bhanda pugchha, keta ya keti dubai ko lagi. "my cousin" bhanera pachhi "he" ya "she" le kun ho bhanna sakinchha.
what is the past tense of "lead"?
The past tense of "lead" is "led": "She led the team to victory."
past form of "sell"
The past tense of "sell" is "sold", and the past participle is also "sold".
past tense of "ring"
The forms of "ring" are: ring, rang, rung. Example: "The bell rang." / "Has the bell rung?"
what are the forms of "steal"
The forms of "steal" are: steal, stole, stolen. Example: "Someone stole my bag." / "My bag was stolen."
past participle of "forget"
The past participle of "forget" is "forgotten": "I have forgotten his name." The past tense is "forgot".
what is a fraction?
A fraction shows a part of a whole. In 3/4, the whole is cut into 4 equal parts and we take 3 of them.
numerator and denominator meaning
In a fraction, the numerator is the top number and the denominator is the bottom number. In 2/5, 2 is the numerator and 5 is the denominator.
what is a decimal number
A decimal number uses a point to show parts of a whole. In 4.5, the 4 is the whole number and .5 means 5 tenths, or one half.
what does percent mean?
"Percent" means "out of 100". So 30% means 30 out of every 100.
what is a factor?
A factor is a number that divides another number exactly. The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.
what is a multiple
A multiple is what you get when you multiply a number by 1, 2, 3 and so on. The multiples of 5 are 5, 10, 15, 20 and so on.
what are integers
Integers are whole numbers and their negatives, including zero: ... -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3 ... They have no fractions or decimals.
What is a negative number?
A negative number is less than zero. It is written with a minus sign, like -5. Temperatures below zero on a cold mountain are negative numbers.
place value of 7 in 4728?
In 4728, the digit 7 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 700.
round 368 to the nearest ten
368 rounded to the nearest ten is 370, because the ones digit 8 is 5 or more, so we round up.
difference between area and perimeter
Perimeter is the distance around the outside of a shape, measured in units like meters. Area is the space inside the shape, measured in square units like square meters.
what is volume?
Volume is the amount of space an object takes up or can hold. It is measured in cubic units like cubic cm, or in liters for liquids.
what is a ratio
A ratio compares two amounts. If there are 3 boys and 2 girls, the ratio of boys to girls is 3:2.
What are mean, median and mode?
The mean is the average (add all and divide by how many). The median is the middle value when the numbers are in order. The mode is the value that appears most often.
find the median of 3, 9, 4, 7, 5
The median is 5.
messages.think: in order: 3, 4, 5, 7, 9. the middle (3rd) value is 5.

messages.content: what is the mode of 2, 4, 4, 6, 4, 8
The mode is 4, because 4 appears most often (3 times).
what is probability in simple words
Probability tells how likely something is to happen, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). When you toss a coin, the probability of heads is 1/2.
probability of rolling a 6 on a dice?
A dice has 6 equal faces and only one of them is 6, so the probability is 1/6.
what is an acute angle?
An acute angle is smaller than 90 degrees. The angle between the hands of a clock at 1 o'clock is acute.
what is an obtuse angle
An obtuse angle is bigger than 90 degrees but smaller than 180 degrees.
what's a reflex angle
A reflex angle is bigger than 180 degrees but smaller than 360 degrees.
types of triangles by sides
By sides, there are three types: equilateral (all 3 sides equal), isosceles (2 sides equal) and scalene (no sides equal).
how many sides does a pentagon have?
A pentagon has 5 sides.
how many sides in an octagon
An octagon has 8 sides. Many stop signs are octagons.
radius and diameter difference
The radius goes from the centre of a circle to its edge. The diameter goes all the way across through the centre, so it is twice the radius.
if the radius of a circle is 7 cm, what is the diameter?
The diameter is 14 cm.
what are parallel lines
Parallel lines are lines that always stay the same distance apart and never meet, like the two rails of a railway track.
what are perpendicular lines?
Perpendicular lines meet or cross at a right angle (90 degrees), like the corner of a book.
what is an equation
An equation is a math sentence that says two things are equal, using "=". For example, 3 + 4 = 7. An equation can also have an unknown, like "x plus 2 equals 5", where x is 3.
solve x + 5 = 12
solve 3x = 21
solve 2x + 4 = 10
what is x if x - 9 = 15?
what is XIV in roman numerals?
XIV is 14.
write 50 in roman numerals
50 is written as L in Roman numerals.
roman numeral for 100 and 1000?
100 is C and 1000 is M in Roman numerals. Also, 500 is D.
what is 2026 in roman numerals
2026 is MMXXVI in Roman numerals.
how do I know if a number is divisible by 3?
Add its digits. If the sum can be divided by 3, the number can too. For 471: 4 + 7 + 1 = 12, and 12 is divisible by 3, so 471 is divisible by 3.
divisibility rule for 9
A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9. For 729: 7 + 2 + 9 = 18, so 729 is divisible by 9.
when is a number divisible by 5?
A number is divisible by 5 if its last digit is 0 or 5, like 35, 120 or 905.
what is BODMAS
BODMAS tells the order to solve a math problem: Brackets, Orders (powers and roots), Division and Multiplication (left to right), then Addition and Subtraction (left to right).
what is 6 + 4 x 2?
6 + 4 x 2 = 14, because we multiply before adding.
solve (8 + 2) x 5
what is 20 - 12 / 4?
square root of 144
The square root of 144 is 12.
what is 10 to the power 3
10 to the power 3 is 1000.
change 0.35 into a percentage
what is 45% as a decimal
45% is 0.45 as a decimal.
simplify 12/16
12/16 simplifies to 3/4.
messages.think: 12 and 16 can both be divided by 4. 12 / 4 = 3 and 16 / 4 = 4.

messages.content: which is bigger, 2/3 or 3/5?
2/3 is bigger than 3/5.
multiply 2/3 by 3/4
what are the three states of matter?
The three common states of matter are solid, liquid and gas. Ice is a solid, water is a liquid and steam is a gas.
what is the melting point of ice?
Ice melts at 0 degrees Celsius. Below that, water stays frozen.
what are conductors and insulators
Conductors let electricity or heat pass through easily, like copper and iron. Insulators do not, like rubber, plastic, wood and glass.
magnets: what are the poles?
Every magnet has two poles, north and south. Opposite poles attract each other, and the same poles push each other away.
name the simple machines
The six simple machines are the lever, pulley, wheel and axle, inclined plane (ramp), wedge and screw. They make work easier.
what are the parts of a plant
The main parts of a plant are the roots, stem, leaves, flowers, fruits and seeds. Roots take in water, leaves make food, and flowers help make seeds.
parts of a flower?
The main parts of a flower are the petals, sepals, stamens (male part, with pollen) and the pistil (female part). After pollination, the pistil can grow into a fruit with seeds.
what happens in the digestive system?

Food is chewed in the mouth, goes down the food pipe to the stomach, and is broken down further in the small intestine, where nutrients go into the blood. The large intestine takes back water, and waste leaves the body.
what are the five senses?
The five senses are sight (eyes), hearing (ears), smell (nose), taste (tongue) and touch (skin).
list the planets in order from the sun
From the sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. A trick to remember: "My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Noodles."
why does the moon change shape?
The moon does not really change shape. As it goes around Earth, we see different amounts of its sunlit side, so it looks full, half or thin like a crescent.
what causes day and night?
Day and night happen because the Earth spins on its axis once about every 24 hours. The side facing the sun has day, and the side away from the sun has night.
what is friction
Friction is a force that slows things down when two surfaces rub together. It helps our shoes grip the ground, and it makes our hands warm when we rub them.
what is energy?
Energy is the ability to do work or make things change. It comes in forms like heat, light, sound, electricity and movement, and it can change from one form to another.
renewable vs non renewable energy
Renewable energy comes from sources that do not run out, like sun, wind and flowing water. Non-renewable energy comes from sources that will run out, like coal, oil and gas.
what is air pollution
Air pollution is when the air has harmful gases, smoke or dust in it. Vehicle smoke, factories, burning rubbish and dust from roads are common causes.
why should we recycle?
Recycling turns used things like paper, plastic, glass and metal into new products. It saves resources and energy, and it reduces waste in landfills and rivers.
what is global warming
Global warming is the slow rise in Earth's average temperature. It happens mainly because burning coal, oil and gas adds gases like carbon dioxide that trap heat in the air.
what is democracy?
Democracy is a system of government where people choose their leaders by voting. People have rights like freedom of speech, and leaders must follow the law.
what is a constitution
A constitution is the main law of a country. It explains how the government works and lists the rights and duties of citizens.
what is an election
An election is when people vote to choose their leaders or representatives. In Nepal, citizens aged 18 and above can vote.
what is a map scale
A map scale shows how distances on the map compare to real distances. For example, 1 cm on the map might equal 10 km on the ground.
if 1 cm on a map is 5 km, how far is 7 cm?
7 cm on the map is 35 km on the ground.
what are the four main directions
The four main directions are north, south, east and west. The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
what is a census?
A census is an official count of all the people in a country, with details like age and education. Nepal holds a census every 10 years.
What are rights and duties?

Rights are things every person should be allowed to have or do, like education and free speech. Duties are things we should do for others and the country, like obeying laws and keeping our surroundings clean.
what is a computer?
A computer is a machine that takes in information, processes it with instructions, and gives a result. It can store data and do tasks very fast.
hardware vs software
Hardware is the physical part of a computer you can touch, like the keyboard, screen and mouse. Software is the programs and apps that tell the hardware what to do.
what is a CPU
The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the "brain" of the computer. It follows instructions and does the calculations.
what is an operating system
An operating system is the main software that runs a computer or phone and lets other programs work. Windows, macOS and Linux are examples.
what is the internet?
The internet is a huge network that connects computers and phones all over the world, so they can share information, websites, messages and videos.
what is an email
An email (electronic mail) is a message sent from one person to another over the internet. It can include text, pictures and files.
what is a web browser
A web browser is an app used to open websites. Chrome, Firefox and Safari are examples.
what is wifi
Wi-Fi is a way to connect devices to the internet without wires, using radio signals from a router.
What does Ctrl+C do?
Ctrl+C copies the selected text or file. Then Ctrl+V pastes it where you want.
what is ctrl z for
Ctrl+Z undoes your last action, like deleting a word by mistake. Ctrl+Y (or Ctrl+Shift+Z in some apps) redoes it.
what is the difference between a file and a folder
A file is a single item, like a document, photo or song. A folder is like a box that holds files and other folders to keep them organised.
what is a computer virus?
A computer virus is a harmful program that can spread to other files or computers and damage data or steal information. Antivirus software and careful downloading help protect you.
what is cloud storage
Cloud storage means saving your files on internet servers instead of only on your own device. You can open them from any device with your login.
what is an app
An app (application) is a program made to do a task, like sending messages, taking photos or playing games, on a phone or computer.
what is a URL
A URL is the address of a web page, like "www.example.com". You type it into a browser to open that page.
what does "download" mean?
To download means to copy a file from the internet onto your device. "Upload" is the opposite: sending a file from your device to the internet.
what is a keyboard shortcut to save a file?
On most computers, Ctrl+S saves the file you are working on. On a Mac, it is Command+S.
what is spam email
Spam is unwanted email sent to many people, often ads or scams. Don't click strange links in spam, and never share passwords by email.
what is phishing?
Phishing is a trick where someone pretends to be a bank, company or friend to steal your password or money. Always check the sender, and don't share OTP codes with anyone.
numerator bhaneko k ho?
"numerator" bhaneko bhinna (fraction) ko mathi ko sankhya ho. jastai 3/4 ma 3 numerator ra 4 "denominator" ho.
BODMAS bhaneko k ho nepali ma bujhaunus
"BODMAS" le hisab garne kram janauchha: pahila koshthak (Brackets), ani ghat (Orders), tyas pachhi bhag ra gun, antma jod ra ghatau. jastai 6 + 4 x 2 ma pahila 4 x 2 = 8 garinchha, ani 6 + 8 = 14.
perimeter ra area ko farak k ho?
"perimeter" bhaneko kunai aakar ko bahiri kinara ko jamma lambai ho. "area" bhaneko tyo aakar bhitra ko thau (chhetrafal) ho, jun square meter jasta ekai ma naapinchha.
ctrl+c le k garchha?
"Ctrl+C" le chhaneko akshar ya file copy garchha. tyas pachhi "Ctrl+V" thichera chahiyeko thau ma paste garna sakinchha.
hardware ra software ko farak nepali ma
"hardware" bhaneko computer ko chhuna milne bhag ho, jastai keyboard, mouse ra screen. "software" bhaneko computer lai kaam garna sikaune program ho, jastai app ra operating system.
acute angle bhaneko k ho?
"acute angle" bhaneko 90 degree bhanda sano kon ho. 90 degree ko kon lai "right angle" ra 90 bhanda thulo tara 180 bhanda sano lai "obtuse angle" bhaninchha.
"median" kasari nikalne?
"median" nikalna sabai sankhya lai sano dekhi thulo kram ma rakhnus ra thik bich ko sankhya hernus. jastai 2, 5, 9 ma median 5 ho.
"equilateral triangle" ko arth?
"equilateral triangle" bhaneko tinai bhuja barabar bhayeko tribhuj ho. yasko tinai kon pani 60 degree ka hunchhan.

"renewable energy" bhaneko nasakine srot bata aaune urja ho, jastai ghaam, hawa ra bagne pani. nepal ma jalvidyut nai mukhya renewable energy ho.

What is a thermometer used for?
A thermometer measures temperature, for example how hot your body is or how cold the air is.
what does a barometer measure?
A barometer measures air pressure. Falling pressure often means bad weather may come.
what is a microscope?
A microscope is an instrument that makes very tiny things look bigger, so we can see cells, germs and small details.
what is a telescope used for
A telescope makes far-away things look closer. People use it to look at the moon, planets and stars.
what does a compass do?
A compass has a magnetic needle that points north. It helps people find directions when travelling.
what is a stethoscope
A stethoscope is a tool doctors use to listen to the heart, lungs and stomach.
what is an ecosystem
An ecosystem is a community of living things, like plants, animals and tiny organisms, together with their surroundings such as water, soil and air. A forest and a pond are ecosystems.
what does "endangered" mean?
An endangered animal or plant is at serious risk of disappearing forever. The red panda and the snow leopard are endangered.
what is soil erosion
Soil erosion is when the top layer of soil is washed or blown away by rain, rivers or wind. Planting trees and grass helps hold the soil.
what is deforestation?
Deforestation is cutting down forests on a large scale. It can cause landslides, floods and loss of animal homes.
write a short paragraph on my school

"My school is a place where I learn and grow. It has a big playground, a small library and kind teachers. I enjoy reading in the library and playing football with my friends. My school teaches me to be honest and work hard."
write 3 sentences about a cow

"The rainy season brings fresh water for our fields and makes the hills green. But heavy rain can also cause floods and landslides, so we must stay careful."
help me describe Pokhara in 3 lines
"Pokhara is a beautiful lake city in Gandaki Province. Phewa Lake reflects the snowy Annapurna mountains on clear days. Visitors enjoy boating, paragliding and the peaceful air."
How do I politely ask my boss for a day off?

You could say: "Excuse me, sir/madam. I have a family matter on Friday. Would it be possible for me to take the day off? I will finish my pending work before that." Ask early and offer a plan for your work.
what can I say when shopping to ask the price?
You can ask: "How much is this?" or "How much does this cost?" To bargain politely: "Could you give me a small discount?"
how do I ask for directions in english
Say: "Excuse me, could you tell me the way to the bus park?" or "How do I get to the hospital from here?" Then: "Is it far?" and "Thank you!"
What do I say to a doctor about my problem?
Start with the main problem and how long it has lasted: "I have had a headache and fever for three days." Then mention other signs, any medicines you took, and allergies if you have any.
help me introduce myself in english
Example: "Hello, my name is Sita Rai. I am from Dhankuta, and I live in Kathmandu now. I am studying business in college. In my free time, I like reading and playing badminton. Nice to meet you!"
how to answer a phone call in english formally?
You can say: "Hello, this is Ram speaking. How may I help you?" At the end: "Thank you for calling. Have a good day."
How do I apologise properly in English?
Say what you did and that you are sorry, then how you will fix it: "I'm sorry I was late today. I should have left earlier. It won't happen again." Keep it simple and sincere.
what are some nice ways to compliment someone?
Try: "You did a great job on this!", "That colour looks really good on you," or "Thank you for being so helpful." Specific compliments feel more sincere.
how do I start small talk with a stranger?
Start with something you both share: "Busy day today, isn't it?" or "Is this the bus to Lalitpur?" Then ask an easy question like "Do you travel this way often?" Smile and listen.
what does "what's up" mean?
"What's up?" is a casual way to say "Hi, how are you?" or "What are you doing?" A common reply is "Not much, you?"
how should I reply to "how's it going"?
You can say "Pretty good, thanks! How about you?" or "Not bad, a bit busy." It's a friendly, casual greeting.
meaning of "take care"
"Take care" is a kind way to say goodbye, meaning "look after yourself". You can reply "You too!"
what does "no worries" mean
"No worries" means "It's okay" or "Don't worry about it." People say it after someone says sorry or thank you.
what does "my bad" mean?
"My bad" is a casual way to say "It was my mistake, sorry." Use it with friends, not in formal situations.
what does "sounds good" mean
"Sounds good" means you agree with a plan or idea. Example: "Let's meet at 5." "Sounds good!"
what does "let's call it a day" mean
"Let's call it a day" means "Let's stop working for today." Example: "We've done enough. Let's call it a day."
what does "under the weather" mean?
"Under the weather" means feeling a little sick. Example: "I'm feeling under the weather, so I'll stay home."
meaning of "cost an arm and a leg"
"Cost an arm and a leg" means something is very expensive. Example: "That new phone costs an arm and a leg."
what does "spill the beans" mean?
"Spill the beans" means to tell a secret. Example: "Who spilled the beans about the surprise party?"
hit the sack meaning
"Hit the sack" means to go to bed. Example: "I'm really tired, I'm going to hit the sack."
what is "bite the bullet"
"Bite the bullet" means to do something difficult or unpleasant that you have been avoiding. Example: "I bit the bullet and went to the dentist."
meaning of "let the cat out of the bag"
It means to reveal a secret by mistake. Example: "She let the cat out of the bag about her brother's wedding."
"when pigs fly" meaning
"When pigs fly" means something will never happen. Example: "He'll clean his room when pigs fly!"
what does "burn the midnight oil" mean?
It means to work or study late into the night. Example: "Before exams, many students burn the midnight oil."
"get cold feet" meaning?
"Get cold feet" means to suddenly feel nervous and not want to do something you planned. Example: "He got cold feet before his speech."
what does "over the moon" mean
"Over the moon" means extremely happy. Example: "She was over the moon when she got the scholarship."
"the ball is in your court" means?
It means it is now your turn to decide or act. Example: "I've made my offer; the ball is in your court."
what does "beat around the bush" mean
It means to avoid saying something directly. Example: "Stop beating around the bush and tell me what happened."
"make a decision" or "do a decision"?
The correct phrase is "make a decision". We also say "make a mistake", "make a choice" and "make a plan".
is it "take a photo" or "make a photo"?
In English we usually say "take a photo" (or "take a picture").
"do exercise" or "make exercise"?
Say "do exercise" or simply "exercise": "I do exercise every morning" or "I exercise every morning."
have a shower or take a shower?
Both are correct. "Have a shower" is more common in British English, and "take a shower" in American English.
how do you pronounce "th"?
Put the tip of your tongue lightly between your teeth and blow air. For "think" and "three" the sound is soft with no voice; for "this" and "mother" you add your voice.
how to say -ed at the end of verbs?
There are three sounds: "t" after sounds like p, k, s, sh, ch (walked, washed), "d" after most other sounds (played, called), and "id" after t or d (wanted, needed).
colour or color, which is right?
Both are right. "Colour" is British spelling and "color" is American spelling. Just use one style consistently in your writing.
centre vs center?
"Centre" is British spelling and "center" is American spelling. They mean the same thing.
lift and elevator, same?
Yes. "Lift" is British English and "elevator" is American English. Both mean the machine that carries people between floors.
what is a flat in british english
In British English, a "flat" is a set of rooms to live in, on one floor of a building. Americans usually call it an "apartment".
petrol vs gas
"Petrol" (British) and "gas" or "gasoline" (American) mean the same fuel for cars and motorbikes.
biscuit or cookie?
In British English, a sweet baked snack is usually a "biscuit"; in American English it's a "cookie". In America, a "biscuit" is a soft bread roll.
is "kids" ok in formal writing?
In formal writing, "children" is better. "Kids" is fine in casual speech and friendly messages.
Formal word for "get" in a letter?
Depending on meaning, you can use "receive" ("I received your letter"), "obtain" ("to obtain a permit") or "become" ("it became dark").
what is a CV?
A CV (curriculum vitae) is a document that lists your education, work experience, skills and contact details. Employers read it to decide whether to interview you.
what should a CV have?
Include your name and contact details, a short summary, education, work experience (latest first), skills, languages and maybe references. Keep it clear, true and 1 or 2 pages long.
what is a cover letter
A cover letter is a short letter sent with your CV. It explains why you want the job and why you are a good fit, in about 3 or 4 short paragraphs.
how to write a good email subject line?
Make it short and clear about the purpose, like "Leave request for 12 March" or "Application for Accountant position". Avoid writing only "Hi" or leaving it blank.

How should I check a foreign job agency before paying?

Check that the agency is licensed by the Department of Foreign Employment, and ask for a written contract with salary, job and hours. Never hand over your passport or big payments without a receipt. Talk to people who went through the same agency.
I feel homesick in a new country. any advice?

Homesickness is very normal. Keep a regular time to call family, cook a familiar meal sometimes, and try to meet other people from Nepal or new friends at work. Keep busy with a small routine, and it usually gets easier with time.
How can I control my anger?

When you feel angry, stop and take 5 slow, deep breaths before you speak. Walk away for a few minutes if you can. Later, talk calmly about what upset you. Regular exercise and enough sleep also help keep your temper calmer.
tips to improve handwriting
Hold the pen loosely and sit with good posture. Write slowly at first, keeping letters the same size and spacing. Practise a few lines every day, and copy neat writing samples.
how do I learn a new skill quickly?
Pick one small part and practise it daily, even for 20 minutes. Learn from a good video or teacher, then try it yourself right away. Ask for feedback and keep notes of mistakes.
How do I build a reading habit?
Start with short, interesting books, and read 10 pages every day at a fixed time, like before bed. Keep a book with you, and don't force yourself to finish books you don't enjoy.
how can I stay motivated?

Set a clear goal and break it into small steps you can finish each day. Track your progress so you can see it grow, and reward yourself for small wins. On low days, just do a tiny part instead of nothing.
I got my first salary. How should I plan it?

Congratulations! First, set aside some money as savings, even 10 to 20 percent. Pay your needs like rent and food, then plan a small treat for yourself or your family. Try to start an emergency fund for surprises.
how should i answer "what is your weakness" in an interview
Choose a real but small weakness and show how you are improving it. Example: "I sometimes take too long on details, so now I set time limits for each task." Don't say "I have no weakness."
How do I answer "Tell me about yourself"?

Keep it to about one minute: your current role or studies, one or two key skills or achievements, and why you want this job. Example: "I recently finished my BBS. I worked as an intern in accounts, where I learned to manage records. I'm interested in this job because..."
why do you want this job - how to answer?

what questions can I ask at the end of an interview?

what is the difference between "job" and "work"?
"Job" is countable and means a paid position: "She has a new job." "Work" is usually uncountable and means activity or effort: "I have a lot of work today."
"Can you borrow me your pen?" is that right?
Not quite. Say "Can you lend me your pen?" or "Can I borrow your pen?" You lend to someone; you borrow from someone.
what is the difference between "hear" and "listen"?
"Hear" is just noticing sound: "I heard a noise." "Listen" means paying attention on purpose: "Listen to your teacher."
see, look and watch - difference?
"See" is noticing with your eyes without trying. "Look" is directing your eyes at something on purpose. "Watch" is looking at something that moves or changes for a while, like TV or a match.
"speak" or "talk"?
Both mean saying words. "Speak" is a bit more formal and is used for languages ("speak English"). "Talk" is more casual and often means a conversation ("talk to a friend").
"excited for" or "excited about"?
"Excited about" is the most common: "I'm excited about the trip." "Excited for" is used for people ("I'm excited for you") and also for events in casual speech.
what's the difference between "fun" and "funny"?
"Fun" means enjoyable: "The picnic was fun." "Funny" means it makes you laugh: "The joke was funny."
"boring" vs "bored"
"Bored" is how you feel: "I am bored." "Boring" describes the thing that causes it: "The film is boring."
"interested" or "interesting"?
"Interested" is how a person feels: "I'm interested in science." "Interesting" describes the thing: "Science is interesting."
"everyday" or "every day"?
"Every day" (two words) means each day: "I walk every day." "Everyday" (one word) is an adjective meaning ordinary: "everyday clothes".
"maybe" vs "may be"
"Maybe" (one word) means perhaps: "Maybe it will rain." "May be" (two words) is a verb: "It may be cold tonight."
"into" or "in to"?
"Into" shows movement inside something: "She walked into the room." "In to" is used when "in" belongs to the verb: "He handed his homework in to the teacher."
when do we use "whom"?
Use "whom" when the person is the object of a verb or preposition: "To whom did you give the book?" In everyday speech, many people just say "who".
is "alot" a word?
No, "alot" is a spelling mistake. Write "a lot" as two words: "Thanks a lot."
"could of" or "could have"?
The correct form is "could have" (short: "could've"). "Could of" is a common mistake because they sound similar when spoken.
what is the difference between "assure", "ensure" and "insure"?
"Assure" means to tell someone to remove doubt: "I assure you it's safe." "Ensure" means to make certain: "Ensure the door is locked." "Insure" means to buy insurance: "Insure your bike."
"loose" or "lose" weight?
It is "lose weight". "Lose" means to have less of something; "loose" means not tight.
"breath" vs "breathe"
"Breath" is a noun: "Take a deep breath." "Breathe" is a verb: "Breathe slowly."
"dying" or "dyeing"?
"Dying" comes from "die" (stop living). "Dyeing" comes from "dye" (change the colour): "She is dyeing her hair."

How do I invite a friend to dinner in English?
You could say: "Hey! Would you like to come over for dinner on Saturday at 7? I'm making dal bhat and momo. Let me know if you can come!"
how do I politely say no to an invitation?

How do I end a conversation politely?
You can say: "It was really nice talking to you. I have to go now, but let's talk again soon. Take care!"
what are the four types of sentences?

The four types are: declarative (a statement: "I like tea."), interrogative (a question: "Do you like tea?"), imperative (a command: "Drink your tea.") and exclamatory (strong feeling: "What great tea!").
what is a clause?
A clause is a group of words with a subject and a verb. A main clause can stand alone ("I stayed home"), but a subordinate clause cannot ("because it rained").
"The team is" or "the team are"?
Both can be correct. In American English, "the team is" is usual because the team is one unit. In British English, "the team are" is also common when thinking of the members.
either or, neither nor - which verb form?
With "either...or" and "neither...nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject: "Neither the boys nor the teacher is here." / "Either Ram or his friends are coming."
is "furnitures" correct?
No. "Furniture" is uncountable, so it has no plural. Say "some furniture" or "three pieces of furniture". "Luggage" and "equipment" work the same way.
do we say "the Everest" or just "Everest"?
Just "Everest" or "Mount Everest". Single mountains usually have no "the", but rivers and mountain ranges do: "the Koshi", "the Himalayas".
why do we say "the USA" but just "Nepal"?

We use "the" with country names that include words like "States", "Kingdom" or "Republic", or that are plural: "the USA", "the UK", "the Maldives". Most single-name countries, like Nepal, India and Japan, have no "the".
too or very?
"Very" just makes a word stronger: "The tea is very hot." "Too" means more than is good or needed: "The tea is too hot to drink."
how to use "enough"
"Enough" comes after adjectives and before nouns: "He is tall enough." / "We have enough rice." It means as much as needed.
already vs yet

"Already" means something happened earlier than expected, mostly in positive sentences: "I have already eaten." "Yet" is used in questions and negatives: "Have you eaten yet?" / "I haven't eaten yet."
ago or before?
"Ago" counts back from now: "I came 2 years ago." "Before" counts back from another past time, or means "earlier": "I had met him two years before that."
will vs going to
Use "going to" for plans and for things you can see coming: "I'm going to visit Pokhara." / "Look at those clouds, it's going to rain." Use "will" for quick decisions and promises: "I'll help you."
"I have seen him yesterday" - correct?
Not correct. With a finished time like "yesterday", use the simple past: "I saw him yesterday." Use the present perfect without a finished time: "I have seen him before."
although vs despite
"Although" is followed by a full clause: "Although it rained, we played." "Despite" is followed by a noun or -ing form: "Despite the rain, we played."
what does "unless" mean?
"Unless" means "if not". "You will miss the bus unless you hurry" means "if you don't hurry, you will miss the bus."
how to use "I wish"
For wishes about now, use "wish" + past tense: "I wish I had a bike." For regrets about the past, use "wish" + had + past participle: "I wish I had studied harder."
what does "you had better" mean?
"Had better" gives strong advice or a warning: "You'd better take an umbrella, or you'll get wet." It is followed by the base verb.
would rather meaning
"Would rather" shows what you prefer: "I would rather stay home than go out tonight." It is followed by the base verb.
change to reported speech: He said to me, "Sit down."
Reported speech: He told me to sit down. For commands, we use "told" + person + "to" + verb.
passive of "You must finish the work."
Passive voice: "The work must be finished." With modals, use modal + "be" + past participle.
who, which and that in relative clauses
Use "who" for people, "which" for things, and "that" for either in defining clauses: "the man who called", "the bag which I bought", "the book that you gave me".
whose vs who's
"Whose" asks about ownership: "Whose phone is this?" "Who's" is short for "who is" or "who has": "Who's coming?"
a lot of vs lots of
They mean the same, "a large amount or number". "Lots of" is a little more casual: "lots of friends", "a lot of work".
each vs every
Both take a singular noun. "Each" looks at members one by one, often in a small group: "Each student got a book." "Every" sees the whole group: "Every student in Nepal studies maths."
what does "as ... as" mean in comparison?
"As ... as" shows two things are equal: "Hari is as tall as Ram." In negative form, it shows a difference: "This bag is not as heavy as that one."
farther or further?
"Farther" is for physical distance: "Dharan is farther than Itahari from here." "Further" can mean distance too, but is also used for "more": "further information".
little vs a little
"A little" means some, enough: "I have a little money, so let's buy tea." "Little" means almost none: "There is little hope."
what's the difference between "start" and "begin"?
They mean almost the same. "Begin" is slightly more formal. But for machines we use "start": "Start the engine," not "begin the engine."
what is drizzle?
Drizzle is very light rain with tiny drops. It is softer than a normal shower.
what does downpour mean
A downpour is a sudden, very heavy fall of rain.
what does humid mean?
"Humid" means the air has a lot of water vapour, so it feels damp and sticky. Terai summers are often hot and humid.
meaning of chilly
"Chilly" means unpleasantly cold, but not freezing. Example: "It's chilly this morning, wear a jacket."
which body part joins the hand and the arm?
The wrist joins the hand and the arm. The elbow is the joint in the middle of the arm, and the ankle joins the foot and the leg.
what is a ladle?
A ladle is a big spoon with a long handle and a deep bowl, used to serve soup or dal.
what's a colander
A colander is a bowl with many small holes, used to drain water from washed vegetables, rice or noodles.
what is a grater used for
A grater is a kitchen tool with sharp holes used to cut food into small thin pieces, like grated carrot or cheese.
what are in-laws?
In-laws are the family of your husband or wife, like your mother-in-law (spouse's mother) or brother-in-law.
what is a stepmother
A stepmother is the wife of your father who is not your birth mother.
what's an itinerary?
An itinerary is a plan of a journey, showing where you will go and when. Example: "Day 1: Kathmandu to Pokhara. Day 2: Sarangkot."
what is a boarding pass
A boarding pass is the card or paper that lets you get on a plane. It shows your name, flight, gate and seat number.
syllabus meaning
A syllabus is a list of the topics that will be taught and tested in a course or subject.
what is a semester
A semester is half of a school or college year, usually about 5 or 6 months long, with exams at the end.
what's the difference between curriculum and syllabus?
A curriculum is the whole plan of what a school teaches across subjects and years. A syllabus is the detailed list of topics for one subject or course.
what is an agenda in a meeting
An agenda is a list of topics to discuss in a meeting, in order. It helps the meeting stay focused.
what are minutes of a meeting?
Minutes are the written record of a meeting: who attended, what was discussed and what was decided.
what is a loan
A loan is money you borrow, usually from a bank, that you must pay back later, often with interest.
what is interest in banking?
Interest is the extra money paid for using money. If you borrow, you pay interest to the bank; if you save, the bank pays interest to you.
what is an EMI?
EMI means Equated Monthly Instalment: a fixed amount you pay every month to repay a loan, including part of the loan and the interest.
what is a savings account
A savings account is a bank account where you keep money safe and earn some interest. You can take money out when you need it.

How do I take good notes in class?
Write key words and short phrases, not every word. Use headings, bullet points and arrows to link ideas. After class, spend 5 minutes reading your notes and adding anything you missed.
how do I revise for exams effectively?

Make a timetable that covers every subject, starting with the hardest. Test yourself with questions instead of only reading, and use old papers. Review each topic a few times over several days, not just once.
tips for SEE exam preparation

Know your full syllabus and mark weak topics. Practise past SEE question papers within the time limit, especially maths and science. Write neat answers with steps, and get enough sleep in the last week instead of studying all night.
how do I choose a subject for plus two?

Think about what you enjoy and are good at, and what jobs you might like later. Science suits medicine and engineering, management suits business and banking, and humanities or law suit many other paths. Talk to teachers, seniors and family before deciding.
how do I talk to my parents about my career choice?

Choose a calm time and explain your interest with facts: what the career is, how to study for it and what jobs it can lead to. Listen to their worries too. Showing a clear plan often helps parents feel more comfortable.
should I keep a diary?
A diary can help you understand your feelings, remember good moments and improve your writing. Even 5 minutes a night, writing 3 things that happened, is enough. Keep it private and honest.
I want to start exercising but I'm out of shape
Start small: a 15 to 20 minute walk every day is a great beginning. Add some light stretching, and slowly increase the time each week. If you have a health condition, check with a doctor first.
how to reduce sugar in my diet?
Cut down slowly: use less sugar in tea each week, and swap sweets and soft drinks for fruit. Read labels, because packaged foods often have hidden sugar. Drink water when you feel like a sweet drink.
how can I sleep early?
Set a fixed bedtime and wake-up time, even on weekends. Dim the lights and put your phone away an hour before bed. Avoid heavy meals and tea late in the evening.
how to reduce screen time?

Check your phone's screen time to see where the hours go. Turn off non-essential notifications, keep the phone out of the bedroom, and set app time limits. Replace scrolling with a walk, a book or talking to family.
I didn't get the result I wanted. What now?

It's okay to feel disappointed. Look at the result calmly and find which parts went wrong. Many paths are still open, like re-exams, other courses or a different plan. Talk with a teacher or family member to choose the next step.
my friends pressure me to do things I don't want

You have the right to say no. Say it clearly and simply: "No, I don't want to." Spend more time with people who respect your choices. If the pressure is about something harmful, talk to a trusted adult.
someone is bullying me online

I'm sorry that's happening. Don't reply to the bully. Save screenshots as proof, block the person and report them on the app. Tell a trusted adult or teacher, and if there are threats, contact the police.
how can kids stay safe online?

Never share your address, school name, passwords or photos with strangers. Don't meet online friends in person without a parent. If something online makes you feel scared or uncomfortable, tell a parent or teacher.
how do I know if news is fake?
Check who published it and whether well-known news sites report the same thing. Look at the date, and be careful with shocking headlines or edited photos. If you are unsure, don't share it.
tell me some facts about Nepal

Nepal is a country in South Asia between China and India. Its capital is Kathmandu, and it has 7 provinces and 77 districts. Mount Everest, the highest mountain in the world, and Lumbini, the birthplace of Buddha, are in Nepal.
What is Nepal famous for?
Nepal is famous for the Himalayas, including Mount Everest, for Lumbini where Buddha was born, for temples and stupas in Kathmandu Valley, and for wildlife like one-horned rhinos in Chitwan.
what currency does nepal use?
Nepal uses the Nepali rupee. Notes and coins are issued by Nepal Rastra Bank.
What language is spoken in Nepal?
Nepali is the official language and is spoken across the country. Many other languages are also spoken, like Maithili, Bhojpuri, Tharu, Tamang and Newar (Nepal Bhasa).
what is the biggest festival in nepal
Dashain is the biggest festival in Nepal. Families gather, elders give tika and jamara, and people fly kites and play on swings.
what is lumbini known for?
Lumbini, in Rupandehi district, is known as the birthplace of Gautam Buddha. It has the Maya Devi Temple, the Ashoka Pillar and many monasteries built by different countries.
what does "namaste" mean
"Namaste" is a respectful greeting in Nepal, said with palms pressed together. It is often explained as "I bow to you".

humid ko nepali k hunchha?

is it "on the weekend" or "at the weekend"?
Both are used. "At the weekend" is common in British English, and "on the weekend" in American English.
what's the plural of "cactus"?
The plural of "cactus" can be "cacti" or "cactuses". Both are accepted.
what is the plural of "crisis"?
The plural of "crisis" is "crises". Similar words: "analysis" becomes "analyses" and "thesis" becomes "theses".
plural of "phenomenon"?
The plural of "phenomenon" is "phenomena".
plural of "potato"
The plural of "potato" is "potatoes". "Tomato" becomes "tomatoes" in the same way, but "photo" becomes "photos".
plural of "leaf"?
The plural of "leaf" is "leaves".
what's the plural of "deer"
The plural of "deer" is "deer". We say "one deer" and "five deer".
what is the singular of "data"?
Strictly, the singular is "datum", but today most people treat "data" as uncountable: "The data is ready." In science writing, "the data are" is also used.
what is the comparative of "far"?
The comparative of "far" is "farther" or "further", and the superlative is "farthest" or "furthest".
superlative of "little"
The superlative of "little" (amount) is "least": little, less, least.
comparative of "many"?
The comparative of "many" is "more", and the superlative is "most".
what's the adverb form of "good"?
The adverb of "good" is "well": "She is a good singer. She sings well."
noun form of "decide"
The noun form of "decide" is "decision".
what is the noun of "happy"?
The noun of "happy" is "happiness".
verb form of "success"
The verb form of "success" is "succeed". The adjective is "successful".
adjective of "danger"?
The adjective of "danger" is "dangerous".
noun form of "strong"
The noun form of "strong" is "strength".
what is the adjective form of "beauty"?
The adjective form of "beauty" is "beautiful".
noun of "free"
The noun of "free" is "freedom".
what's the opposite of "include"?
The opposite of "include" is "exclude".
opposite of "arrival"
The opposite of "arrival" is "departure".
antonym of "expand"?
The antonym of "expand" is "contract" or "shrink".
what is the opposite of "honest"
The opposite of "honest" is "dishonest".
opposite of "possible"?
The opposite of "possible" is "impossible".
what's the opposite of "legal"?
The opposite of "legal" is "illegal".
the opposite of "responsible"
The opposite of "responsible" is "irresponsible".
why do some opposites start with "il", "im" or "ir"?
The prefix "in" (meaning "not") changes to match the next sound: "il" before l (illegal), "im" before m or p (impossible, immature), and "ir" before r (irregular).
Can you check my sentence: "I am very much happy today."
Better: "I am very happy today." We don't use "much" before "happy" in this way.
check: "She is married with a doctor."

correct: "I am waiting you."

correct this: "He explained me the problem."

correct: "Can you tell me where is the bank?"
Correct: "Can you tell me where the bank is?" Inside a polite question, use normal word order.
correct: "I have two sisters and one brothers."
Correct: "I have two sisters and one brother." After "one", the noun is singular.
correct this: "Did you went to school?"
Correct: "Did you go to school?" After "did", use the base form of the verb.
is "I am knowing him" right?

what is a palindrome?
A palindrome is a word, number or sentence that reads the same backwards and forwards, like "madam", "level", "racecar" or 12321.
what's an anagram
An anagram is a word made by rearranging the letters of another word. For example, "listen" can become "silent", and "earth" can become "heart".
what is an acronym?
An acronym is a word made from the first letters of other words, and it is said as a word, like NASA or UNESCO. When you say each letter, like "UN", it is often called an abbreviation or initialism.
what does ASAP mean
ASAP means "as soon as possible". Example: "Please reply ASAP."
FYI meaning?
FYI means "for your information". People use it when sharing something useful: "FYI, the office is closed on Friday."
what does BTW stand for
BTW means "by the way". It is used in casual messages to add another point.
difference between e.g. and i.e.
"e.g." means "for example": "fruits, e.g. apples and bananas". "i.e." means "that is" and explains exactly: "the capital, i.e. Kathmandu".
what does etc. mean?
"etc." is short for the Latin "et cetera", meaning "and so on". Example: "Bring pens, pencils, erasers, etc."
what do a.m. and p.m. mean
"a.m." means the time from midnight to noon, and "p.m." means from noon to midnight. So 7 a.m. is morning and 7 p.m. is evening.
what is RSVP on an invitation?
RSVP comes from French and means "please reply". The host wants to know whether you will come.
what does UN stand for
UN stands for the United Nations, an organisation of countries working for peace and cooperation. Nepal joined it in 1955.
what is WHO?
WHO is the World Health Organization, a United Nations agency that works on health around the world. Its headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland.
full form of SAARC
SAARC stands for the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation. It has 8 member countries, and its secretariat is in Kathmandu.
what is an NGO?
NGO stands for Non-Governmental Organization. It is a group, not run by the government, that works on things like education, health or the environment.
What does GDP mean?
GDP means Gross Domestic Product: the total value of all goods and services produced in a country in a year. It is used to measure the size of an economy.
what does CEO stand for
CEO stands for Chief Executive Officer, the top manager of a company.
ATM full form?
ATM stands for Automated Teller Machine, a machine that lets you take out cash with a bank card.
what is a PIN?
PIN stands for Personal Identification Number, a secret number used with a card or phone. Never share it with anyone.
what does OTP mean
OTP means One-Time Password, a code sent to your phone that works only once. Banks and apps use it to check it is really you, so never tell it to anyone.
what is a SIM card
SIM stands for Subscriber Identity Module. The small SIM card in your phone connects it to your mobile network and number.
what does PDF stand for?
PDF stands for Portable Document Format, a file type that keeps a document looking the same on any device.
what is USB
USB stands for Universal Serial Bus, a common type of port and cable used to connect and charge devices.
what does GPS mean?
GPS stands for Global Positioning System. It uses satellites to find your exact location, which map apps use for directions.
what is DIY
DIY means "do it yourself": making or repairing something yourself instead of paying someone.
VIP meaning
VIP means "very important person", someone who gets special treatment, like a guest of honour.

What is BMI?
BMI (Body Mass Index) is a rough measure of body weight for height: weight in kg divided by height in meters squared. For most adults, a BMI from 18.5 to 24.9 is considered healthy.

what is a calorie?
A calorie is a unit of energy. On food labels, "calories" (really kilocalories) tell how much energy the food gives your body.
what is cholesterol in simple words
Cholesterol is a fatty substance in the blood. The body needs some, but too much of the "bad" kind (LDL) can block blood vessels and raise the risk of heart disease.
what is blood pressure
Blood pressure is the force of blood pushing on the walls of your blood vessels. It is written as two numbers, like 120/80; high blood pressure can harm the heart and kidneys.
what are carbohydrates
Carbohydrates are the body's main source of energy. Rice, roti, potatoes, maize and fruit are rich in carbohydrates.
what does DNA do
DNA carries the instructions for how a living thing grows and works. You get half of your DNA from your mother and half from your father.
why do we need sleep?
Sleep lets the body repair itself and helps the brain store memories and clear waste. Without enough sleep, focus, mood and immunity get worse.
