My sister is coming home from Dubai next week. What should I cook for her first dinner?
Cook something simple that she has missed: dal bhat with gundruk, or momo if she likes it. Ask her which dish she missed most and make that one. The first meal at home should feel normal, not fancy.
I want to start running in the mornings. How much should I run on the first day?
Start small: walk fast for ten minutes and run slowly for two or three minutes in between. If you can still talk while running, your speed is right. Add a little more each week.
Tomorrow is my first day at a new college and I am nervous.
That feeling is normal. Take a notebook and a pen, reach a little early, and speak to one person sitting near you. Everyone there is new on the first day too.
how to make friends in a new class where everyone already knows each other?
Sit near someone who looks friendly and ask a small question, like "Is this the maths class?" or "Did sir give any notes yesterday?" One small question often starts a friendship.
My neighbour plays loud music late at night. What can I say politely?
Say: "Namaste, I am sorry to disturb you. The music is a little loud at night and my children are sleeping. Could you please lower it after ten?" Say it calmly in person, not in anger.
how do I say no to a friend who keeps asking to borrow money?
Be clear and kind: "I am sorry, I cannot lend money right now." You do not need a long reason. A short answer said honestly is better than a promise you cannot keep.
my younger brother eats only junk food. how to change him?
Do not lecture him. Cook one simple home dish he likes and eat it with him, keep fruit where he can see it, and let him choose. Habits change slowly, and nagging usually makes them worse.
my friends always go out to eat and I can't afford it every week. what should I do?
Be honest: "I am saving money this month, so I will join you for tea instead." Suggest cheaper plans, like a walk or cooking together at someone's room. Good friends will understand.
my laptop has become very slow. what can I try first?

Restart it, close the programs you are not using, and delete big files you do not need, because a nearly full disk slows a computer down. If it is still slow after that, ask a repair shop to check it.
how to keep vegetables fresh for longer without a fridge?
Keep them dry, wrap them in newspaper or a cloth, and store them in a cool dark place. Do not wash them until you are ready to cook. Onions and potatoes should stay out of the plastic bag.
Is it too late to learn cycling at 26?
No, it is not late. Start on a small quiet road with the seat low so both feet reach the ground. Practise balance for ten minutes a day. Many adults learn within a few weeks.
My mother is alone at home all day. What can she do to pass the time?

Ask her what she enjoyed before marriage or before the children grew up: singing, sewing, gardening, or meeting neighbours. Help her start one small thing, like a few plants on the roof or a weekly walk with a friend.
The shopkeeper gave me less change today. How do I say it without arguing?
Say kindly: "Excuse me, I think the change is short by twenty rupees. Could you check again?" Show the note you paid with. Most mistakes are honest, so start politely.
I always forget where I put my keys. Any trick?
Choose one fixed place, like a hook or a bowl near the door, and put the keys there every time you come in. After two or three weeks it becomes a habit and you stop searching.
My exam is next week and I have not studied anything yet.

Pick the two subjects that worry you most and study only those today. Make a short list of the main topics, then read one topic and close the book and say it aloud. Something is better than nothing, and panic wastes the time you have.
how do I wake up early in winter?

Put the alarm far from the bed so you have to stand up to stop it, and keep warm clothes ready beside you. Sleep early the night before. Waking up is easier when you already know what you will do first.
how to keep a room cool in summer without an AC?
Close the curtains on the sunny side during the day and open the windows at night. A wet cloth or a bowl of water near the window helps a little. Use a fan on the floor, since cool air stays low.
how can I talk to a new colleague without sounding strange?
Start with work: "How long have you been on this team?" or "Do you know where the printer is?" Work questions are easy and natural, and friendship usually follows later.
what should I gift my teacher on teacher's day?
A card with a few honest lines is better than an expensive gift. Write one thing she taught you that you still remember. If you want to add something, a small plant or a pen is enough.
How do I dry clothes in the rainy season when nothing dries?
Hang them near an open window with a fan running, and leave space between the clothes so air can move. Thin cotton dries faster than thick towels, so wash those first.
A stray dog follows me on my way to school. What should I do?
Do not run and do not stare at it. Walk calmly and slowly, and do not put your hand out. If it keeps following, tell an adult nearby. Most stray dogs follow for food, not to bite.
there is an ink stain on my white shirt, how to remove it?
Blot it with a clean cloth, then rub a little soap and cold water on the stain before washing. Do not use hot water first, because heat fixes the stain into the cloth.
how to keep ants out of the kitchen?
Keep sugar, honey and sweets in closed containers, wipe the shelf with a wet cloth daily, and put the rubbish bin outside at night. Ants follow a smell trail, so cleaning the trail is the real fix.
My father's birthday is coming. Any small gift idea that is not expensive?
Think about what he uses every day. A good torch, a warm cap, a photo of the family in a frame, or a shirt in his colour. A useful gift from your own money means more than a costly one.
how do I start a conversation at a wedding where I know almost nobody?
Ask about the wedding itself: "Are you from the bride's side or the groom's?" or "The food is really good, have you tried the sel roti?" Such questions are easy to answer and start a talk.
what do I say to a friend whose father is in hospital?
Keep it simple: "I heard about your father. I am sorry. Is there anything I can do?" Do not give medical advice and do not say "everything will be fine". Just being there is enough.
how to ask for a seat on a crowded bus politely?
Say: "Excuse me, could I sit here? I am not feeling well." If the person says no, thank them anyway and move on. On a long journey, asking clearly is better than standing silently.
a tourist asked me the way to the bus park and I froze. what could I have said?

Give short steps with a landmark: "Go straight down this road, then turn left at the (landmark). The bus park is on your right." If you are not sure of the way, say: "Sorry, I am not sure. You could ask at that shop."
my younger sister copies my homework every day
Tell her kindly that you will help her understand instead of giving the answers: "Sit with me for twenty minutes and I will explain this chapter." If it continues, tell your parents calmly.
Write a short message to a friend who is moving to another city.
"I will really miss you. Thank you for all the tea and the long talks. Message me when you reach, and come back to visit whenever you can. Your friend always."
Help me write a two-line note to put on my shop door.
Here is a simple one: "Shop closed for a short time. Back at (time). Thank you for waiting." Write the time in numbers so people can read it from the road.
Write a message to a colleague asking for a file.
"Hi (name), could you please send me the (name of the file) when you have a minute? I need it to finish my part of the work. Thank you!"
Write a short thank you note to my neighbour who watered my plants.
"Thank you so much for watering my plants. It was very kind of you, and they look healthy and green. Please come over for tea one evening."
I read my sister's diary by mistake. How do I apologise to her?

"I am really sorry that I read your diary. It was your private space, and I should have closed it at once. It will not happen again, and I will not talk about what I saw." Say it in person if you can.
write a message to cancel my appointment at the clinic
"Namaste, this is (your name). I have an appointment on (day) at (time), but I am sorry, I cannot come. Could I move it to another day? Thank you."
write a short message asking my friend to return my book
"Hi, hope you are well. Could you please bring my book back when you get a chance? Thanks a lot!" A short, friendly message works better than a long reminder.
write a message to my landlord asking him to repaint the room
"Namaste sir, I wanted to ask if my room could be repainted. Could you please let me know when it would be possible? Thank you."
what does "considerate" mean?
A considerate person thinks about other people's feelings and needs. Example: "It was considerate of you to call before visiting." In Nepali you could say "arka ko khyal garne".
explain "reluctant" in simple words
"Reluctant" means not wanting to do something, so you do it slowly or unhappily, like "anakani garnu" in Nepali. Example: "He was reluctant to lend his new bike." The noun is "reluctance".
what is the meaning of "sensible"?

"Sensible" means showing good judgement. A sensible person takes an umbrella when the sky is dark. Example: "It was sensible of her to save money every month." In Nepali you could say "bibekshil" or "samajhdar".
what does "look forward to" mean? my teacher wrote it in an email

"Look forward to" means to wait happily for something. "I look forward to meeting you" means "I am glad that we will meet." After "to", use a noun or an -ing verb: "I look forward to hearing from you."
meaning of "in a hurry"? I saw it in a story.
"In a hurry" means moving fast because you have little time. Example: "He left in a hurry and forgot his keys."
is "He has two childrens" correct?
No. Say: "He has two children." "Children" is already plural, so it does not take another "s".
"I have 20 years old" - is this right?
No. Say: "I am 20 years old." In English, age uses the verb "be", not "have", even though Nepali uses "chha".
check this: "My father is doctor"
Say: "My father is a doctor." A job needs "a" or "an" before it: a doctor, an engineer, a teacher.
is "My mother she is a teacher" ok?
No. Say: "My mother is a teacher." Do not repeat the subject with "she" after "my mother"; one subject is enough.
correct my sentence: "I am going to home"
Say: "I am going home." The word "home" does not take "to" after verbs like go, come and walk.
is "I can able to swim" right?
No. Say "I can swim" or "I am able to swim." "Can" and "able to" mean the same thing, so use only one of them.
please check: "Today morning I went to the bank"

Say: "This morning I went to the bank." In English we say "this morning", "this evening" and "tonight", not "today morning". In the same way, "yesterday night" should be "last night". The mistake comes from Nepali "aaja bihana" and "hijo raati".
what does the Nepali word "dhukuti" mean in English?

"Dhukuti" means a treasury or a store where money, grain or precious things are kept safe. For example, "desh ko dhukuti" is the national treasury, and "gyan ko dhukuti" means a treasure of knowledge. Do not mix it up with "dhikuti", which is a group savings fund.
how do I answer when someone says thank you?
Say: "You are welcome." With friends you can also say "No problem" or "Anytime". A short warm reply is enough.
How can I say "dhanyabad" in a stronger way in English?
Say "Thank you so much" or "I am really grateful for your help." For a big favour, add the reason: "Thank you so much for waiting for me."
my friend replied "Never mind" to me. is she angry?
Probably not. "Never mind" usually means "It is not important, forget it." If she writes it in a short way after you apologise, she is letting the matter go.
what is the difference between "sorry" and "excuse me"?

"Excuse me" is said before you disturb someone, like when you pass in front of them. "Sorry" is said after a mistake. "Excuse me" gets attention; "sorry" says you regret something. In Nepali, "maaf garnus" covers both, so learners often mix them up.
when do we use "the" and when do we leave it out?

Use "the" when both people know which thing you mean: "Close the door." Leave it out when you talk about things in general: "Dogs are loyal." So: "I like the mangoes you brought" but "I like mangoes."
Fill in a or an: ___ MBA student, ___ uniform, ___ X-ray
An MBA student, a uniform, an X-ray. The sound decides, not the letter: "MBA" starts with "em", "uniform" with "yoo" and "X-ray" with "eks".
explain plural of words ending in y
If a consonant comes before "y", change "y" to "ies": city to cities, story to stories, lady to ladies. If a vowel comes before "y", just add "s": key to keys, day to days, monkey to monkeys.
is "two pair of shoes" correct?
Say "two pairs of shoes". "Pair" is the word being counted, so it takes the plural: one pair of socks, three pairs of trousers.
what is the rule for subject and verb agreement in the present tense?
If the subject is he, she, it or one person or thing, the verb takes "s": "She plays", "The bus stops here." With I, you, we and they, the verb has no "s": "They play", "I walk."
Fill in: Look! The baby ___ (sleep) in the cradle.
"Look! The baby is sleeping in the cradle." "Look!" shows it is happening right now, so we use the present continuous: is + verb-ing.
"The boys plays football" - what is wrong?
"The boys" is plural, so the verb has no "s": "The boys play football." Only a single subject takes the "s": "The boy plays football."
which is right: "Everyone are ready" or "Everyone is ready"?
"Everyone is ready." Words like everyone, everybody, someone and nobody take a singular verb, even though they talk about many people.
Fill in with in, on or at: My cousin lives ___ Biratnagar, ___ a small house ___ Main Road.
"My cousin lives in Biratnagar, in a small house on Main Road." Use "in" for a city and for inside a building, "on" for the name of a road, and "at" for an exact address: "at 12 Main Road".
what is the plural of "goose" and "ox"?
"Goose" becomes "geese" and "ox" becomes "oxen". They do not follow the "s" rule. Others like them: man to men, woman to women, foot to feet.
correct: "I have three luggages for the bus"
Say: "I have three bags for the bus" or "three pieces of luggage". "Luggage" cannot be counted, so it has no plural form. "Baggage" works the same way.
which is right - "My friends is coming" or "are coming"?
"My friends are coming." "Friends" is plural, so we use "are". With one person we use "is": "My friend is coming."
when do we use "was" and "were"?
Use "was" with I, he, she and it: "I was tired", "It was cold." Use "were" with you, we and they: "They were late." One special case: "If I were you, I would rest."
correct: "I go to school by the bus"
Say: "I go to school by bus." After "by" for transport we do not use "the": by bus, by car, by plane. With "on" we do: "I go to school on the bus."
difference between "in" and "on" for place?
"In" means inside something: in the room, in the bag. "On" means touching the top or a surface: on the table, on the wall. So the pen is "on" the desk, and the money is "in" the drawer.
Fill in: By the time we reached the bus park, the bus ___ (leave).
"By the time we reached the bus park, the bus had left." The bus left first, before we arrived, so we use the past perfect: had + past participle.
correct: "I didn't do nothing"
Say: "I didn't do anything" or "I did nothing." Standard English uses only one negative word in a sentence, so "didn't" and "nothing" together are wrong.
"I am good in English" or "good at English"?
Say "good at English". We are good "at" a skill or a subject: good at maths, good at singing. But we get marks "in" a subject: "She got good marks in English."
correct: "He works hardly"
Say: "He works hard." "Hard" is already an adverb. "Hardly" means almost not, so "He hardly works" means he does very little work, the opposite meaning.
what preposition goes with "depend"?
"Depend on": "It depends on the weather." "Depend upon" is also correct but more formal. Never "depend of".
correct my sentence please: "Let's go for a walk, isn't it?"
Say: "Let's go for a walk, shall we?" After "let's", the question tag is "shall we". "Isn't it" fits only sentences with "it is", like "It is cold, isn't it?"
is it "listen to music" or "listen music"?
"Listen to music." We always listen "to" something: listen to the radio, listen to your teacher. Without an object you can say just "Listen!"
is "Myself Ramesh" a correct way to introduce myself?
It is common in South Asia, but it is not correct English. Say "I am Ramesh" or "My name is Ramesh." Use "myself" after a verb, as in "I cooked it myself."
correct: "She is angry on me"
Say: "She is angry with me." We are angry "with" a person and angry "about" a thing: "He is angry about the delay."
what is the present perfect continuous?
It shows an action that started in the past and is still going on: "I have been waiting for an hour." Form: have or has been + verb-ing. It often answers "How long?"
correct: "My all friends came to the party"
Say: "All my friends came to the party." "All" comes before words like my, our and the: all my books, all the students.
which is correct - "different from" or "different than"?
"Different from" is accepted everywhere: "My answer is different from yours." "Different than" is common in American speech, but "different from" is the safe choice in school.
what is wrong in "She is senior than me"?
Say: "She is senior to me." Senior, junior, superior and inferior go with "to", not "than": "He is junior to me at work."
is it correct to say "I am fine, what about you?"
Yes, it is correct and friendly. You can also say "I'm fine, thanks. And you?" or "Good, thanks. How about you?"
make a question asking "where" from: "Sabina works in a bank."
"Where does Sabina work?" Use "does" because Sabina is one person, and "works" goes back to "work" after "does".
how do I make "She can drive" negative?
"She cannot drive" or "She can't drive." With can, will, must and should, just add "not" after them: "He should not go", "We will not stay."
what is the future perfect tense? simple example please
It shows that something will be finished before a time in the future: "By 6 pm, I will have finished my work." Form: will have + past participle, as in will have eaten, will have gone.
correct: "What means this word?"
Say: "What does this word mean?" In questions with most verbs we need "do" or "does": "What does it mean?", "Where does she live?"
difference between "sometimes" and "sometime"?
"Sometimes" means now and then: "I sometimes walk to work." "Sometime" means at a time that is not fixed: "Let's meet sometime next week."
Fill in: She ___ (cook) dinner when the lights went out.
"She was cooking dinner when the lights went out." The cooking was already going on when the power cut happened, so we use "was cooking".
"beside" or "besides"?
"Beside" means next to: "Sit beside me." "Besides" means also or apart from: "Besides English, she speaks Hindi and Maithili."
what is the difference between "wake up" and "get up"?
"Wake up" means to stop sleeping. "Get up" means to get out of bed. You can wake up at 6 and still get up at 6:30. In Nepali, "biujhanu" is to wake up and "uthnu" is to get up.
Fill in: Every evening my grandmother ___ (tell) us a story.
"Every evening my grandmother tells us a story." "Every evening" shows a habit, and "grandmother" is one person, so the verb takes "s".
"remember" or "remind"?

You remember something yourself: "I remember her name." You remind another person: "Please remind me to call Aama." "Remind" always needs a person after it. In Nepali: remember is "samjhanu", remind is "samjhaunu".
is "staffs" correct?
Usually no. "Staff" means all the workers of a place as a group: "The hospital staff are kind." For one person, say "a staff member" or "one of the staff".
what's the difference between "cloth" and "clothes"?

"Cloth" is the material, like cotton cloth for a kurta. "Clothes" are the things you wear: shirts, trousers, saris. "Clothes" is always plural: "My clothes are wet." In Nepali, cloth is "kapada" and clothes are "luga".
Is "pass out" the same as "graduate"?
Not in standard English. "Pass out" usually means to faint. For finishing a course, say "graduate": "She graduated from college last year."
fill in the article: "She plays ___ madal and ___ flute."
"She plays the madal and the flute." We use "the" with musical instruments: play the guitar, play the sarangi. But there is no article with sports: play football.
my friend wrote "My father is a good cooker". right?
Not quite. A cooker is a machine, like a pressure cooker. A person who cooks is a "cook": "My father is a good cook."
what is the plural of "mother-in-law"?
"Mothers-in-law". In these words the main word takes the "s": sons-in-law, brothers-in-law, passers-by.
"economic" vs "economical" - which one for a bike that saves petrol?
"Economical." It means saving money or using little: "This bike is economical." "Economic" is about money and trade in a country: "economic growth".
when do we say "eldest" and when "oldest"?
"Eldest" is used only for people in a family: "my eldest brother". "Oldest" works for anything, family included: "the oldest tree in the village", "my oldest sister".
difference between "costume" and "custom"?
A costume is special clothing for a show or a festival, like a dance costume. A custom is a tradition: "Making sel roti in Tihar is a custom in many homes."
difference between "wait" and "expect"?

To wait is to stay until something happens: "I waited for the bus." To expect is to think something will happen: "I expect the bus at 9." You can expect rain without waiting for it. In Nepali, wait is "parkhanu" and expect is "aasha garnu".
when do we use "been" and when "gone"?
"Gone" means the person is still away: "She has gone to Pokhara" (she is there now). "Been" means went and came back: "She has been to Pokhara" (she is back now).
what is the past tense of "study"?
"Studied". When a verb ends in a consonant plus "y", change "y" to "i" and add "ed": study to studied, carry to carried, try to tried.
past tense of "stop" - stopped or stoped?
"Stopped", with two p's. A short verb ending in one vowel and one consonant doubles the last letter: stop to stopped, plan to planned, shop to shopped.
when do we add "es" instead of "s" for plurals?
Add "es" after words ending in s, sh, ch, x or z: bus to buses, dish to dishes, watch to watches, fox to foxes. Many words ending in o also take "es": tomato to tomatoes, hero to heroes.
is "I am going to the market for buy rice" correct?
No. Say: "I am going to the market to buy rice." To show purpose, use "to" + verb. "For" goes with a noun: "I am going to the market for rice."
what does "ripe" mean?
"Ripe" means fully grown and ready to eat, used for fruit and grain: "These mangoes are ripe and sweet." The opposite is "unripe" or "raw". In Nepali: "pakeko".
meaning of "stale"?
"Stale" means no longer fresh, used for food like bread, biscuits or chiura that has become old and dry: "The bread is stale, so don't eat it." Nepali speakers often say "basi" for this.
give me the opposite of "shallow"
The opposite of "shallow" is "deep". Example: "The river is shallow near the bank but deep in the middle."
what is another word for "crowded"?
You can say "packed" or "full of people": "The bus was packed this morning." "Jam-packed" is even stronger and is used in speech.
use "afford" in a sentence
"We cannot afford a new car this year, so we will repair the old one." "Afford" means to have enough money for something, and it often comes with "can" or "cannot".
synonym of "buy" for a formal letter?
Use "purchase": "I purchased this phone from your shop on Sunday." In everyday talk, "buy" is simpler and better.
what does "chores" mean?
Chores are small jobs you do regularly at home, like washing dishes, sweeping and feeding the animals. Example: "I finish my chores before I play." In Nepali: "ghar ko kaam".
what is an "errand"?
An errand is a short trip to do a small job, like buying milk or paying a bill. "I have to run some errands" means "I have to go out and do a few small jobs."
how do I pronounce "vegetable"?
Say it in three parts: VEJ-tuh-bul. The second "e" is not pronounced, and the stress is on the first part.
what does "a blessing in disguise" mean?
It means something that looked bad at first but turned out to be good. Example: "Missing the bus was a blessing in disguise; I met an old friend while I waited."
what does "leftovers" mean
Leftovers are food left after a meal and kept to eat later: "We had last night's leftovers for lunch."
what does "steep" mean? for a road
A steep road goes up or down sharply, so it is hard to climb: "The road to the village is very steep." In Nepali we say "thado ukalo". A road that rises slowly has a gentle slope.
I mix up v and w when I speak. any tip?

For "v", touch your top teeth to your lower lip and push air: very, van. For "w", round your lips like a small "o" and keep your teeth away: well, water. Practise pairs slowly: vest and west, vine and wine.
make a sentence with "as soon as"
"I will call you as soon as I reach Butwal." "As soon as" means right after something happens. Use the present tense after it, even when you talk about the future.
meaning of "on the same page"?
"On the same page" means two people understand and agree about a plan. Example: "Before the meeting, let's make sure we are on the same page."
what does "drowsy" mean
"Drowsy" means sleepy and slow, often after a big meal or a long bus ride: "I felt drowsy after lunch." In Nepali: "nindra lagne" or "lol lagne".
opposite of "tidy"
"Untidy" or "messy". Example: "His desk is tidy, but his bag is messy."
how do you say "Wednesday"?
Say WENZ-day. The first "d" and the second "e" are silent, so the word has only two parts.
what is the meaning of "relieved"?
"Relieved" means you feel better because a worry is over: "I was relieved when my brother called from the airport." In Nepali: "man halka bhayo".
what does "learn by heart" mean?
It means to learn something so well that you can say it without looking: "We learned the poem by heart." In Nepali: "kantha garnu".
give me a sentence using "whereas"
"My sister loves sweet tea, whereas I like it without sugar." "Whereas" shows a contrast between two facts.
"read" in the past - how to pronounce?
The past of "read" is spelled the same but sounds like "red": "Yesterday I read a book." In the present it sounds like "reed": "I read every night."
what does "get the hang of it" mean
It means to slowly learn how to do something well: "Driving was hard at first, but I got the hang of it in a week."
what is the opposite of "guilty"?
"Innocent". Example: "The court said he was innocent." "Guilty" means you did something wrong. In Nepali: guilty is "dosi" and innocent is "nirdosh".
what does "fond of" mean
"Fond of" means liking someone or something a lot: "My grandfather is fond of old songs." After "of", use a noun or an -ing verb: "She is fond of cooking."
how to say "comfortable"
Most people say KUMF-ter-bul, in three parts. The stress is on the first part, and the middle sound is very short.
"Better late than never" meaning?
It means it is better to do something late than not to do it at all. Example: "He started saving at forty. Better late than never!"
another word for "fix"
"Repair" or "mend". "Repair" is used for machines: repair a bike. "Mend" is often for clothes or small things: mend a torn shirt.
why do we say "record" in two different ways?
The stress shows the job of the word. As a noun, stress the first part: a REcord. As a verb, stress the second part: to reCORD a song. "Present" works the same: a PREsent, to preSENT.
what is "in the same boat"?
"In the same boat" means in the same difficult situation as someone else: "Don't worry about the hard exam; the whole class is in the same boat."
what does "keep an eye on" mean
It means to watch something carefully: "Please keep an eye on the milk so it does not boil over."
how do you pronounce "island"?
Say EYE-land. The "s" is silent. The same silent "s" is in "aisle".
what does "out of the blue" mean
It means suddenly, with no warning: "My school friend called me out of the blue after ten years." In Nepali: "achanak".
what does "make ends meet" mean?
It means to have just enough money for basic needs: "When prices go up, many families find it hard to make ends meet."
someone told me "Help yourself". what does it mean?
It means "Please take what you want; you don't need to ask." Hosts say it when food is on the table: "The momo is ready, help yourself!"
what does "long time no see" mean?
It is a friendly, informal greeting for someone you have not met for a long time. You can reply: "Yes, it's been ages! How are you?"
my boss replied "Noted" to my email. is that rude?
No, it is not rude. "Noted" means "I have read this and I understand." It is short and common in office emails.
what does "Kindly do the needful" mean?
It means "Please do what is necessary." It is common in South Asian offices but sounds old-fashioned elsewhere. It is clearer to say exactly what you need: "Please send the form by Friday."
is "prepone" a real English word?
It is used in India and Nepal, but it is not standard English everywhere. Say "bring forward" or "move earlier": "The meeting has been brought forward to 10 am."
what do I say at the bank to open a savings account?
"Good morning. I would like to open a savings account. Could you tell me which documents I need?" They will give you a form and usually ask for an ID card and photos.
"Mina gave her old bicycle to her cousin Rabin and bought a new one for 9500 rupees. Rabin painted the old bicycle blue." Who got the old bicycle?
Rabin got the old bicycle.
messages.think: The text says "Mina gave her old bicycle to her cousin Rabin": Mina gave, Rabin got.

messages.content: "Mina gave her old bicycle to her cousin Rabin and bought a new one for 9500 rupees. Rabin painted the old bicycle blue." Who gave the bicycle away?
Mina gave the bicycle away.
messages.think: The text says "Mina gave her old bicycle to her cousin Rabin": the giver is Mina.

messages.content: "Mina gave her old bicycle to her cousin Rabin and bought a new one for 9500 rupees. Rabin painted the old bicycle blue." How much did the new bicycle cost?
The new bicycle cost 9500 rupees.
messages.think: The text says "bought a new one for 9500 rupees". This is a lookup, so no calculation is needed.

messages.content: "Mina gave her old bicycle to her cousin Rabin and bought a new one for 9500 rupees. Rabin painted the old bicycle blue." What colour is the new bicycle?
The text does not say what colour the new bicycle is. It only says that Rabin painted the old bicycle blue.
messages.think: The text says only that Rabin painted the old bicycle blue. It gives no colour for the new one.

messages.content: A tailor stitches 4 kurtas a day and works 6 days a week. How many kurtas does she stitch in 2 weeks?
She stitches 48 kurtas in 2 weeks.
I saw the word "chautari" on a trekking map. What is it?

A chautari is a raised stone platform, usually built around one or two big trees beside a trail, where travellers rest in the shade. There is no single English word for it; "resting platform" is close.
the ATM kept my card. how do I explain this to the bank staff?
"Excuse me, the ATM outside did not give my card back. Could you please help me get it?" Carry your ID, because the bank needs to check that the card is yours.
A school trip costs 850 rupees per student and 38 students are going. What is the total cost?
The total cost is 32300 rupees.
what does OPD mean at a hospital?

OPD means Outpatient Department. It is where you see a doctor and go home the same day, without staying in a hospital bed. You usually get an OPD ticket at the counter first and then wait for your turn.
Explain the Nepali word "parma" in English.
"Parma" is a way of sharing farm work: you help a neighbour plant or harvest, and later they help on your field for the same number of days. No money is paid. In English it is called labour exchange.
A shop packs eggs in trays of 30. How many full trays can it fill with 400 eggs, and how many eggs are left over?
It can fill 13 full trays, with 10 eggs left over.
messages.think: 30 x 13 = 390. 400 - 390 = 10. One more tray would need 30 x 14 = 420, which is more than 400.

messages.content: the nurse said my father will be discharged tomorrow. what does that mean?

It means the hospital will let him go home tomorrow because he no longer needs to stay. The doctor usually gives a discharge paper with advice and a date for the next check-up. Ask the nurse about anything that is unclear.
"Notice: The Ward 4 health camp will be held on Saturday from 10 am to 3 pm at the school ground. Free eye check-ups for people over 50." Where will the camp be held?
The camp will be held at the school ground.
messages.think: The notice says "at the school ground".

messages.content: "Notice: The Ward 4 health camp will be held on Saturday from 10 am to 3 pm at the school ground. Free eye check-ups for people over 50." For how many hours will the camp run?
The camp will run for 5 hours.
messages.think: The camp runs "from 10 am to 3 pm". 10 am to 12 noon is 2 hours, and 12 noon to 3 pm is 3 hours. 2 + 3 = 5.

messages.content: "Notice: The Ward 4 health camp will be held on Saturday from 10 am to 3 pm at the school ground. Free eye check-ups for people over 50." Who can get a free eye check-up?
People over 50 can get a free eye check-up.
messages.think: The notice says "Free eye check-ups for people over 50."

messages.content: "Notice: The Ward 4 health camp will be held on Saturday from 10 am to 3 pm at the school ground. Free eye check-ups for people over 50." So the camp is on Sunday, right?
No. The camp is on Saturday, not Sunday.
messages.think: The notice says the camp "will be held on Saturday".

messages.content: what is a "doko"?
A doko is a big basket woven from bamboo and carried on the back with a strap, called a "namlo", across the forehead. People carry grass, firewood and vegetables in it.
how do I ask the bus conductor to tell me when my stop comes?
"Excuse me, could you tell me when we reach (name of your stop)? I need to get off there." Sit near the door if you can, and remind him a little before the stop.
My data pack gives 1.5 GB a day. How much data is that in a 28-day pack?
That is 42 GB in 28 days.
how do I explain "jutho" to a foreign friend?
You can say: "Jutho is food or a drink that has already touched someone's mouth or plate. In many Nepali homes, people do not share it." There is no exact English word for it.
how do I ask for a window seat when buying a bus ticket?
"One ticket, please. Is there a window seat available?" If there is none: "Then a seat near the front, please."
A 20-liter jar of water costs 45 rupees. We use 3 jars a week. How much do we pay in 4 weeks?
You pay 540 rupees in 4 weeks.
the phone line keeps breaking. what should I say in English?
"Sorry, the line is not clear. Could you say that again?" If it is very bad: "I can't hear you well. Let me call you back in a minute."
What does "bhanjyang" mean?
"Bhanjyang" means a mountain pass: the low point on a ridge where a trail crosses to the other side. You see the word in many village and trail names in the hills.
"Asha: Did you finish the report? Kiran: Not yet. I finished the charts, but the summary is still left." What has Kiran finished?
Kiran has finished the charts.
"Asha: Did you finish the report? Kiran: Not yet. I finished the charts, but the summary is still left." What is still left?
The summary is still left.
messages.think: Kiran says "the summary is still left".

messages.content: "Asha: Did you finish the report? Kiran: Not yet. I finished the charts, but the summary is still left." Who asked about the report?
Asha asked about the report.
messages.think: The first line is "Asha: Did you finish the report?"

messages.content: A recipe uses 250 g of flour for 10 sel roti. How much flour is needed for 30?
You need 750 g of flour for 30 sel roti.
how do I leave a voicemail in English?
Say your name, the reason and your number slowly: "Hello, this is (your name). I am calling about (the reason). Please call me back on (your number). Thank you."
what is a "khutruke" in english?
A khutruke is a small clay or tin box with a narrow slot for saving coins. In English it is called a money box or a piggy bank. You break it or open it when it is full.
how should I answer "Where do you see yourself in five years?" in an interview?

Show that you want to grow in this kind of work: "In five years, I hope to have stronger skills in this field and to take on bigger responsibilities here." Keep it honest and realistic, not too grand.
A farmer has three plots of 1200, 950 and 1350 square meters. What is the total area?
The total area is 3500 square meters.
what does "tole" mean?
A "tole" is a neighbourhood: a small part of a town where a group of houses stand close together. A "tole sudhar samiti" is a neighbourhood committee.
what if I don't know the answer to a question in an interview?
Stay calm and be honest: "I am not sure about that, but I would find out quickly." If you know something close, say that. An honest answer leaves a better feeling than a confident guess.
A bike loan needs 8500 rupees a month for 24 months. How much is paid in total?
The total paid is 204000 rupees.
What does "lahure" mean?

A "lahure" is a Nepali who serves in a foreign army, such as the British or Indian army. Some people also use it loosely for anyone working abroad. The word is said to come from Lahore, where Nepali soldiers once went to serve.
what do CC and BCC mean in an email?
CC means "carbon copy": the people in CC get a copy so they know about the email, but it is mainly for the person in "To". BCC means "blind carbon copy": the others cannot see who is in BCC.
A van carries 12 passengers and travels at 60 km per hour. It makes 3 full trips. How many passengers does it carry?
The van carries 36 passengers in 3 trips.
messages.think: The speed is not needed. 12 x 3 = 36.

messages.content: what is "dhindo"?
Dhindo is a thick porridge made by stirring millet, maize or buckwheat flour into boiling water. It is eaten with gundruk, vegetable curry or meat, especially in the hills.
how do I politely follow up when someone has not replied to my email?
Write: "Dear Sir, I am writing to follow up on my earlier email about (the topic). Could you please let me know when you have a moment? Thank you." Wait a few working days before you send it.
I bought 4 shirts and paid with a 5000 rupee note. How much change should I get?
I need the price of the shirts to work this out. How much did one shirt cost, or what was the total? Then I can find your change.
how do I ask the shopkeeper for a bigger size?
"Excuse me, do you have this in a bigger size?" or "Do you have it in large?" To try it: "Can I try it on? Where is the trial room?" In many countries it is called the "fitting room".
what does "udharo" mean?
"Udharo" means taking something now and paying for it later. Example: "The shopkeeper gave me rice on udharo." In English we say "on credit".
I get 1200 rupees pocket money and spend 35% on books. How much is left?
You have 780 rupees left.
how to ask if I can pay with a QR code?
"Can I pay by QR code?" or "Do you take mobile payments?" After paying, show the screen and say: "I have paid. Here is the confirmation."
what does "nanglo" mean?
A nanglo is a flat round tray woven from bamboo. It is used to clean grain by tossing it so the husk blows away, and to dry things in the sun. In English it is a winnowing tray.
Classes start at 10:15. There are three periods of 45 minutes, with a 15-minute break after the second period. When do classes end?
Classes end at 12:45.
messages.think: 45 + 45 + 15 + 45 = 150 minutes, which is 2 hours 30 minutes. 10:15 plus 2 hours 30 minutes is 12:45.

messages.content: how to tell the waiter I want the food less spicy?
"Could you make it less spicy, please?" or "Not too spicy, please." If you want none at all: "No chilli, please." In Nepali eateries people say "kam piro".
I just planted tomatoes in pots on my roof!

That's a great start! Tomatoes love sun, so keep the pots where they get at least six hours of light, and water them when the top soil feels dry. Each plant will need a small stick for support as it grows.
my cat had four kittens last night

Congratulations, four kittens! Give the mother a quiet, warm corner with a soft cloth, and keep food and water close to her. Try not to handle the kittens much in the first couple of weeks; the mother will look after them.
I failed my driving test today. I feel so stupid.
You are not stupid; many people pass on their second or third try. Ask your trainer which part went wrong, practise that part a little every day, and book the test again when you feel ready.
I won the school quiz competition!
Well done! That takes a lot of reading and quick thinking. Which question was the hardest one?
My grandmother is coming to stay with us for a month.
How nice! A month is a good chance to hear her stories and learn a dish or two from her. Ask her about her childhood; grandparents usually love to talk about it.
I'm learning to play the madal but my hands hurt.
That is normal in the first weeks. Play for shorter times, like fifteen minutes, and rest your hands in between. Strike with relaxed fingers, not with force. Your hands will get used to it.
The power has gone off again in our area. So boring.
Power cuts are annoying! It could be a good time to read, chat with your family or go for a short walk. Keep a torch and a charged power bank ready for the next time.
I got a scholarship for my bachelor's degree!
Congratulations! That is a big achievement, and it will make your studies much easier. You earned it. Which subject are you going to study?
We are moving to Biratnagar next month. I don't know anyone there.
Moving is hard at first. Once you are there, greet your neighbours, find a nearby shop you visit often, and join one group, like a sports club or a class. Familiar faces come quickly that way.
The bus was so crowded today that I stood for two hours.
That sounds tiring! Standing that long is hard on the legs. If you take the same bus often, leaving a little earlier may help you find a seat. Rest well tonight.
I finished my first English novel!
Wonderful! Finishing a whole novel in a new language is a real step forward. What was it about, and are you going to read another one?
My best friend's wedding is next week and I have to give a short speech. Help!

Keep it to about two minutes. Say how you met your friend, share one happy memory, say something kind about the couple, and end with a wish: "I wish you both a lifetime of love and laughter." Practise it aloud a few times.
my son took his first steps today!!
What a special moment! Congratulations. From now on he will want to walk everywhere, so keep the floor clear and move sharp or heavy things out of his reach.
I burnt the rice again lol
It happens to everyone! Next time, lower the heat once the water starts boiling and set an alarm on your phone. If only the bottom is burnt, the top part is usually still fine to eat.
I feel shy speaking English in front of my classmates.

Many learners feel this way, even good ones. Start with short sentences you are sure of, like "Can I ask a question?" Practise alone first, then with one friend. Mistakes are part of learning, and others notice them much less than you think.
can you talk to me in English so I can practise?
Of course! Let's start simple. Tell me about your day: what did you do this morning?
My little sister asks "why" about everything all day.
That means she is curious and learning fast. When you can, answer simply, or ask her back: "Why do you think?" When you are busy, say kindly, "Ask me again after dinner."
It's my first salary today and I want to buy something for my parents.
That's a lovely thought. Think about what they use every day: a warm shawl, a good pair of sandals, or something for the house. Giving it with your own hands will mean the most to them.
I'm flying for the first time next week and I'm a bit scared.

That's normal. Reach the airport early, keep your ID and ticket handy, and listen to the safety talk. Small bumps in the air are normal and safe. If you feel nervous, breathe slowly and look out of the window.
My English teacher said my speaking has improved a lot!
That's great news! Your practice is paying off. Keep it going: speak a little English every day, even if it is just to describe what you are doing.
Write a short message inviting my classmates to a study group on Friday at 4 pm in the library.
"Hi everyone! Let's study together this Friday at 4 pm in the library. Bring your notes and your questions. See you there!"
Help me text my tuition teacher that I will be 10 minutes late today.
"Good afternoon, sir. I am sorry, I will be about 10 minutes late today. I will come as soon as I can." Use "madam" if your teacher is a woman.
Write an English caption for a photo of me and my mother.
Here are three to choose from: "My first home, my best friend." / "With the woman who taught me everything." / "Aama and me, always."
Write a message to the school saying my son was absent yesterday because he had a fever.
"Dear Sir/Madam, my son could not come to school yesterday because he had a fever. Please excuse his absence, and kindly let us know if he missed any homework. Thank you."
A customer asked if my shop is open on Saturday. We open 10 to 5. Help me reply.
"Yes, we are open on Saturday from 10 am to 5 pm. You are welcome to visit!"
Make this message polite: "Send me the money now."
"Could you please send the money as soon as possible? Thank you." Adding "please" and a question form makes a request sound polite.
Make this sound more professional: "I can't come tomorrow, sorry."
"I am sorry, but I will not be able to come tomorrow. Please let me know if I should finish anything before then."
Write a two-line bio for my profile. I am a nurse in Dharan and I love hiking.
"Nurse in Dharan. Happiest on a hill trail on my days off." Or shorter: "Nurse | Dharan | Hiker."
Write a note to my son's class teacher asking for a short meeting.
"Dear Sir/Madam, I would like to meet you for a few minutes to talk about my son's studies. Please let me know a day and time that suits you. Thank you."
How do I reply in English to "Are you free this evening?" if I'm busy?
"Sorry, I'm busy this evening. How about tomorrow?" or "I wish I could, but I already have plans. Maybe another day?"
what does this mean: "The early bird catches the worm."?
It means people who start early get the best chances. Example: "Go to the vegetable market at seven; the early bird catches the worm, and everything is freshest then."
A notice says "Office closed due to unavoidable circumstances." What does it mean?
It means the office is closed because of something they could not control or avoid. The notice does not give the exact reason. Call or come back another day to check when it will open.
what does "subject to availability" mean?
It means you will get it only if some is still available. "Free dessert, subject to availability" means you get the dessert only if there is some left.
My bank SMS says "Your a/c has been debited by Rs 500". What does debited mean?

"Debited" means money has been taken out of your account, and "a/c" means account. So 500 rupees has gone out. "Credited" is the opposite: money has come in. If you did not make this payment, call your bank.
what does "terms and conditions apply" mean in an advertisement?
It means the offer has rules written somewhere else, often in small print. Read them before you buy, because the offer may be only for some items, some days or some customers.
The website says "out of stock". what does that mean?
It means the shop has none of that item left right now. They may get more later. "In stock" means it is available.
what is a "toll-free" number?
A toll-free number is a phone number you can call without paying for the call; the company pays instead. Many banks and service companies have one for customer help.
A sign on the door says "Wet paint". What should I do?
It means the paint is fresh and not dry yet. Do not touch the door or lean on it, or the paint will come off on your hands and clothes. In Nepali: "rang sukeko chhaina".
Fill in the articles: "___ sun rises in ___ east."
"The sun rises in the east." We use "the" for things there is only one of, like the sun, the moon and the sky, and for directions: the east, the north.
should it be "I had a breakfast" or "I had breakfast"?
"I had breakfast." We usually use no article with meals: have breakfast, eat lunch, cook dinner. Use "a" only when an adjective comes in: "We had a big breakfast."
Fill in: "It was ___ honour to meet you."
"It was an honour to meet you." The "h" in "honour" is silent, so the word starts with a vowel sound and takes "an".
what is the difference between "go to school" and "go to the school"?

"Go to school" means going there to study: "I go to school every day." "Go to the school" means going to the building for another reason: "My mother went to the school to meet my teacher." "Hospital" works the same way in British English.
why is it "photos" but "heroes"?

Many words ending in "o" take "es" (heroes, potatoes, echoes), but short or borrowed words often take only "s": photos, radios, pianos, kilos. There is no single rule, so these are learned one by one.
is "peoples" a word?
Usually we say "people", which is already plural: "Many people came." "Peoples" is used only for different nations or groups: "the peoples of South Asia." In daily English, use "people".
scissors is or are?
"Are": "The scissors are on the table." Scissors, trousers, glasses and jeans are always plural. To count them, use "a pair of": "A pair of scissors is on the table."
"He is six foot tall" or "six feet tall"?
"He is six feet tall" is the standard form. But before a noun, use the singular with a hyphen: "a six-foot man", just like "a ten-year-old girl" and "a five-kilometre walk".
Fill in: "I ___ (not eat) anything since morning."
"I haven't eaten anything since morning." The time runs from the past up to now, so we use the present perfect: have not + eaten.
Fill in: "If you heat ice, it ___ (melt)."
"If you heat ice, it melts." This is a general truth, so both parts use the present simple. It is called the zero conditional.
Fill in: "The new bridge ___ (open) next month."
"The new bridge will be opened next month." Someone will open it, so we use the future passive: will be + past participle. In everyday speech, "The new bridge will open next month" is also fine.
What tense is "They had been working all night"?
It is the past perfect continuous. It shows an action that went on for some time before another past moment: "They had been working all night when the power came back."
"One of my friends live in Japan" - right?
Say "One of my friends lives in Japan." The subject is "one", so the verb takes "s". "My friends" is only part of the phrase.
"The number of students" is or are?
"The number of students is growing", because the number is one thing. But "A number of students are absent", because it means many students. "The number" takes "is"; "a number" takes "are".
is it "Ten kilometres is a long walk" or "are"?
"Ten kilometres is a long walk." When a distance, an amount of money or a time is one whole, the verb is singular: "Five hundred rupees is enough."
"The police is coming" or "are coming"?
"The police are coming." "Police" is always plural in English. For one person, say "a police officer".
"Bread and butter ___ my breakfast" - is or are?
"Bread and butter is my breakfast." Here bread and butter is one dish, so the verb is singular. Two separate things take "are": "Rice and dal are cheap here."
"Ram, along with his friends, are going" - correct?
Say "Ram, along with his friends, is going." The subject is Ram; "along with his friends" is extra information, so the verb stays singular. Compare: "Ram and his friends are going."
"arrive in" or "arrive at"?
Use "arrive in" for a city or a country: "We arrived in Nepalgunj at noon." Use "arrive at" for a building or a smaller place: "We arrived at the bus park." Never "arrive to".
Fill in the prepositions: afraid ___ dogs, proud ___ my son, worried ___ the exam
Afraid of dogs, proud of my son, worried about the exam.
"on time" or "in time"?
"On time" means at the planned time, not late: "The bus left on time." "In time" means early enough for something: "We reached in time to see the start of the play."
what is the difference between "at the end" and "in the end"?
"At the end" means at the last part of something: "at the end of the road", "at the end of the film". "In the end" means finally, after everything: "In the end, we decided to stay home."
"by Monday" or "until Monday"?
"By Monday" means not later than Monday: "Submit the form by Monday." "Until Monday" means the whole time up to Monday: "The shop is closed until Monday."
correct: "I congratulate you for your success"
Say: "I congratulate you on your success." We congratulate someone "on" something: "Congratulations on your new job!"
correct: "He is suffering by fever"
Say: "He is suffering from a fever" or simply "He has a fever." We suffer "from" an illness.
correct: "I am interested to join the club"
Say: "I am interested in joining the club." "Interested" goes with "in", and after a preposition the verb takes the -ing form.
is "The house comprises of five rooms" right?
Say "The house comprises five rooms" or "The house consists of five rooms." "Comprise" does not take "of", but "consist" does.
correct: "Please repeat it again"
Say: "Please repeat it." "Repeat" already means "say again", so "again" is extra. In the same way, "return back" should be just "return".
correct: "I like very much tea"
Say: "I like tea very much." In English, "very much" comes after the object, not between the verb and the object.
correct: "Always I go to bed at ten"
Say: "I always go to bed at ten." Words like always, usually, often and never come before the main verb, but after am, is and are: "She is always late."
correct: "Although it was raining, but we went out"

Say: "Although it was raining, we went out" or "It was raining, but we went out." Use "although" or "but", not both. Nepali often uses "yadyapi ... tara" together, which is why this mistake is common.
correct: "Thank you for help me"
Say: "Thank you for helping me" or "Thank you for your help." After "for", use a noun or the -ing form of a verb.
correct: "Let me to go"
Say: "Let me go." After "let" and "make", the verb comes without "to": "Let her speak", "They made us wait."
"between you and I" or "between you and me"?
"Between you and me." After words like between, with and for, use the object form: me, him, her, us, them.
Fill in: "My bag is ___ (heavy) than yours."
"My bag is heavier than yours." For short adjectives ending in a consonant + y, change "y" to "i" and add "er": heavy to heavier, easy to easier, happy to happier.
what is the superlative of "famous"?
"Most famous": "the most famous singer in our town". Long adjectives use "more" and "most" instead of "-er" and "-est": more careful, most beautiful.
what is the difference between "mustn't" and "don't have to"?
"Mustn't" means it is not allowed: "You mustn't park here." "Don't have to" means it is not necessary, though you can if you want: "You don't have to come early tomorrow."
is "I want a glass of water" rude?
It is not wrong, but it can sound too direct. "I would like a glass of water, please" or "Could I have a glass of water?" sounds more polite, especially in shops and offices.
complete: "The more you practise, ___"
"The more you practise, the better you get." This pattern shows two things growing together: "The sooner we leave, the earlier we will reach."
Fill in the question tag: "She is coming with us, ___?"
"She is coming with us, isn't she?" A positive sentence takes a negative tag with the same helping verb: is becomes isn't, can becomes can't.
Spelling check: "seperate" or "separate"?
"Separate" is right. A trick to remember it: there is "a rat" in sep-A-RAT-e.
is it "definately" or "definitely"?
"Definitely" is correct. It comes from "finite", so think of def-INITE-ly.
how to spell "occasion"? I always mix up the c and the s.
"Occasion" has two c's and one s. Two more that people often get wrong: "necessary" has one c and two s's, and "embarrass" has two r's and two s's.
what's the opposite of "spacious"?
"Cramped". A spacious room has plenty of space; a cramped room is too small for the people or things in it: "With six of us inside, the small room felt cramped."
"Didi, the tailor called. Your blouse will be ready on Thursday, not Tuesday. He needs 200 rupees more for the extra lining. - Nisha" When will the blouse be ready?
The blouse will be ready on Thursday.
messages.think: The message says "Your blouse will be ready on Thursday, not Tuesday."
