The tailor called.
"Didi, the tailor called. Your blouse will be ready on Thursday, not Tuesday. He needs 200 rupees more for the extra lining. - Nisha" Who wrote this message?
Nisha wrote the message.
messages.think: The message ends with "- Nisha", so Nisha wrote it.

messages.content: "Didi, the tailor called. Your blouse will be ready on Thursday, not Tuesday. He needs 200 rupees more for the extra lining. - Nisha" How much more money does the tailor want?
The tailor needs 200 rupees more, for the extra lining.
messages.think: The message says "He needs 200 rupees more for the extra lining." This is a lookup.

messages.content: what does "fragrant" mean?
"Fragrant" means having a sweet, pleasant smell: "fragrant jasmine flowers". In Nepali: "sugandhit" or "baasna aaune".
A printer prints 18 pages a minute. How long will it take to print 270 pages?
It will take 15 minutes.
why does "ch" sound different in "school" and "machine"?
In "school", "ch" sounds like "k": skool. In "machine", it sounds like "sh": ma-SHEEN. In most words, like "chair" and "lunch", it has the usual "ch" sound.
what does "hit the nail on the head" mean?
It means to say exactly the right thing about a problem. Example: "When she said we need more practice, not more books, she hit the nail on the head."
What do I say when I check in at a hotel?
"Hello, I have a booking under the name (your name)." They will ask for an ID. Useful questions after that: "What time is breakfast?" and "What time is check-out?"
is "spicy" the same as "hot"?

Not always. "Spicy" means full of chilli or spices. "Hot" can mean spicy, but it also means high in temperature. To be clear, say "very spicy" for chilli and "very hot" for tea that burns your tongue.
"Lunch menu: veg thali 250, chicken thali 380, plain rice 80, extra dal 40 (all prices in rupees)." How much is a chicken thali?
A chicken thali costs 380 rupees.
messages.think: The menu says "chicken thali 380". This is a lookup, so no calculation is needed.

messages.content: "Lunch menu: veg thali 250, chicken thali 380, plain rice 80, extra dal 40 (all prices in rupees)." How much do two veg thalis cost?
Two veg thalis cost 500 rupees.
"Lunch menu: veg thali 250, chicken thali 380, plain rice 80, extra dal 40 (all prices in rupees)." Which costs less, plain rice or extra dal?
Extra dal costs less: 40 rupees, against 80 for plain rice.
messages.think: Plain rice is 80 and extra dal is 40. 40 is less than 80.

messages.content: "Lunch menu: veg thali 250, chicken thali 380, plain rice 80, extra dal 40 (all prices in rupees)." How much is a fish thali?
The menu does not have a fish thali, so it gives no price for it. It only lists veg thali, chicken thali, plain rice and extra dal.
messages.think: The menu lists veg thali, chicken thali, plain rice and extra dal. There is no fish thali.

messages.content: meaning of "bland"
"Bland" means having very little taste: "The soup was bland, so I added salt and pepper." In Nepali we would say "khallo".
what does "the last straw" mean?
It means the final small problem that makes you lose your patience after many others. Example: "He was late every day, and missing the meeting was the last straw."
A family uses 2 gas cylinders every 3 months. How many cylinders do they use in a year?
They use 8 gas cylinders in a year.
messages.think: A year has 12 months. 12 / 3 = 4 periods of 3 months. 4 x 2 = 8.

messages.content: how do I ask for the bill in a restaurant?
"Could we have the bill, please?" In American English people say "the check". You can also catch the waiter's eye and raise your hand a little.
what does "crisp" mean for food?
"Crisp" means firm and dry, so it makes a sound when you bite it: crisp biscuits, a crisp apple, crisp fried potatoes. The opposite is "soggy", which means wet and soft.
how do I say words with "ough"? they confuse me
"Ough" has many sounds: though (oh), through (oo), tough (uff), cough (off), bought (aw). There is no single rule, so learn each word by ear.
what does "don't cry over spilt milk" mean?
It means do not waste time feeling sad about something that has already happened and cannot be changed. Example: "You missed the bus, but don't cry over spilt milk; take the next one."

"Rajesh's grandfather is 4 years older than his grandmother. His grandmother is 68. Every morning the grandfather walks to the dairy for milk, while the grandmother stays home and makes tea." How old is the grandfather?
The grandfather is 72 years old.
messages.think: The text says the grandmother "is 68" and the grandfather "is 4 years older". 68 + 4 = 72.

messages.content: "Rajesh's grandfather is 4 years older than his grandmother. His grandmother is 68. Every morning the grandfather walks to the dairy for milk, while the grandmother stays home and makes tea." Who makes the tea?
The grandmother makes the tea.
messages.think: The text says "the grandmother stays home and makes tea".

messages.content: "Rajesh's grandfather is 4 years older than his grandmother. His grandmother is 68. Every morning the grandfather walks to the dairy for milk, while the grandmother stays home and makes tea." Who goes to the dairy?
The grandfather goes to the dairy.
messages.think: The text says "the grandfather walks to the dairy for milk".

messages.content: "Rajesh's grandfather is 4 years older than his grandmother. His grandmother is 68. Every morning the grandfather walks to the dairy for milk, while the grandmother stays home and makes tea." How old is Rajesh?
The text does not say how old Rajesh is. It only tells us that his grandmother is 68 and his grandfather is 4 years older.
messages.think: The text gives the ages of the grandparents only. It says nothing about Rajesh's age.

messages.content: what does "homesick" mean?
"Homesick" means feeling sad because you are far from home and miss your family and your place. Example: "In his first month abroad, he was very homesick."
what do I say when I don't understand a form at an office?
"Excuse me, could you help me with this form? I am not sure what to write here." Point to the part you do not understand. Staff are used to this question.
A cinema hall has 24 rows of 18 seats. 395 tickets were sold for a show. How many seats are empty?
37 seats are empty.
what is "bhauju" in English?
"Bhauju" is your elder brother's wife. In English she is your "sister-in-law", but English uses that one word for several relations, so the Nepali word is more exact.
what does "actions speak louder than words" mean?
It means what you do shows more about you than what you say. Example: "He says he will help, but he never comes. Actions speak louder than words."
"postpone" in a sentence please
"The match was postponed because of the rain." "Postpone" means to move something to a later time. "Cancel" means it will not happen at all.
"minute" has two meanings?
Yes. Said "MIN-it", it is sixty seconds: "Wait a minute." Said "my-NYOOT", it means very small: "a minute insect". Same spelling, different sound and meaning.
someone called the wrong number. what do I say politely?
"Sorry, I think you have the wrong number." If they ask whose phone it is, you do not need to give your name; just say, "This is not the number you want."
A shopkeeper buys 50 kg of sugar at 95 rupees per kg and sells it at 110 rupees per kg. What is his profit?
His profit is 750 rupees.
what does "mit" or "mitini" mean?
"Mit" is a lifelong friendship made with a small ceremony, and the two families then treat each other like relatives. Men become "mit", women become "mitini". In English, "bond friend" comes close.
is it "attend the meeting" or "attend to the meeting"?
"Attend the meeting", with no "to". "Attend" means to be present at something: attend class, attend a wedding. "Attend to" means to deal with or look after: "The nurse attended to the patient."
what does "every cloud has a silver lining" mean?
It means every bad situation has something good in it too. Example: "I lost my job, but every cloud has a silver lining: now I have time to finish my course."
how do I ask a caller to wait a moment?
"Could you hold on for a moment, please?" or "Please stay on the line, I will get her." When you come back: "Thank you for waiting."
what's the difference between "fare" and "fair"?
A "fare" is the money you pay to travel: "The bus fare is 50 rupees." "Fair" means just and equal, as in "a fair decision". It is also a big outdoor event: "a book fair".
A plant needs 250 ml of water a day. How many liters is that in 30 days?
It needs 7.5 liters of water in 30 days.
what is a "pidhi"?
A "pidhi" is the raised platform or veranda along the front of a village house, often made of mud, where people sit, work and chat. In English: a veranda or porch.
what does "break the ice" mean?
It means to say or do something to make people feel relaxed when they meet for the first time. Example: "The teacher told a funny story to break the ice on the first day."
how to ask who is calling, politely?
"May I know who is calling, please?" or "Who am I speaking to?" Both are polite. "Who are you?" sounds rude on the phone.
"flour" and "flower" sound the same. how do I know which one?
They do sound the same. "Flour" is the powder for making roti and bread. "Flower" is the coloured part of a plant. The sentence tells you which one: "two kilos of flour", "a red flower".
Zoo tickets are 100 rupees for an adult and 50 for a child. How much do 2 adults and 3 children pay?
They pay 350 rupees.
what is a "kulo"?
A "kulo" is a small channel that carries water from a stream or river to the fields. In English it is an irrigation channel.
what does "pull someone's leg" mean?
It means to joke with someone by saying something untrue, in a friendly way. Example: "Don't worry, there is no exam tomorrow. I'm just pulling your leg!"
how do I ask the pharmacist if I need a prescription?
"Excuse me, do I need a prescription for this medicine?" If you are not sure what to buy, describe the problem and ask: "What do you suggest?" For anything serious, see a doctor first.
"week" or "weak"?
"Week" is seven days: "next week". "Weak" means not strong: "I feel weak after the fever." They sound the same, so the meaning tells you which one to write.
A bus with 45 seats carries 38 passengers from Dhangadhi, and each pays 1200 rupees. How much money is collected?
45600 rupees is collected.
messages.think: The number of seats is not needed. 38 x 1200 = 45600.

messages.content: what does "kharka" mean?
A "kharka" is a high grassy pasture in the hills or mountains, where herders take cows, sheep or yaks to graze in summer.
what does "lend a hand" mean?
It means to help someone. Example: "Can you lend me a hand with these bags?" It is a friendly way to ask for or offer help.
how do I return a shirt that doesn't fit?
Take the shirt and the bill to the shop and say: "Hello, I bought this shirt here, but it doesn't fit. Could I exchange it for another size?" Ask early, before you wash or wear it.
what is a synonym of "end"?
"Finish" or "conclude". "Finish" is for everyday talk: "Finish your food." "Conclude" is formal: "The meeting concluded at five."
My salary went up by 8%. What is my new salary?
I need your old salary to work this out. Tell me how much you earned before the rise, and I will add the 8% for you.
what is "kosheli"?
"Kosheli" is a gift you take when you visit someone, often food from your own area, like fruit, sweets or homemade pickle. In English it is simply a gift or present.
what does "see eye to eye" mean?
It means to agree with someone. It is often used in the negative: "My brother and I don't see eye to eye about money."
how do I report a lost phone at the police station in English?
Say: "I would like to report a lost phone." Then give the details: where and when you last had it, the model and colour, and your phone number. Ask for a copy of the report for your phone company.
how do I pronounce "close" in "close the door" and "close to home"?
"Close the door" has a "z" sound: kloz. "Close to home", meaning near, has an "s" sound: klohs. The verb uses "z"; the adjective uses "s".
Of 60 mangoes in a box, 1/4 were rotten. How many were good?
45 mangoes were good.
what does "saapat" mean?
"Saapat" means borrowing money or things from someone you know, to return later, usually without interest. In English you could call it an informal loan.
another word for "rubbish"
"Garbage", "trash" or "waste". "Rubbish" is British, "garbage" and "trash" are American, and "waste" is used in both: "kitchen waste".
someone at work said "Hang on a second". what does it mean?
It means "Please wait a moment." It is informal and friendly. You can reply "Sure" and wait.
how do I ask the bank to update my mobile number?
"Hello, I would like to update the mobile number on my account. What do I need to do?" They will usually give you a form and check your ID.
what's the opposite of "sharp" for a knife?
"Blunt". A sharp knife cuts easily; a blunt knife does not: "This knife is blunt, so it needs sharpening."
A shop took in 4200 rupees on Sunday, 3900 on Monday and 5100 on Tuesday. What is the average per day?
The average is 4400 rupees per day.
what is a "ghatta"?
A "ghatta" is a traditional water mill. A stream turns a wooden wheel, and the wheel turns a stone that grinds grain into flour.
what does "Fair enough" mean?
It means "That is reasonable, I accept it." Example: "I can't come today, but I'll come tomorrow." "Fair enough."
how should I answer "Why should we hire you?"

Link your skills to the job: "I have the skills you need for this role, I learn quickly, and I work well with people. I am ready to work hard and grow here." Add one real example from your study or work.
what is the opposite of "maximum"?
"Minimum". Example: "The minimum age for this job is 18 and the maximum is 35."
how to pronounce words ending in "-tion"?
Say "-tion" as "shun": station (STAY-shun), nation (NAY-shun), education (ed-yoo-KAY-shun). The stress usually falls just before "-tion".
I start studying at 7:40 pm and study for 1 hour 35 minutes. When do I stop?
You stop at 9:15 pm.
messages.think: 7:40 pm plus 1 hour is 8:40 pm. 35 more minutes makes 9:15 pm.

messages.content: what is the difference between "khet" and "bari"?
"Khet" is low, flat land that holds water, where rice is grown. "Bari" is dry, higher land for maize, millet and vegetables. In English, you can say "paddy field" for khet and "dry field" for bari.
what does "It's up to you" mean?
It means "You decide." Example: "Tea or coffee?" "It's up to you." It is polite, but if you always say it, people may want you to choose sometimes.
how do I end a job interview politely?
Stand up, smile and say: "Thank you for your time. I enjoyed learning about the job, and I look forward to hearing from you." A firm, short handshake is fine if they offer one.
opposite of "visible"
"Invisible". Something visible can be seen; something invisible cannot: "Air is invisible."
how do you pronounce "cupboard"?
Say KUB-erd. The "p" is silent and the "board" part becomes a short "erd".
A runner covers 5 km in 25 minutes. How many minutes does she take per km?
She takes 5 minutes per km.
what is a "pandhero"?
A "pandhero" is a village water source, a spring or spout where people fetch water and wash. In English: a spring or a water point.
my friends said "Count me in" about the picnic. what does it mean?
It means "I will join you; include me." The opposite is "Count me out", which means "I won't join."
in an email, is "Dear Sir" or "Hi" better?
For a formal email to someone you do not know, use "Dear Sir" or "Dear Madam", or "Dear Mr. Rai" if you know the name. Use "Hi (name)" for colleagues and people you know well.
use "instead of" in a sentence
"I drank water instead of cold drinks." "Instead of" means in place of something. After it, use a noun or an -ing verb: "Walk instead of taking the bus."
what does "revert" mean in an office email?

In standard English, "revert" means to go back to an earlier state. In South Asian offices, "Please revert" is often used to mean "Please reply". It is clearer to write "Please reply" or "Please let me know."
how do I write "please find attached" correctly?
Write: "Please find the report attached." or "I have attached the report." The second one sounds more modern and friendly. Always check that the file is really attached before you press Send.
make a sentence with "so that"
"I left early so that I could catch the first bus." "So that" shows the purpose of an action. It often comes with "can" or "could".
how to say "receipt"?
Say ri-SEET. The "p" is silent.
what does "What is your good name?" mean?
It is a polite way of asking "What is your name?" in South Asian English. In standard English, just say "May I know your name?" or "What's your name?"
word for a person who does not eat meat?
A "vegetarian". If someone also avoids milk, eggs and other animal foods, they are a "vegan". In Nepali: "shakahari".
where is the stress in "photograph" and "photographer"?
PHO-to-graph has the stress at the start, but pho-TOG-ra-pher moves it to the second part. Many long words shift their stress like this, so listen and repeat.
how should I end an email to my teacher?
End with "Thank you," or "Kind regards," and then write your full name on the next line. Add your class and roll number if the teacher needs them to know who you are.
I'm going to Lumbini with my school next week!

That sounds like a wonderful trip! Lumbini is the birthplace of the Buddha, and the garden and the monasteries are peaceful to walk around. Carry a water bottle and a cap, because the Terai sun can be strong.
My grandfather turned 90 today.
Ninety years! What a wonderful milestone. Please wish him a very happy birthday. Ask him to tell you one story from when he was your age; it will be a lovely memory for both of you.
I made sel roti for the first time and they came out round!
Well done! Getting them round is the hardest part. Your family must be proud. Next time, try making a few extra for the neighbours.
Our football team lost the final 2-1. Everyone is sad.
Losing a final by one goal hurts, but reaching the final shows how good your team is. Rest for a day, then talk about what went well and what to practise. Next season you will be stronger.
I'm saving for a laptop that costs 75000 rupees. I have 30000 so far.
Great progress! You need 45000 rupees more. If you save a fixed amount every month, you can work out exactly when you will reach your goal.
My mom says I spend too much time on my phone.
She may have a point. Try a simple rule: no phone during meals and for the last hour before sleep. Check your screen time in the phone's settings; seeing the real number often helps you cut down.
My little brother broke my headphones.

That is frustrating! Take a breath before you talk to him. If it was an accident, tell him calmly that he must ask before using your things. Sometimes a broken wire or plug can be repaired at a phone shop for a small cost.
We have guests from Japan coming next week. What Nepali food should we serve?

Dal bhat with a few vegetable dishes is a safe start, and momo is almost always a hit. Sel roti or yomari can be a nice sweet treat. Ask them how spicy they like their food, and keep the chilli on the side.
I want to grow vegetables but I only have a small balcony.

Pots and old buckets work well. Start with easy leafy greens like spinach (palungo), mustard greens (rayo) and coriander, which grow fast and need only a few hours of sun. Make holes at the bottom of each pot so the water can drain.
My hostel roommate keeps the light on until 2 am and I can't sleep.
Talk to your roommate at a calm time, not at 2 am: "I find it hard to sleep with the light on. Could you use a small table lamp after 11?" A sleeping mask can help while you sort it out.
It's my parents' wedding anniversary on Sunday. What can I do for them?
Something simple and personal works best: cook their favourite meal, write them a card, or frame an old photo of the two of them. An evening together without phones may be the best gift of all.
I got selected for the district volleyball team!
Congratulations! That is a big step. Keep training regularly, eat well and sleep enough before matches. Which position do you play?
My elder sister is going abroad to study and I will miss her a lot.
Of course you will. It is a big change for both of you. Plan a weekly video call, send her photos of home, and maybe write her one letter by hand. Distance feels shorter when you keep a routine.
I'm so bored of reading the same chapter again and again.

Change the way you study it. Close the book and explain the chapter aloud as if you were teaching someone, make a one-page summary, or answer old exam questions on it. A new method makes the same chapter feel fresh.
I passed my driving test on the second try!
Congratulations! Passing on the second try shows you did not give up. Drive carefully in the first months; the license is the start of learning, not the end.
Write a message to my class group that tomorrow's class is cancelled.
"Hello everyone, tomorrow's class is cancelled. Please pass this on to anyone who is not in the group. Thank you."
Help me write a short note asking my neighbour to move their bike away from my gate.
"Namaste! Your bike is parked in front of my gate. Could you please move it a little so the gate can open? Thank you."
Write a message to my friend saying I can't come to his birthday party because I have an exam the next day.
"Happy birthday in advance! I am really sorry, I can't come to the party because I have an exam the next day. Have a great time, and let's celebrate together after my exam."
Write a message to my teacher asking for the notes I missed when I was sick.
"Good morning, sir. I was sick and missed some classes. Could you please tell me which notes and homework I missed? I will copy them and catch up. Thank you." Use "madam" if your teacher is a woman.
Rewrite this to sound kinder: "Your work is bad. Do it again."
"Thank you for your work. Some parts need a little more care. Could you look at it again and improve these points?" Then point to the exact parts, so the person knows what to fix.
Make this shorter: "I am writing this message to let you know that I will not be able to attend the meeting that is going to be held tomorrow."
"Sorry, I can't attend tomorrow's meeting."
Write a one-line reminder for my family to turn off the gas before sleeping.
"Before you go to sleep, please check that the gas is turned off. Safety first!"
How can I ask my manager for feedback on my work?
"Could you spare ten minutes this week to give me some feedback on my work? I would like to know what I am doing well and what I can improve." Asking this way shows you care about growing.
Write a message to a seller asking if the second-hand bike is still available.
"Hello, I saw your ad for the second-hand bike. Is it still available? If yes, could I come and see it this week?"
Write a short English line for the board of my momo shop in Butwal.
A few options: "Hot momo, served fresh in Butwal." / "Your momo stop in Butwal." / "Butwal's place for momo and smiles." Pick the one that fits your shop best.
What does "Beware of dog" mean on a gate?
It means there is a dog inside that may bark or bite, so be careful. Do not open the gate yourself; ring the bell or call, and wait for the owner.
a restaurant menu says "10% service charge extra". what does that mean?
It means 10% of your food bill will be added for the service. So if your food costs 1000 rupees, the service charge is 100 rupees and you pay 1100, plus any tax shown on the bill.
There is a "No horn" sign on the road. What does it mean?
It means drivers should not sound their horn in that area. Such signs are common near hospitals and schools and in busy city areas, to reduce noise.
what does "Handle with care" on a box mean?
It means the box holds something that can break or get damaged easily, so carry it gently and do not throw or drop it.
what does "Keep left" mean on the road?
It means vehicles should stay on the left side of the road. Traffic in Nepal drives on the left, so you see this sign often at turns and road dividers.
A sign at someone's house says "Please remove your shoes". What should I do?
It means you should take off your shoes before you go inside. Leave them by the door or on the shoe rack. Many Nepali homes ask guests to do this.
correct: "I am having fever since yesterday"
Say: "I have had a fever since yesterday" or simply "I have a fever." We do not use "having" for an illness, and "since yesterday" needs the present perfect.
is "My head is paining" correct English?
Say: "I have a headache" or "My head hurts." "Paining" is used in South Asian English, but standard English uses "hurt" or "ache".
my friend says "open the light". is that right?

In English we say "turn on the light" or "switch on the light", and "turn off the light". "Open" and "close" are for doors, windows and boxes. In Nepali, "batti bala" is the closest to "turn on the light".
correct: "I am going to give my exam tomorrow"
Say: "I am going to take my exam tomorrow" or "I have an exam tomorrow." In British English you can also "sit" an exam. Teachers give exams; students take them.
is "She is eating medicine" right?
Say: "She is taking medicine." In English we "take" medicine, even though Nepali says "aushadhi khanu".
correct: "We will do party tonight"
Say: "We will have a party tonight." You can also "throw a party" or "hold a party", but not "do" one.
correct: "My brother is doing job in Qatar"
Say: "My brother works in Qatar" or "My brother has a job in Qatar." English does not say "doing job".
"I am born in Jhapa" - right?
Say: "I was born in Jhapa." Birth happened in the past, so we always use "was born" or "were born".
correct: "We were five people in the car"
Say: "There were five of us in the car." To give the number of people in a group, English uses "there were ... of us".
correct: "Do you know cooking?"
Say: "Do you know how to cook?" or "Can you cook?" To ask about a skill, use "know how to" + verb, or "can".
correct: "She is very beautiful than her sister"
Say: "She is more beautiful than her sister", or "much more beautiful" for a stronger form. "Very" does not go with comparisons; use "much" or "far" instead.
Is "Many many happy returns of the day" correct?
The traditional phrase is "Many happy returns of the day", with one "many". It sounds a little old-fashioned now; "Happy birthday!" is the usual wish today.
correct: "Where is your native place?"
Say: "Where are you from?" or "Where is your hometown?" "Native place" is common in South Asian English but sounds unusual to other speakers.
Someone said "Happy Dashain!" and I replied "Same to you". Is that okay?
Yes, "Same to you" is correct and polite. You can also say "You too!" or "Happy Dashain to you too!"
correct: "He enjoys to swim in the river"
Say: "He enjoys swimming in the river." Some verbs, like enjoy, finish, avoid and mind, are followed by the -ing form, not by "to".
correct: "We decided going to Pokhara"
Say: "We decided to go to Pokhara." Verbs like decide, hope, plan and want are followed by "to" + verb.
is it "I had my hair cut" or "I cut my hair"?
Both are correct but they mean different things. "I had my hair cut" means a barber cut it for you. "I cut my hair" means you cut it yourself. Use "had something done" when someone else does the job.
correct: "Me also want to come"
Say: "I also want to come" or "I want to come too." Use "I" as the subject; "me" comes after verbs and prepositions: "Take me with you."
"He hurt him while playing" - who got hurt?
As written, "him" means another person got hurt. If he hurt his own body, say: "He hurt himself while playing." Use himself, herself and myself when the doer and the receiver are the same person.
correct: "Please do not disturb me, I am in hurry"
Say: "Please do not disturb me, I am in a hurry." The phrase is "in a hurry", with "a".
How do I answer "Don't you like tea?" if I do like it?

Say "Yes, I do." In English the answer follows the fact, not the question: "Yes, I do" if you like it, "No, I don't" if you don't. In Nepali, "ho" can agree with a negative question, so this one is easy to get wrong.
what does "Do you mind if I sit here?" mean, and how do I say yes?
It asks if you have a problem with the person sitting there. To allow it, say "No, not at all" or "Please go ahead." Saying "Yes" would mean you do mind, which is the opposite of what you want.
what is the right order: "a red big ball" or "a big red ball"?
"A big red ball." In English, size usually comes before colour: "a small black bag", "a long white scarf". Opinion words come first of all: "a lovely big red ball".
how do I say dates in English, like 5/6?

Say "the fifth of June" or "June the fifth". In writing: "5 June" in British English or "June 5" in American English. Careful: in American English 5/6 means May 6, so write the month as a word to avoid confusion.
How do we say 7:45 in English?
Say "seven forty-five" or "a quarter to eight". In the same way, 7:15 is "a quarter past seven" and 7:30 is "half past seven".
How do I read 1,25,000 in English?
In English it is "one hundred and twenty-five thousand", written 125,000. Nepali and Indian writing groups the digits by lakh (1,25,000), but international English groups them in threes.
"a piece of", "a loaf of" - how do I count things like bread and soap?
Use a container or shape word: a loaf of bread, a bar of soap, a bunch of bananas, a packet of biscuits, a cup of tea, a slice of cake. This is how we count things that cannot be counted directly.
what does "Have you ever" mean? Like "Have you ever been to Ilam?"
"Have you ever" asks if something happened at any time in your life up to now. Answer "Yes, I have" or "No, I haven't." If you add when, change to the past: "Yes, I went there last year."
what is the difference between "each other" and "themselves"?
"Each other" means one person does it to the other: "Sita and Gita helped each other." "Themselves" means each person does it to his or her own self: "They looked at themselves in the mirror."
what does "harvest" mean?
To harvest is to cut and collect a crop when it is ready, like rice in Mangsir. It is also a noun: "The harvest was good this year." In Nepali: "baali katnu".
what does "I should have studied" mean?
It means you did not study, and now you feel that was a mistake. "Should have + past participle" talks about the past with regret: "I should have left earlier."
how do I pronounce "the" before "apple"?
Before a vowel sound, say "thee": thee apple, thee egg. Before a consonant sound, say a short "thuh": thuh book, thuh bus. The spelling stays the same.
what is the difference between "sow" and "plant"?
You sow seeds: you spread them or put them into the soil. You plant young plants or trees: "We planted the rice seedlings in Asar." In Nepali, sowing is "biu chharnu" and planting rice is "ropnu".
what does "take it easy" mean?
It means relax and don't work too hard or worry too much. People also say it as a friendly goodbye: "See you tomorrow. Take it easy!"
"across", "through" and "along" - how are they different?

"Across" means from one side to the other: walk across the road. "Through" means inside something from one end to the other: walk through the forest. "Along" means following a line: walk along the river.
what does "plough" mean?
To plough is to turn over the soil before planting, with oxen or a tractor. In Nepali: "halo jotnu". The tool is also called a plough.
I say "sip" when I mean "ship". How do I fix it?

For "sh", round your lips a little and pull your tongue back from your teeth, then push air: ship, she, shop. For "s", keep your lips flat and your tongue close to your teeth: sip, sea, sock. Practise the pairs slowly.
Can "since" mean "because"?
Yes. "Since it was raining, we stayed home" means "because it was raining". "Since" can also mean "from a time": "since Monday". The sentence tells you which one it is.
my geography book says "terrace farming". what does it mean?
Terrace farming is growing crops on flat steps cut into a hillside, so the soil and water do not run down the slope. You see it all over the hills of Nepal. Each step is a "gara" in Nepali.
what does "on cloud nine" mean?
It means extremely happy. Example: "When she got her visa, she was on cloud nine."
"children's" or "childrens'"?
"Children's". "Children" is already plural, so we just add 's: the children's park, the women's team. For plurals that end in s, add only the apostrophe: the students' books.
what does "yield" mean for a farmer?
"Yield" is the amount a field or a crop produces. Example: "With better seeds, the yield of his wheat field went up." It is also a verb: "This field yields a lot of maize."
why is the k silent in "knee"?
In English words that start with "kn", the k is not pronounced: knee (nee), know (noh), knife (nife), knock (nok). It was spoken long ago, but the sound dropped while the spelling stayed.
how do I write 1st, 2nd, 3rd in words?
First (1st), second (2nd), third (3rd), and then fourth (4th) and onwards with "th". But 21st, 22nd and 23rd go back to st, nd and rd, while 11th, 12th and 13th always take "th".
someone asked me "Does the name Bikash Rai ring a bell?" what does that mean?
"Does it ring a bell?" means "Does it sound familiar? Do you remember it?" You can answer: "Yes, it rings a bell" or "No, it doesn't ring a bell."
what is compost?
Compost is rotted plant and food waste, like vegetable peels and leaves, that becomes rich soil. Farmers mix it into the fields to feed the crops. Cow dung manure, "gobar mal", does a similar job.
how to make "Run in the corridor" into a rule saying not to?
"Do not run in the corridor" or "Don't run in the corridor." For a polite sign: "Please do not run in the corridor."
what does "sprain" mean?
A sprain is an injury when you twist a joint, like an ankle or a wrist, and it swells and hurts. In Nepali: "markinu". Rest it, keep it raised and see a doctor if the pain or swelling is bad.
what does "sit on the fence" mean?
It means not choosing a side in an argument or decision. Example: "Mum wants to go to the village and Dad wants to stay; my sister is sitting on the fence."
what does "would" mean in "When I was small, my grandmother would tell me stories"?
Here "would" means something that happened again and again in the past, like "used to": "My grandmother used to tell me stories." It does not talk about the future here.
what is a "bruise"?
A bruise is a blue or purple mark on the skin after you hit or bump something. It slowly turns green and yellow and goes away by itself in a week or two.
which words have a silent w?
The w is silent before r at the start of a word: write, wrong, wrap, wrist. It is also silent in "answer", "sword" and "two".
"let's" or "lets"?
"Let's" with an apostrophe means "let us": "Let's go." "Lets" without an apostrophe is the verb "let" with "s": "My father lets me ride his bike."
what does "steal the show" mean?
It means to get the most attention and praise at an event. Example: "The little dancers stole the show at the school function."
what is a rash on the skin?
A rash is a patch of red spots or redness on the skin, often itchy. Do not scratch it. If it spreads, lasts more than a few days or comes with fever, see a doctor.
When do I say "me too" and when "me neither"?
"Me too" agrees with a positive sentence: "I love momo." "Me too!" "Me neither" agrees with a negative one: "I don't like bitter gourd." "Me neither."
what does "dizzy" mean?
Dizzy means feeling that the room is spinning and you might fall. In Nepali: "ringata lagnu". Sit down at once, drink some water, and see a doctor if it happens often.
how do you pronounce "often"?
Most people say OFF-en, with a silent t. Some speakers say the t, as in OFF-ten, and both are accepted.
what does "a drop in the ocean" mean?
It means a very small amount compared with what is needed. Example: "Our 2000 rupees is a drop in the ocean, but every bit helps the flood victims."
difference between "Would you like tea?" and "Do you like tea?"

"Would you like tea?" is an offer: do you want some now? "Do you like tea?" asks about your taste in general. Answer the first with "Yes, please" or "No, thank you", and the second with "Yes, I do" or "Not really."
what does "sore throat" mean?
A sore throat is pain in the throat, often with a cold, so it hurts to swallow. In Nepali: "ghaati dukhnu". Warm drinks and rest usually help; see a doctor if it lasts or comes with a high fever.
correct: "She speaks the English very well"
Say: "She speaks English very well." A language name alone takes no "the". Use "the" only with the word "language": "the English language".
what is a "runny nose"?
A runny nose is when liquid keeps coming out of your nose, usually with a cold. In Nepali: "singhan bagnu". Keep tissues with you and wash your hands often.
how do I say "clothes"?
Say klohz, in one part, with a "z" sound at the end. It sounds almost the same as the verb "close", as in "close the door".
what does "word of mouth" mean?
It means news that spreads because people tell each other, not through advertisements. Example: "Her tea shop became popular by word of mouth."
what does "must" mean in "He must be tired"?
Here "must" means you are almost sure because of what you know: he worked all day, so he must be tired. It is not an order. The opposite is "can't be": "She can't be at school; it's Saturday."
what does "itchy" mean?
"Itchy" describes a feeling on the skin that makes you want to scratch: "Mosquito bites are itchy." In Nepali: "chilaunu".
what does "have a sweet tooth" mean?
It means you love eating sweet things. Example: "My grandfather has a sweet tooth; he always keeps jeri and laddu at home."
what is the difference between "chop", "slice" and "dice"?
To chop is to cut into pieces, not always neat: chop onions. To slice is to cut thin flat pieces: slice bread. To dice is to cut into small cubes: dice potatoes for a curry.
how to make adverbs from adjectives?
Usually add "ly": quick to quickly, careful to carefully. If the word ends in "y", change it to "i": happy to happily. Some are irregular: good becomes well, while fast and hard stay the same.
what does "knead" mean in a recipe?
To knead is to press, fold and push dough with your hands until it is smooth, as you do for roti. In Nepali: "pitho mugnu". The "k" is silent, so it sounds like "need".
how do I hear the difference between "can" and "can't" when people speak fast?
In fast speech "can" is short and weak, like "kn": "I kn come." "Can't" is longer, with a clear vowel and often a t at the end: "I CAN'T come." Listen for the stress.
what does "in a nutshell" mean?
It means in very few words, as a short summary. Example: "In a nutshell, the trip was tiring but fun."
Why do we say "The bus leaves at 6 tomorrow" in the present tense?
For fixed timetables and schedules, English uses the present simple even for the future: "The bus leaves at 6", "The exam starts on Monday." The plan is fixed, so it is treated like a fact.
what does "simmer" mean?
To simmer is to cook something gently on low heat, just below boiling, with only small bubbles, like dal after it comes to a boil.
what does "keep your fingers crossed" mean?
It means to hope for good luck. Example: "My results come out tomorrow. Keep your fingers crossed for me!"
what does "steam" mean in cooking?
To steam is to cook food with the hot vapour from boiling water, without putting the food in the water. Momo are steamed in a special pot with layers. In Nepali: "baaph ma pakaunu".
When do we say "What a" and when "How"?
Use "What a" with a noun: "What a beautiful view!" Use "How" with an adjective alone: "How beautiful!" With plurals, drop "a": "What lovely flowers!"
is "fry" the same as "deep-fry"?
Not quite. To fry is to cook in a little oil in a pan. To deep-fry is to cook food fully covered in hot oil, like sel roti, pakoda or samosa.
what does "time flies" mean?
It means time passes very quickly. People often say, "Time flies when you're having fun." Example: "My son is starting college already. Time flies!"
what does "peel" mean?
To peel is to take the skin off a fruit or vegetable: peel a potato, peel an orange. The skin itself is also called the peel. In Nepali: "bokra".
how do I use "it takes" for time?
Use "It takes" + time + "to" + verb: "It takes 20 minutes to walk to school." Add a person: "It takes me 20 minutes." In the past: "It took us six hours to reach Pokhara."
what does "a pinch of salt" mean?
A pinch is the very small amount you can hold between your finger and thumb: "Add a pinch of salt." The phrase "take it with a pinch of salt" means do not fully believe something.
what does "easier said than done" mean?
It means something sounds easy but is hard to do in real life. Example: "Just wake up at 5 every day? Easier said than done!"
fog and mist - are they the same?
Both are tiny water drops in the air, but fog is thicker, so you cannot see far. Mist is lighter and thinner. Nepali uses "kuhiro" for both.
what is "hail"?
Hail is small balls of ice that fall from the sky during a storm, like frozen rain. In Nepali: "asina". It can damage crops and roofs.
what does "back to square one" mean?
It means you have to start again from the beginning because your plan failed. Example: "The landlord sold the house, so our search for a room is back to square one."
what is a "drought"?
A drought is a long time with little or no rain, so fields, wells and streams dry up. In Nepali: "khaderi". It rhymes with "out": drowt.
thunder and lightning - what is the difference?
Lightning is the bright flash in the sky. Thunder is the loud sound that comes after it. Light travels faster than sound, so we see the flash first and hear the thunder later.
what does "on the dot" mean?
It means at exactly that time. Example: "The class starts at 7 on the dot, so don't be late."
what is the opposite of "export"?
"Import". To export is to sell goods to another country; to import is to bring goods in from another country. Example: "Nepal imports petrol and exports tea and carpets."
How do I book an appointment with a doctor on the phone?
"Hello, I would like to book an appointment with Dr. (name). Is there a time free this week?" Then give your name and phone number, and repeat the date and time back to make sure you heard it right.
"Bus timetable, Dhulikhel to Kathmandu: 6:30 am, 8:00 am, 11:15 am and 2:45 pm. The trip takes about 1 hour 30 minutes." When is the last bus?
The last bus leaves at 2:45 pm.
messages.think: The times are 6:30 am, 8:00 am, 11:15 am and 2:45 pm. The last one is 2:45 pm.

messages.content: "Bus timetable, Dhulikhel to Kathmandu: 6:30 am, 8:00 am, 11:15 am and 2:45 pm. The trip takes about 1 hour 30 minutes." When is the first bus?
The first bus leaves at 6:30 am.
messages.think: The earliest time in the list is 6:30 am.

messages.content: "Bus timetable, Dhulikhel to Kathmandu: 6:30 am, 8:00 am, 11:15 am and 2:45 pm. The trip takes about 1 hour 30 minutes." If I take the 8:00 bus, when will I reach Kathmandu?
You will reach Kathmandu at about 9:30 am.
messages.think: The trip takes about 1 hour 30 minutes. 8:00 plus 1 hour is 9:00, plus 30 minutes is 9:30.

messages.content: "Bus timetable, Dhulikhel to Kathmandu: 6:30 am, 8:00 am, 11:15 am and 2:45 pm. The trip takes about 1 hour 30 minutes." How many buses run each day?
4 buses run each day.
messages.think: The list has 6:30, 8:00, 11:15 and 2:45: that is 4 times.

messages.content: At the post office, how do I ask to send a parcel to India?
"I would like to send this parcel to India. How much will it cost, and how long will it take?" They may weigh it and ask what is inside, so keep a list of the things you packed.
A tea shop sells 120 cups a day at 25 rupees each. How much does it earn in a week?
The tea shop earns 21000 rupees in a week.
what does "jhola" mean?
A jhola is a cloth bag with a shoulder strap, used for carrying books, shopping or things for a journey. In English: a shoulder bag or cloth bag.
How do I say my phone screen is broken at a repair shop?
"Hello, my phone screen is cracked. How much will it cost to change it, and how long will it take?" Ask if they use an original screen, and remove your SIM and memory card before you leave the phone.
"Sujata's diary: Monday - I woke up late and missed the school bus, so my father took me on his bike. In the evening I finished my science project." How did Sujata go to school on Monday?
She went to school on her father's bike.
messages.think: The diary says "my father took me on his bike".

messages.content: "Sujata's diary: Monday - I woke up late and missed the school bus, so my father took me on his bike. In the evening I finished my science project." Why did she miss the school bus?
She missed the bus because she woke up late.
messages.think: The diary says "I woke up late and missed the school bus".

messages.content: "Sujata's diary: Monday - I woke up late and missed the school bus, so my father took me on his bike. In the evening I finished my science project." What did she finish in the evening?
She finished her science project.
messages.think: The diary says "In the evening I finished my science project."

messages.content: "Sujata's diary: Monday - I woke up late and missed the school bus, so my father took me on his bike. In the evening I finished my science project." Did her mother take her to school?
No. Her father took her to school, not her mother.
messages.think: The diary says "my father took me on his bike". It does not say her mother took her.

messages.content: what does "dharmashala" mean?
A dharmashala is a simple free or cheap resting house for travellers and pilgrims, often near a temple or on an old trail. In English: a rest house.
how do I ask my landlord to fix a leaking tap?
"Namaste, the tap in the kitchen is leaking and water is being wasted. Could you please send a plumber to fix it? Thank you." Send a photo if it helps.
A tank holds 1000 liters. It is 3/5 full. How many more liters are needed to fill it?
400 more liters are needed to fill the tank.
what does "gundruk" mean?

Gundruk is fermented and dried leafy greens, usually from mustard, radish or cauliflower leaves. It is made into a sour soup or pickle and is eaten with rice or dhindo. It is one of Nepal's best-known foods.
In an interview, how do I talk about my weakness without sounding bad?

Choose a real but small weakness and show what you are doing about it: "I used to find it hard to speak in meetings, so now I prepare my points in advance and I speak up more." Avoid a weakness that is central to the job.
"Market prices: tomatoes 80 rupees per kg, onions 70 rupees per kg, cauliflower 60 rupees each." How much do 3 kg of onions cost?
3 kg of onions cost 210 rupees.
messages.think: The list says "onions 70 rupees per kg". 3 x 70 = 210.

messages.content: "Market prices: tomatoes 80 rupees per kg, onions 70 rupees per kg, cauliflower 60 rupees each." How is cauliflower sold?
Cauliflower is sold by the piece, at 60 rupees each.
messages.think: The list says "cauliflower 60 rupees each", so it is sold by the piece, not by the kg.

messages.content: "Market prices: tomatoes 80 rupees per kg, onions 70 rupees per kg, cauliflower 60 rupees each." Which costs more per kg, tomatoes or onions?
Tomatoes cost more: 80 rupees per kg, against 70 for onions.
messages.think: Tomatoes are 80 per kg and onions 70 per kg. 80 is more than 70.

messages.content: "Market prices: tomatoes 80 rupees per kg, onions 70 rupees per kg, cauliflower 60 rupees each." How much are potatoes?
The list does not give a price for potatoes. It only has tomatoes, onions and cauliflower.
messages.think: The list has tomatoes, onions and cauliflower only. Potatoes are not on it.

messages.content: what does "kachahari" mean?
"Kachahari" is an old word for a court: a place where disputes were heard and settled. In English: a court or a hearing.
How do I complain to a bus company that my bag was damaged?

"Dear Sir/Madam, I travelled on your bus and my bag was damaged during the trip. I am attaching a photo and my ticket. Please let me know how you can help." Give your ticket number and travel date if you have them.
A carpenter makes 3 chairs in 2 days. How many chairs can he make in 10 days?
He can make 15 chairs in 10 days.
what does "gaun" mean in English?
"Gaun" means village. "Gaunle" means a villager, and "gaunpalika" means a rural municipality, the local government of a rural area.
what should I say if I get a wrong bill at a restaurant?
"Excuse me, I think there is a mistake in the bill. We did not order this item. Could you please check it?" Point to the item, and stay polite; the staff can correct it quickly.
"Office notice: From 1 Baisakh, office hours will be 10 am to 5 pm. Lunch break is from 1 pm to 1:30 pm. Saturday remains a holiday." What time will the office close?
The office will close at 5 pm.
messages.think: The notice says "office hours will be 10 am to 5 pm".

messages.content: "Office notice: From 1 Baisakh, office hours will be 10 am to 5 pm. Lunch break is from 1 pm to 1:30 pm. Saturday remains a holiday." How long is the lunch break?
The lunch break is 30 minutes long.
messages.think: The break is "from 1 pm to 1:30 pm". That is 30 minutes.

messages.content: "Office notice: From 1 Baisakh, office hours will be 10 am to 5 pm. Lunch break is from 1 pm to 1:30 pm. Saturday remains a holiday." Which day is a holiday?
Saturday is a holiday.
messages.think: The notice says "Saturday remains a holiday."

messages.content: "Office notice: From 1 Baisakh, office hours will be 10 am to 5 pm. Lunch break is from 1 pm to 1:30 pm. Saturday remains a holiday." Is Sunday a holiday too?
The notice does not say that Sunday is a holiday. It only says Saturday remains a holiday.
messages.think: The notice names only Saturday as a holiday. It says nothing about Sunday.

messages.content: what is a "bhatti"?
A bhatti is a small roadside eatery and lodge where travellers can get tea, simple meals and sometimes a bed. In English: a small inn or tea house.
what do I say to the receptionist when I reach a hospital?
"Hello, I need to see a doctor. Where do I get the ticket?" If it is serious, say "This is an emergency" so they can send you straight to the emergency room.
A school has 6 classes of 32 students. 18 students are absent today. How many are present?
174 students are present.
what does "bratabandha" mean?

Bratabandha is a coming-of-age ceremony for boys in some Nepali communities. The boy's head is shaved and he receives a sacred thread, called the "janai". In English it is often called a sacred thread ceremony.
what do I say to a teacher when I need more time for an assignment?
"Sir, I am sorry, I could not finish the assignment on time. Could I please submit it by (day)?" Ask before the due date, not after, and give the true reason briefly if you want.
I walk 2 km in 25 minutes. How long will 6 km take at the same speed?
6 km will take 75 minutes, which is 1 hour 15 minutes.
messages.think: 6 / 2 = 3. 3 x 25 = 75 minutes, which is 1 hour 15 minutes.

messages.content: what does "mela" mean?
A mela is a fair: a big outdoor gathering with stalls, food, games and often a festival or a temple event at its heart. In English: a fair or festival fair.
how do I ask someone to repeat their name?
"Sorry, could you say your name again, please?" or "How do you spell that?" It is polite to ask; getting someone's name right shows respect.
A shop sells notebooks in packs of 5 for 300 rupees. How much does one notebook cost?
One notebook costs 60 rupees.
what is "achar"?
Achar is a spicy side dish, like a pickle or a fresh chutney, eaten with rice or snacks. It can be made from tomato, radish, mango, timur or many other things.
How do I tell my colleague that I will cover his shift?
"Don't worry, I can cover your shift on (day). Just let me know if there is anything special I need to do."
"Ramesh and Pratima both run every morning. Ramesh runs 4 km and Pratima runs 6 km. Pratima starts at 5:30 and Ramesh at 6:00." Who runs farther?
Pratima runs farther.
messages.think: Ramesh runs 4 km and Pratima runs 6 km. 6 is more than 4.

messages.content: "Ramesh and Pratima both run every morning. Ramesh runs 4 km and Pratima runs 6 km. Pratima starts at 5:30 and Ramesh at 6:00." Who starts earlier?
Pratima starts earlier.
messages.think: Pratima starts at 5:30 and Ramesh at 6:00. 5:30 comes before 6:00.

messages.content: "Ramesh and Pratima both run every morning. Ramesh runs 4 km and Pratima runs 6 km. Pratima starts at 5:30 and Ramesh at 6:00." How many km do they run together in a week?
Together they run 70 km in a week.
messages.think: one day: 4 + 6 = 10 km. one week: 10 x 7 = 70 km.

messages.content: "Ramesh and Pratima both run every morning. Ramesh runs 4 km and Pratima runs 6 km. Pratima starts at 5:30 and Ramesh at 6:00." Who starts later?
Ramesh starts later.
messages.think: Ramesh starts at 6:00, which is after Pratima's 5:30.

messages.content: what does "mukhiya" mean?
A mukhiya is a village headman, a leader of a village or community, especially in the past. The word is still used in some places for a respected local leader.
How do I ask for a discount politely in a clothes shop?
"This is a little over my budget. Is there any discount on this?" or "If I buy two, can you give me a better price?" A smile helps, and if they say no, accept it kindly.
A driver earns 1500 rupees a day and works 26 days a month. He spends 22000 rupees a month. How much does he save?
He saves 17000 rupees a month.
what does "kodo" mean?
"Kodo" is finger millet, a small reddish-brown grain grown in the hills. It is used to make dhindo and roti.
How do I say "I'm just looking" in a shop?
Say: "I'm just looking, thank you." It politely tells the shopkeeper you do not need help right now. If you have a question later, say: "Excuse me, could you help me?"
3 friends share a taxi fare of 1350 rupees equally. How much does each pay?
Each friend pays 450 rupees.
what is "pathshala"?
"Pathshala" is an old word for a school, a place of learning. Today "school" or "vidyalaya" is more common, but you see "pathshala" in some old names.
I want to open a new SIM card. What do I say at the shop?
"Hello, I would like a new SIM card. What documents do you need?" They usually ask for your citizenship card or passport and a photo. Ask which data packs they have.
A wall clock gains 2 minutes every day. How many minutes will it gain in 3 weeks?
It will gain 42 minutes in 3 weeks.
what is a "gufa"?
A "gufa" is a cave. Two well-known caves, Gupteshwor Mahadev and Mahendra cave, are near Pokhara.
how do I tell a friend that I'm sorry I forgot to call back?
"Sorry, I completely forgot to call you back! Is now a good time to talk?" Keep it light and call soon; that fixes it better than a long apology.
A family of 5 eats 1.5 kg of rice a day. How much rice do they need for 30 days?
They need 45 kg of rice for 30 days.
messages.think: 1.5 x 30 = 45. The number of people is already included in the daily amount.

messages.content: what does "bajar" mean?
"Bajar" means market or bazaar: a place with many shops. "Bajar jaanu" means to go shopping or go to the market area.
I opened a small tea shop near the bus park last week.

Congratulations on your new shop! A bus park is a busy spot, so mornings and evenings will be your best hours. Keep the tea fresh, the cups clean and the price clear on a board. Regular customers come back for a friendly face.
Change into plural: "This is my book."
"These are my books." "This" becomes "these", "is" becomes "are", and "book" becomes "books".
Write an email to a hotel in Pokhara to book a double room for two nights from Friday.

"Dear Sir/Madam, I would like to book a double room for two nights, from Friday. Could you please let me know if a room is available and what the price per night is? Thank you. Kind regards, (your name)"
is "She is best student in our class" correct?
Say: "She is the best student in our class." A superlative like best, tallest or most careful needs "the" before it.
I fixed the chain of my bicycle all by myself today!
Nice work! Fixing things yourself saves money and feels great. Put a few drops of oil on the chain every few weeks, and it will run smoothly for longer.
Make it negative: "He has a car."
"He doesn't have a car." In British English you can also say "He hasn't got a car." Note that "has" becomes "have" after "doesn't".
correct: "My bag is same like yours"
Say: "My bag is the same as yours." The phrase is "the same as". You can also say "My bag is like yours" or "similar to yours."
Our cow gave birth to a calf this morning!

Congratulations! Make sure the calf drinks its mother's first milk, called "bigauti", soon after birth; it protects the calf from illness. Keep them both in a clean, dry shed, and call a vet if the cow or the calf seems weak.
Write a short out-of-office reply. I'm away until Monday.
"Thank you for your email. I am away until Monday and will reply when I am back. Thank you for your patience."
Make a question: "They are playing in the yard."
"Are they playing in the yard?" Move "are" to the front. To ask where: "Where are they playing?"
is "He is one of the best player in the team" right?
Say: "He is one of the best players in the team." After "one of the", the noun is always plural, because he is one among many.
I want to read English newspapers but they are too hard for me.

Start small: read only the headlines and the first paragraph of two or three stories each day. Sports and weather pages use simpler words. Underline five new words, look them up, and use one of them in a sentence that day.
Change to the past: "I eat rice and dal."
"I ate rice and dal." "Eat" is irregular, so its past form is "ate", not "eated".
Write a short review for a restaurant. The momo were great but the service was slow.
"The momo were delicious, juicy and full of flavour. The service was slow, though, so come when you are not in a hurry. I would still go back for the momo."
correct: "I read in class 9"
Say: "I study in Class 9" or "I am in Class 9." "Read" means looking at words in a book; it does not mean studying in a class. In Nepali, "padhchhu" covers both.
I lost my wallet on the bus today. What should I do first?

Call the bus office or the number on your ticket and ask them to check the bus. If your bank card was in it, call the bank to block it at once. For a lost citizenship card or license, report it at the nearest police office so you can get a new one.
Change into the future: "She goes to Dharan."
"She will go to Dharan." You can also say "She is going to go to Dharan" if it is already a plan.
correct: "I will reach to home at six"
Say: "I will reach home at six." "Reach" does not take "to". We say reach home, reach school, reach Kathmandu.
Write a message to the courier company asking where my parcel is. Tracking number is 45821.
"Hello, I am waiting for a parcel with tracking number 45821. Could you please tell me where it is now and when it will be delivered? Thank you."
Put the words in order: to / going / I / am / Ilam / tomorrow
"I am going to Ilam tomorrow." English order is usually subject, then verb, then place, then time.
My phone fell in water!

Take it out and switch it off at once; do not try to charge it. Wipe it dry, take out the SIM tray and the cover, and leave it in a dry, airy place for a day or two. If it still does not work, take it to a repair shop.
correct: "Today is holiday"
Say: "Today is a holiday." "Holiday" is a countable noun, so it needs "a". You can also say "We have a holiday today."
Join with "who": "I met a man. He sells honey."
"I met a man who sells honey." "Who" joins the two sentences and stands for "he", the man.
Write a message to my teacher asking for a recommendation letter for a scholarship.
"Dear Sir/Madam, I am applying for a scholarship, and I need a letter of recommendation. Would you be kind enough to write one for me? I can send you any details you need. Thank you very much."
correct: "What is the time in your watch?"
Say: "What time is it by your watch?" or "What time does your watch say?" In daily talk, just "What time is it?" is fine.
My father retired from the post office today.
That is a big day for him and the whole family. Thank him for all those years of hard work. Now he has time for things he enjoys; ask him what he wants to do first, and help him start a new routine.
Join with "so": "It was raining. We stayed inside."
"It was raining, so we stayed inside." "So" shows the result. Put a comma before it.
correct: "Almost students passed the exam"
Say: "Almost all the students passed the exam" or "Most students passed the exam." "Almost" cannot come straight before a noun; it needs "all" after it.
Write a message to a plumber asking him to come tomorrow morning to fix the bathroom pipe.
"Namaste dai, the pipe in our bathroom is broken and leaking. Could you please come tomorrow morning to fix it? Please let me know what time you can come. Thank you."
Fill in: "She has ___ (write) three letters."
"She has written three letters." After "has" or "have", use the past participle: write, wrote, written.
I keep forgetting the new English words I learn.

Use each new word in your own sentence on the same day. Look at your list again the next day, then after three days, then after a week. A small notebook or word cards in your pocket help you review on the bus.
Which is right: "This book is my" or "This book is mine"?
"This book is mine." When no noun follows, use mine, yours, his, hers, ours and theirs. With a noun: "This is my book."
someone at work told me "I am not getting you". what does it mean?
It means "I don't understand what you are saying." It is common in South Asian English. In standard English, people say "Sorry, I don't follow" or "Could you explain that again?"
Help me write a note for the delivery person: leave the parcel with the shop downstairs.
"Dear delivery person, if I am not home, please leave my parcel with the shop downstairs. Thank you!"
Join: "It was very cold. We could not go out." Use "so ... that".
"It was so cold that we could not go out." Put the adjective after "so", and the result after "that".
My best friend did not invite me to her birthday party. I feel hurt.

That hurts, and your feeling is real. There may be a reason you don't know, like a small family-only party. When you feel calm, ask her gently: "I felt a bit left out. Was it a small party?" One talk is better than guessing.
what does "not only ... but also" mean? give an example
It means "this and also that", with extra force. Example: "She not only cooked dinner but also cleaned the kitchen." It shows that the second thing is a surprise or an addition.
is "Where do you stay?" correct for asking where someone lives?
In South Asian English it means "Where do you live?", but elsewhere "stay" means a short time, like a hotel. To ask about someone's home, say "Where do you live?"
Write a message to my boss saying I made a mistake in the report I sent yesterday, and I have fixed it.
"Dear Sir/Madam, I found a mistake in the report I sent yesterday. I have corrected it, and the new version is attached. I am sorry for the trouble."
what does "in case" mean? Like "Take an umbrella in case it rains."
"In case" means "because it might happen". "Take an umbrella in case it rains" means take it now, because rain is possible. It is different from "if": you take the umbrella either way.
I'm scared of speaking English on the phone.

That is very common, because you cannot see the other person's face. Write two or three lines before you call, speak a little slower than usual, and it is fine to say "Sorry, could you repeat that?" Each call gets easier.
correct: "This word has been in use since long"
Say: "This word has been in use for a long time." "Since" needs a starting point, like "since 2010". For a length of time, use "for".
Use "as long as" in a sentence
"You can borrow my bike as long as you bring it back by evening." "As long as" means "only if" a condition is kept.
Write a message to welcome a new member to our office team. Her name is Sushma.
"Welcome to the team, Sushma! We are very happy to have you with us. If you need anything as you settle in, please ask any of us."
"until" and "till" - are they the same?
Yes, they mean the same: "Wait until six" and "Wait till six." "Till" is a little more informal. "Til" with one l is not standard; avoid it in school writing.
I learned to swim this summer!
That's a great skill to have! Keep practising in safe places, and always swim with someone nearby. Rivers can look calm but have strong currents, so be extra careful there.
Change to reported speech: "I will call you," she said.
"She said that she would call me." In reported speech, "will" usually becomes "would", and "I" and "you" change to fit the person speaking.
correct: "I met him five years back"
Say: "I met him five years ago." "Ago" is the standard word for time counted back from now. "Back" is common in South Asian English but sounds informal elsewhere.
How do I reply to an email that offers me a job? I want to accept.

"Dear (name), thank you very much for offering me the position of (job title). I am happy to accept the offer. Please let me know the next steps and the documents I should bring. Kind regards, (your name)"
what's the difference between "during" and "while"?
"During" is followed by a noun: "during the meeting", "during Dashain". "While" is followed by a subject and a verb: "while we were eating". Both talk about a time when something happens.
Can I learn English at 45?

Yes, of course. Adults learn well because they are focused and know why they want to learn. Practise a little every day: listen to simple English, read short texts and speak out loud. Steady practice matters more than age.
correct: "The meeting is postponed because the boss is out of station"
Say: "The meeting is postponed because the boss is out of town" or "is travelling". "Out of station" is South Asian English; other speakers will not understand it.
Fill in "in" or "into": "The boy jumped ___ the river."
"The boy jumped into the river." "Into" shows movement from outside to inside. "In" shows where something already is: "He is swimming in the river."
Make this message friendlier: "Come at 5. Don't be late."
"See you at 5! Please try to be on time, as we have a lot to do."
"all" or "whole"? "I ate the ___ cake."
"I ate the whole cake." "Whole" comes after "the": the whole day, the whole class. "All" comes before "the": "I ate all the cake." Both mean every part.
correct: "We have to do updation of the records"
Say: "We have to update the records." "Updation" is not standard English. Use the verb "update", or the noun "an update": "The records need an update."
I donated blood for the first time today!
That is a kind and brave thing to do. Drink plenty of water today, eat a good meal, and avoid heavy lifting or hard exercise for the rest of the day. Your blood may help save someone's life.
Use "both ... and" in a sentence about my family. My brother and sister live in Pokhara.
"Both my brother and my sister live in Pokhara." With "both ... and", the verb is plural, because it talks about two people.
correct: "I want to order for food"
Say: "I want to order food" or "I would like to order, please." "Order" takes the food directly, without "for". But you can order food "for" someone: "I ordered momo for my sister."
Fill in with a, an or nothing: "She is ___ honest girl. I like ___ milk."
"She is an honest girl. I like milk." "Honest" starts with a vowel sound, so "an". "Milk" in general takes no article.
Write a polite message to remind my friend about the 2000 rupees he borrowed.
"Hi! Hope you are well. Just a small reminder about the 2000 rupees I lent you. Could you return it when you can, maybe this week? Thanks a lot."
correct: "Do one thing, call him now"
In standard English, say: "Here is an idea: call him now" or simply "Why don't you call him now?" "Do one thing" is common in South Asian English but sounds strange to others.
what is a "zebra crossing"?

A zebra crossing is a place on the road painted with wide white stripes, where people walk across. Vehicles should stop and let people cross there. The name comes from the black and white stripes of a zebra.
what does "a penny for your thoughts" mean?
It is a gentle way to ask someone who looks quiet or lost in thought, "What are you thinking about?"
how do you pronounce "February"?
Many people say FEB-roo-air-ee or FEB-yoo-air-ee. Both are accepted. The first "r" is often softened, which is why the word is tricky.
"jhyau lagyo" lai english ma kasari bhanne?
It depends on the feeling. For boredom: "I'm bored." For being tired of something that keeps happening: "I'm fed up with this." For something annoying: "This is so annoying."
what does "detour" mean?
A detour is a longer route you take because the usual road is closed or blocked. Example: "The bridge was being repaired, so the bus took a detour through the village."
what is the difference between "upset" and "angry"?
"Angry" is a strong, hot feeling against someone or something. "Upset" is softer: you feel sad, hurt or worried. A child can be upset when a toy breaks without being angry at anyone.
what does "the apple of my eye" mean?
It means the person you love and care about the most. Example: "My little granddaughter is the apple of my eye."
how to pronounce "library"?
Say LIE-brer-ee, with three parts. Do not drop the first "r": it is not "lie-berry".
what does "overtake" mean on the road?
To overtake is to go past a slower vehicle moving in the same direction. Example: "Never overtake on a sharp bend."
what's the difference between "disappointed" and "sad"?
"Disappointed" means sad because something did not happen the way you hoped: "I was disappointed with my marks." "Sad" is wider: you can be sad without expecting anything.
what does "cry wolf" mean?
It means to keep raising a false alarm, so people stop believing you even when the danger is real. It comes from the story of the shepherd boy who shouted "Wolf!" as a joke.
"dhilo bhayo" office ma english ma kasari bhanne?
Say: "Sorry, I'm late." If you are still on the way: "I'm running a little late. I'll be there in ten minutes." If it is about work: "Sorry for the delay."
how do you say "sugar"? is it "su-gar"?
It sounds like SHOO-ger. The "s" in "sugar" and "sure" makes a "sh" sound.
what is a "junction"?
A junction is a place where two or more roads meet. Example: "Turn right at the next junction." In Nepali, "chok" or "dobato" for where two roads meet.
what does "thrilled" mean?
"Thrilled" means extremely happy and excited: "She was thrilled to get the job." It is stronger than "happy".
what does "in hot water" mean?
It means in trouble. Example: "He will be in hot water if his father sees the broken window."
why is the b silent in "debt" and "climb"?
Many English words keep an old spelling with a silent b: debt (det), doubt (dowt), climb (klime), thumb (thum), comb (kohm). After "m" at the end of a word, the b is usually silent.
what's the meaning of "talkative"?
A talkative person likes to talk a lot: "My talkative neighbour tells me all the news of the tole." It is a gentle word. "Chatterbox" is a friendly, informal word for such a person.
what does "practice makes perfect" mean?
It means doing something again and again is how you become very good at it. Example: "Your writing will improve with every letter you write. Practice makes perfect."
"hajur" ko english k hunchha?

There is no single English word for it. When it means "yes", say "Yes". When it means "Sorry, what did you say?", say "Pardon?" or "Sorry?" When it shows respect, English uses "sir" or "madam", or just a polite tone.
what is a "speed breaker"?
A speed breaker is a raised strip across the road that makes vehicles slow down. In British English it is often called a "speed bump", and in American English also a "speed hump".
explain "introvert" and "extrovert"
An introvert enjoys quiet time and feels tired after a lot of social time. An extrovert gets energy from being with people. Most people are a mix of both.
what does "a storm in a teacup" mean?
It means a lot of anger or worry about a very small matter. Example: "The fight over the TV remote was a storm in a teacup." Americans say "a tempest in a teapot".
how should I say "listen" and "castle"?
The t is silent in both: LIS-en and KAS-ul. The same silent t is in whistle, fasten and often, though some people say the t in often.
what is a shortcut?
A shortcut is a quicker or shorter way to get somewhere: "We took a shortcut through the fields." It is also a quick way to do a task on a computer, like Ctrl+S to save.
what does "easy-going" mean?
An easy-going person is relaxed and does not get upset or angry easily. Example: "Our new teacher is easy-going, but she still wants homework on time."
"khana khanus" bhanda english ma k bhanne?
Just saying "Please eat" sounds a little odd in English. Say "Please help yourself" when the food is on the table, or "Enjoy your meal!" when you serve someone.
what does "let sleeping dogs lie" mean?
It means do not bring up an old problem that is quiet now, because talking about it may cause trouble again. Example: "They have made up after the fight. Let sleeping dogs lie."
what does "deposit" mean at a bank?
To deposit is to put money into your bank account. The opposite is "withdraw", which is to take money out. Example: "I deposited 5000 rupees and withdrew 2000."
what does "bossy" mean?
A bossy person always tells others what to do, even when it is not their job. Example: "My elder cousin is bossy when we play." It is not a polite word to use about someone in front of them.
how to pronounce "chocolate"?
Most people say CHOK-lit, in two parts. The middle "o" is usually not pronounced.
what does "no pain, no gain" mean?
It means you have to work hard, or go through something difficult, to get good results. People say it about exercise, study and saving money.
What is my "account balance"?
Your account balance is how much money is in your bank account right now. You can check it at an ATM, in the bank's app, or by asking at the bank.

Say: "I will definitely come" or "I'll be there for sure." For a stronger promise: "I promise I'll come." In casual talk: "Count on me!"
what does "nosy" mean?
A nosy person is too interested in other people's private matters. Example: "Our nosy neighbour always asks how much my rent is." It is not a polite word.
what does "where there's a will, there's a way" mean?
It means if you really want to do something, you will find a way to do it. Example: "She studied by a candle during power cuts and passed with good marks. Where there's a will, there's a way."
I say "pan" when I mean "fan". How do I fix it?

For "f", touch your top teeth gently to your lower lip and blow air through: fan, fish, coffee. For "p", close both lips and open them with a small puff: pan, pin, copy. Practise pairs: fan and pan, fine and pine.
what's the difference between "income" and "expense"?
Income is the money you get, like salary or sales. An expense is money you spend, like rent, food or school fees. If your income is more than your expenses, you can save.
what does "two heads are better than one" mean?
It means two people thinking together can solve a problem better than one person alone. Example: "Let's do this maths problem together. Two heads are better than one."
what does "content" mean as a feeling?

As an adjective, "content" (kun-TENT) means happy and satisfied with what you have: "My grandmother is content with her small garden." As a noun, "content" (KON-tent) means what is inside something, like the content of a book.
how do I say "temperature"?
Most people say TEM-pruh-cher, in three parts. The "a" in the middle is often not pronounced in fast speech.
what is a "debt"?
A debt is money you owe to someone and must pay back. Example: "He worked abroad to pay off his debt." Say it "det"; the b is silent. In Nepali: "rin".
what does "look before you leap" mean?
It means think carefully about the results before you do something. Example: "Before you quit your job, look before you leap: do you have another one ready?"
how should I describe my pain to a doctor in English?

Say where it hurts, what kind of pain it is and how long you have had it. Useful words: "sharp" (sudden and strong), "dull" (a steady ache), "throbbing" (beating like a pulse) and "burning". Example: "I have a dull pain in my lower back for four days."
what does "don't count your chickens before they hatch" mean?
It means do not be too sure of a good result before it really happens. Example: "You have not got the visa yet, so don't count your chickens before they hatch."

Say: "I'll get going now" or "I should get going." With friends: "See you!" or "Bye for now!" "Let's go" is used only when everyone is leaving together.
how do I say "Thursday" correctly?
Say THURZ-day. Put your tongue lightly between your teeth for the "th", and blow air. It is different from "Tuesday", which starts with a "t" sound: TYOOZ-day.
what words describe taste in English?
Sweet (like honey), sour (like lemon), salty (like chips), bitter (like karela) and spicy (like chilli). "Tangy" means pleasantly sour, like a good tomato achar.
what does "it's raining cats and dogs" mean?
It means it is raining very heavily. It is an old, informal phrase, and it has nothing to do with real cats or dogs. Today people often just say "It's pouring."
what is a "queue"?
A queue is a line of people waiting for their turn, for example at a bank or a ticket counter. "Please join the queue." Americans say "line". It sounds like the letter "Q".
what does "a fish out of water" mean?
It means someone who feels uncomfortable because they are in a new or strange place. Example: "On my first day in the city office, I felt like a fish out of water."

Say: "How are you?" To an elder or in a formal setting: "How are you keeping?" or "I hope you are well." With friends: "How's it going?"
what is the difference between "pull" and "pool" in sound?
"Pull" has a short vowel, the same as in "book". "Pool" has a long "oo", the same as in "food". Keep "pull" short and stretch "pool". The same goes for "full" and "fool".
what is a "voucher"?
A voucher is a printed or digital paper that you can use instead of money, or to get a discount. Example: "With this voucher you get 200 rupees off your next meal."
what does "the tip of the iceberg" mean?
It means only a small part of a much bigger problem can be seen. Example: "The broken roof was just the tip of the iceberg; the whole house needed repair."
what does "outgoing" mean?
An outgoing person is friendly and enjoys meeting and talking to new people. Example: "Being outgoing helped her make friends quickly in college."
What does "don't put all your eggs in one basket" mean?
It means do not depend on only one plan or one thing, because if it fails you lose everything. Example: "Apply to more than one college; don't put all your eggs in one basket."
