Make the "s" sound, like a snake, and then add your voice so it buzzes: zzz. Your throat should feel a small buzz. Practise: zoo, zero, zip. Do not let your tongue touch the roof of your mouth like for "j".
what is a "quotation" in business?
A quotation is a written price that a shop or worker gives before doing a job or selling something. Example: "Get quotations from three carpenters before you choose one." People also say "a quote".
what does "the best of both worlds" mean?
It means enjoying the good parts of two different things at the same time. Example: "Living in Dhulikhel gives me the best of both worlds: fresh air and a short drive to the city."
what does "appetite" mean?
Appetite is the wish to eat: "After the long walk, I had a big appetite." If a sick person "has no appetite", they do not feel like eating. In Nepali: "ruchi" or "khana man lagne".
what's the meaning of "go the extra mile"?
It means to do more than what is expected. Example: "The nurse went the extra mile and called to check on my mother after she went home."
"live" and "leave" - how to say them differently?
"Live" has a short "i", like in "sit": liv. "Leave" has a long "ee", like in "see": leev. Stretch the sound for "leave". The same goes for "fill" and "feel", "ship" and "sheep".
what is a "souvenir"?
A souvenir is a small thing you buy or keep to remember a place or a trip. Example: "I bought a small khukuri as a souvenir from Dharan."
what does "get the ball rolling" mean?
It means to start something, so that others can join in. Example: "Let me get the ball rolling: I will share my idea first."
what's the difference between "walk" and "work" when I say them?
"Walk" has no "l" sound and sounds like "wawk", with an open "aw". "Work" has an "er" sound, like "wurk". Say "I walk to work" slowly, and feel your mouth change.

messages.content: what are "besi" and "taar"?

"Besi" is low, warm land in a valley, beside a river, often good for rice. "Taar" is raised flat land above a river, usually drier. In English, besi is a valley floor and taar is a river terrace or plateau.
"To make lemon tea: boil one cup of water, add half a spoon of tea leaves and wait two minutes. Then add lemon juice and honey." How long do you wait after adding the tea leaves?
You wait two minutes.
messages.think: The recipe says "add half a spoon of tea leaves and wait two minutes".

messages.content: 1 liter of oil costs 290 rupees, and a 5-liter can costs 1400 rupees. Which is cheaper per liter?
The 5-liter can is cheaper: 280 rupees per liter, against 290.
messages.think: 5-liter can: 1400 / 5 = 280 per liter. 280 is less than 290.

messages.content: How do I answer "What are your salary expectations?" in an interview?
Find out the usual pay for this kind of job first. Then say: "Based on my skills and the role, I am looking for around (amount), but I am open to discussion." Giving a range is also fine.
"To make lemon tea: boil one cup of water, add half a spoon of tea leaves and wait two minutes. Then add lemon juice and honey." What do you add after waiting?
After waiting, you add lemon juice and honey.
messages.think: The recipe says "Then add lemon juice and honey."

messages.content: How much will I pay for 5 kg of sugar and 2 kg of lentils?
I need the prices to work this out. Tell me the price of 1 kg of sugar and 1 kg of lentils, and I will add it up for you.
"To make lemon tea: boil one cup of water, add half a spoon of tea leaves and wait two minutes. Then add lemon juice and honey." Do I add milk?
No. The recipe does not use milk; it uses water, tea leaves, lemon juice and honey.
messages.think: The recipe lists water, tea leaves, lemon juice and honey. It does not mention milk.

messages.content: what does "pareli" mean in English?
"Pareli" means eyelashes: the small hairs on the edge of your eyelids. The line of hair above the eye is the eyebrow, "aankhibhau" in Nepali.
A stationery shop with 3 workers sells 45 pens a day at 20 rupees each. How much does it earn from pens in a day?
It earns 900 rupees a day from pens.
messages.think: The number of workers is not needed. 45 x 20 = 900.

messages.content: How do I fill in a bank deposit slip?

Write the date, the account number, the account holder's name and the amount, both in figures (5000) and in words (five thousand rupees). Sign it, and check the account number twice before you hand it in.
Out of 30 momo, Ram ate 2/5. How many are left?
18 momo are left.
A school had 160 students last year and 208 this year. By what percent did the number grow?
The number of students grew by 30%.
I'm going back to my village after three years. I'm so excited!

Three years is a long time, so this will be a happy trip! Take a little time to visit the elders and old friends, and walk around the places you remember. You may notice many changes, both big and small.
Explain this in simple English: "The meeting has been deferred until further notice."
It means the meeting has been moved to a later time, and no new date has been fixed yet. They will tell you the new date later. In Nepali: "baithak arko suchana nabhaye samma sarieko chha."
what is the difference between "There is" and "It is"?

"There is" says that something exists or is somewhere: "There is a shop near my house." "It is" describes something already known: "It is a small shop." So: "There is a new cafe in town. It is very busy."
I'm teaching English to small kids in my village on Saturdays.
That's a wonderful thing to do! With small kids, use songs, pictures and games; they learn best when they are having fun. Keep each activity short, about ten minutes, and praise every small step.
what does "Applicants must submit the form in person" mean?
It means you have to go yourself and hand in the form. You cannot send it by post, by email or through another person.
Fill in "there is" or "there are": "___ two banks and ___ a post office on this road."
"There are two banks and there is a post office on this road." Use "there are" with plural nouns and "there is" with a single noun.
My friend is always late when we meet. How do I tell her without fighting?

Talk when you are both calm, not while you are waiting angrily: "I really like meeting you, but waiting a long time is hard for me. Can we try to be on time?" You could also suggest meeting at a place where waiting is easy, like a tea shop.
yo notice ko meaning bhanidinus: "Water supply will be interrupted from 10 am to 4 pm due to maintenance work."

It means there will be no tap water from 10 am to 4 pm because the pipes or the system are being repaired. Store some water before 10 am. In Nepali: "marmat ko kaam le garda 10 baje dekhi 4 baje samma pani aaudaina."
"She gave me a book." Which is the direct object and which is the indirect object?
"A book" is the direct object: it is the thing given. "Me" is the indirect object: the person who receives it. You can also say it as "She gave a book to me."
I got a 3.6 GPA in SEE!
Congratulations! That is a strong result, and it shows a lot of steady work. Enjoy the moment with your family, and then you can start thinking about which subjects you want to study next.
Make this simpler: "Kindly ensure that all electronic devices are switched off."
"Please switch off all phones and other devices."
Fill in the question words: "___ is your name? ___ do you live? ___ old are you?"
"What is your name? Where do you live? How old are you?" What asks about things, where asks about places, and how old asks about age.
My grandmother wants to learn to use a smartphone. How do I teach her?

Teach one thing at a time, starting with what she wants most, like video calls with family. Make the text bigger in the settings, and write the steps on a paper in big letters. Let her press the buttons herself, and be patient when she asks again.
what does "BRB" mean in chat?

"BRB" means "be right back". People write it when they leave the chat for a short time. Other common ones: "TTYL" means "talk to you later", and "IDK" means "I don't know." Use them only in casual chat, not in emails.
"at night" or "in the night"?
"At night" is the usual phrase for night in general: "I study at night." "In the night" is for something that happened at a point during one particular night: "The baby woke up twice in the night."
How can I feel more confident talking to my boss?

Prepare before you go: write your main point in one or two lines. Start with the most important thing, speak slowly and look at the person. Remember that your boss is just a person with a job, like you; being clear is more important than being perfect.
what does "I'm on my way" mean?
It means "I have already left and I am coming now." Example: "Don't worry, I'm on my way. I'll be there in ten minutes."
correct: "He learned me English"
Say: "He taught me English." To teach is to give knowledge; to learn is to get it. So: "He taught me English, and I learned it from him."
My father does not let me go on a trip with my friends.

That is frustrating, but he is probably worried about your safety. Talk to him calmly: share where you will go, who is going, how you will travel and when you will be back. Offer to call him at fixed times. Showing that you have a plan builds trust.
Help me write an SMS to my mother that I will be late for dinner.
"Aama, I will be a little late for dinner tonight. Please don't wait for me to eat. I'll message you when I am on my way."
"We won the other team" - right?
Say: "We beat the other team." You win a game, a match or a prize: "We won the match." You beat a person or a team: "We beat them 3-1."
correct: "I lost the bus this morning"
Say: "I missed the bus this morning." You miss a bus, a train or a class when you are too late for it. You lose something when you cannot find it: "I lost my umbrella."
I'm going to Janakpur for Chhath this year!
How exciting! Chhath in Janakpur is beautiful, with families gathered at the ponds and rivers at sunset and sunrise. The ghats get very crowded, so go early, and keep your phone and bag safe.
Write a message to tell my friend I reached home safely.
"Hi! I reached home safely. Thank you for a lovely day. Talk soon!"
"Ram and Sita's house" or "Ram's and Sita's house"?
If they share one house, put 's only on the last name: "Ram and Sita's house." If each has their own, put 's on both: "Ram's and Sita's houses."
what is the difference between "sensible" and "sensitive"?

"Sensible" means wise and practical: "a sensible decision". "Sensitive" means easily affected or hurt, or quick to notice feelings: "sensitive skin", "a sensitive child". They look similar but mean different things.
How can I help my parents more at home?

Notice the jobs they do every day and quietly take one, like washing the dishes after dinner or buying vegetables. Doing it without being asked means a lot. Ask them once a week, "What can I take care of this week?"
"price" or "prize"? I won first ___ in the quiz.
"I won first prize in the quiz." A prize is something you win. A price is how much something costs: "The price of rice went up."
is "Respected Sir" okay to start a letter?
It is common in South Asia, and many teachers in Nepal still use it. In international English, "Dear Sir" or "Dear Mr. Shrestha" is the standard opening. For job applications abroad, use "Dear".
"diary" or "dairy"?
A diary (DIE-uh-ree) is a book where you write about your days. A dairy (DAIR-ee) is a place for milk and milk products: "We buy milk from the dairy." Watch the order of the letters "i" and "a".
Write a message to cancel today's tuition class because we have a family function.
"Namaste sir/madam, I am sorry, I cannot come to tuition today because we have a family function at home. I will catch up on what I miss. Thank you for understanding."
"Please seat" or "Please sit"?
"Please sit down" or, more formally, "Please be seated." "Seat" is a noun or a verb that means to give someone a seat, so "Please seat" is wrong on its own.
My best friend is moving abroad. How can I say goodbye in a special way?

Give something personal: a photo album, a letter about your best memories together, or a small thing from home they can carry. Spend a simple last day doing what you two always loved. Promise a regular call, and keep the promise.
what is the difference between "historic" and "historical"?
"Historic" means very important in history: "a historic day for the country." "Historical" means about or from the past: "a historical film", "historical records."
How do I write 45 in words? Is it "fourty-five"?
It is "forty-five". "Four" has a "u", but "forty" does not. Use a hyphen for numbers from 21 to 99: twenty-one, forty-five, ninety-nine.
Reply to a customer who says the bottle she bought from my shop was broken.
"I am very sorry that the bottle was broken. Please bring it to the shop with the bill, and we will give you a new one or your money back. Thank you for letting us know."
"lose" or "loss"? "I don't want to ___ my job."
"I don't want to lose my job." "Lose" is the verb. "Loss" is the noun: "The loss of his job was hard for the family."
what is the difference between "shade" and "shadow"?
Shade is a cool area away from the sun: "Let's sit in the shade of the tree." A shadow is the dark shape something makes when it blocks light: "My shadow is long in the evening."
what does "won't" stand for?
"Won't" is short for "will not": "I won't be late." Some others: "can't" is "cannot", "shan't" is "shall not", and "didn't" is "did not".
Write a note to stick on the fridge: please don't eat the cake, it is for Didi's party.
"Please do not eat the cake! It is for Didi's party. Thank you!"
is it "the tallest in the class" or "the tallest of the class"?
"The tallest in the class." Use "in" with a place or a group: in the class, in the village, in the team. Use "of" with a number of people: "the tallest of the three brothers."
My sister says I'm too sensitive. What does she mean?
She probably means you get hurt or upset easily by small things others say. Being sensitive also has a good side: you notice how other people feel. You can ask her calmly what made her say it.
how to spell "grammar" and "calendar"? I always write "grammer" and "calender".
Both end in "ar": grammar, calendar. A trick: "grammar" has two a's around "mm" and the word "calendar" has the same ending as "dollar".
what is an auxiliary verb?

An auxiliary verb is a helping verb that comes with the main verb to make tenses, questions and negatives: be, have and do, plus modals like can and will. In "She is reading" and "Do you know?", "is" and "do" are auxiliary verbs.
"Ill" and "sick" - same?
Mostly yes: both mean not well. "Sick" is more common in American English and in daily talk. In British English, "sick" can also mean throwing up: "I was sick on the bus" means you vomited.
how to spell "government" and "environment"?
Both have an "n" before "ment" that is often not heard: gover-N-ment, enviro-N-ment. Say them slowly in parts when you write: gov-ern-ment, en-vi-ron-ment.
correct: "I have bought two CD's"
Say: "I have bought two CDs." To make a short form plural, just add "s" with no apostrophe: CDs, ATMs, PDFs. The apostrophe is for owning or for missing letters.
"personal" or "personnel"?
"Personal" (PER-sun-ul) means private or about one person: "a personal question". "Personnel" (per-suh-NEL) means the staff of an organisation: "hospital personnel".
how do I spell "beginning" and "business"?
"Beginning" has a double n before "ing": begin-n-ing. "Business" has "i" after "s": bus-i-ness, though the "i" is not pronounced: BIZ-ness.
what does "hospitable" mean?
"Hospitable" means friendly and generous to guests. Example: "The villagers were very hospitable; they gave us tea and a place to sleep." The noun is "hospitality". In Nepali: "atithi satkar garne".
what does "turn down" mean?
"Turn down" has two common meanings. It can mean to refuse an offer: "She turned down the job in Dubai." It can also mean to lower the sound: "Please turn down the TV."
how do I pronounce "pronunciation"? I always say "pronounciation".
The noun is pro-NUN-see-ay-shun, with "nun" in the middle, not "noun". The spelling drops the "o" too: pronunciation. Only the verb "pronounce" has "noun" in it.
what does "every dog has its day" mean?
It means everyone gets a moment of success at some time. Example: "He lost every race last year, but this year he came first. Every dog has its day."
what's the opposite of "arrive"?
"Depart" or "leave". Example: "The bus departs at 6 and arrives at 11." "Depart" is used on timetables; "leave" is used in daily talk.
what does "stingy" mean?
"Stingy" means not willing to spend or share money, even when it is needed. Example: "He is too stingy to buy his own tea." It is not a polite word. A kinder word for careful spending is "thrifty".
meaning of "carry on"?
"Carry on" means to continue: "Carry on with your work; I'll wait." It can also mean to keep doing something after a break: "After the rain stopped, the match carried on."
why does "women" sound like "wimmin"?
Because the "o" in "women" is said like a short "i": WIM-in. The singular "woman" sounds as it looks: WUM-an. It is an old spelling that never changed.
what does "out of sight, out of mind" mean?
It means we soon forget people or things we do not see often. Example: "I put the bills in a drawer and forgot to pay them. Out of sight, out of mind!"
what is the opposite of "asleep"?
"Awake". Example: "The baby is asleep, but his sister is still awake." Both words come after the verb: we say "the baby is asleep", not "the asleep baby".
what does "awkward" mean?
"Awkward" means uncomfortable or embarrassing, or hard to handle. Example: "There was an awkward silence after his joke." It can also mean clumsy: "an awkward way of holding a pen."
what does "set off" mean?
"Set off" means to start a journey: "We set off for Gorkha at five in the morning." It can also mean to make something start, like an alarm: "The smoke set off the fire alarm."
how do you say "says" and "said"?
"Says" sounds like "sez" and "said" sounds like "sed". Both are short. Only "say" has the long "ay" sound.
what does "a picture is worth a thousand words" mean?
It means a picture can show something more clearly than a long description. Example: "Instead of explaining the damage, just send a photo. A picture is worth a thousand words."
what's the opposite of "smooth"?
"Rough". Example: "The new road is smooth, but the old one is rough and full of holes." For hair or skin, the opposite can also be "dry" or "coarse".
what does "naughty" mean?
"Naughty" is used for children who behave badly or do not obey, often in a playful way: "The naughty boy hid his sister's shoes." In Nepali we often call such a child "badmas".
what does "come across" mean?
"Come across" means to find or meet by chance: "I came across an old photo of my parents while cleaning." It can also mean to seem: "He comes across as shy, but he is very friendly."
how do I say "busy"? I read it as "bushy".
Say BIZ-ee. The "u" sounds like a short "i", and the "s" sounds like "z". The noun "business" starts the same way: BIZ-ness.
what does "honesty is the best policy" mean?
It means telling the truth is always the best choice, even when it is hard. Example: "He told the shopkeeper she gave him too much change. Honesty is the best policy."
what does "sturdy" mean?
"Sturdy" means strong and well made, not easy to break: "a sturdy table", "sturdy shoes for the trek." For people, it means strong and healthy-looking.
what does "look up" mean? my teacher said "look it up"

"Look it up" means find the information in a dictionary, a book or online. Example: "If you don't know a word, look it up in the dictionary." "Look up" also means to raise your eyes: "Look up at the sky."
what's the opposite of "tight"?
"Loose". Example: "These shoes are too tight; I need a bigger size." "My old shirt is loose now." Careful: "loose" has two o's, "lose" (to not find) has one.
what does "slow and steady wins the race" mean?

It means working at a steady pace, without giving up, brings better results than rushing. It comes from the story of the hare and the tortoise. Example: "Study one chapter a day. Slow and steady wins the race."
what does "handy" mean?
"Handy" means useful and easy to use: "A torch is handy during power cuts." It can also mean near and easy to reach: "Keep your ID handy at the airport."
what does "get along with" mean?
It means to have a friendly relationship with someone: "I get along well with my roommate." The opposite is "not get along": "My cousins don't get along."
how to pronounce "recipe"? is it "re-sipe"?
Say RES-uh-pee, in three parts. The final "e" is pronounced like "ee". It does not rhyme with "pipe".
what does "don't judge a book by its cover" mean?
It means do not decide what someone or something is like only from how it looks. Example: "The tea shop looks old, but the tea is the best in town. Don't judge a book by its cover."
what does "fussy" mean?
A fussy person is hard to please and cares too much about small details, especially about food or clothes. Example: "My little brother is a fussy eater; he picks out every onion."
what does "take after" mean?
It means to look or behave like an older family member: "She takes after her grandmother; they both love singing." It is used for family resemblance, not for friends.
why is the l silent in "half" and "calm"?
In many common words the "l" is not pronounced: half (hahf), calf, calm (kahm), palm, walk, talk. The spelling stayed from an older form of English.
what does "better safe than sorry" mean?
It means it is wiser to be careful now than to be sorry later. Example: "The sky looks dark. Take the umbrella; better safe than sorry."
what does "cosy" mean?
"Cosy" means warm, comfortable and pleasant: "a cosy room with a heater on a winter night." American spelling is "cozy".
what does "call off" mean?
"Call off" means to cancel something that was planned: "The picnic was called off because of the rain." It is used for events, meetings, matches and plans.
"could", "would", "should" - do I say the l?
No. The l is silent in all three: kud, wud, shud. They rhyme with "good".
what does "all that glitters is not gold" mean?
It means something that looks attractive is not always valuable or good. Example: "That job promises a lot of money very fast, but all that glitters is not gold. Check it carefully."
what does "gloomy" mean?
"Gloomy" means dark and sad. It describes weather: "a gloomy, cloudy day", or a mood: "He looked gloomy after the result." The opposite is "bright" or "cheerful".
what does "break down" mean for a vehicle?
It means the vehicle stops working because of a problem: "Our bus broke down near Mugling, so we waited two hours." For a person, "break down" means to start crying because of strong feelings.
how do you say "breakfast"? I say "break-fast".
Most people say BREK-fust, in two short parts. The "ea" sounds like "e" in "bed", not like the word "break".
what does "when in Rome, do as the Romans do" mean?
It means when you are in a new place, follow the customs of the people there. Example: "In Nepali homes, guests take off their shoes at the door. When in Rome, do as the Romans do."
what does "rusty" mean?
"Rusty" means covered with rust, the red-brown layer that forms on old iron: "a rusty gate". It also means out of practice: "My English is a bit rusty; I haven't spoken it for years."
what does "hand in" mean?
"Hand in" means to give your work to a teacher or someone in charge: "Hand in your homework by Friday." It is the same as "submit", but less formal.
what does "make hay while the sun shines" mean?

It means use a good chance while it lasts, because it may not come again. It comes from farming: hay must be cut and dried on sunny days. Example: "Tourist season is short, so the hotels make hay while the sun shines."
what does "faded" mean?
"Faded" means the colour has become lighter and weaker, often from the sun or washing: "a faded blue shirt". It can also mean a memory that is not clear anymore: "a faded memory".
Use "hardly" in a sentence
"I could hardly hear him because the bus was so noisy." "Hardly" means almost not. It already has a negative meaning, so do not use "not" with it.
what does "a friend in need is a friend indeed" mean?
It means a true friend is the one who helps you when you are in trouble. Example: "When I was sick, Suman brought my notes every day. A friend in need is a friend indeed."
what does "spotless" mean?
"Spotless" means completely clean, with no marks or dirt at all: "Her kitchen is always spotless."
Use "even though" in a sentence
"Even though it was raining, the farmers kept planting the rice." "Even though" means "although", but it sounds a little stronger.
what does "too many cooks spoil the broth" mean?
It means when too many people try to control one job, the result is worse. Example: "Five of us tried to plan the party together and nothing got done. Too many cooks spoil the broth."
Use "otherwise" in a sentence
"Wear a jacket; otherwise you will catch a cold." "Otherwise" means "if not". It often comes after a semicolon or at the start of a new sentence.
what does "Rome wasn't built in a day" mean?
It means big things take time and patience to finish. Example: "Your English won't be perfect in one month. Rome wasn't built in a day."
what does "birds of a feather flock together" mean?
It means people who are similar often spend time together. Example: "All the cricket fans in our class sit together. Birds of a feather flock together."
Use "rather than" in a sentence
"I'd like to walk rather than take the bus today." "Rather than" means "instead of", and it shows what you prefer.
what does "money doesn't grow on trees" mean?
It means money is hard to earn, so it should not be wasted. Parents often say it: "We can't buy a new phone every year. Money doesn't grow on trees!"
what does "once bitten, twice shy" mean?
It means after a bad experience, people become more careful about the same thing. Example: "After losing money in that scheme, he checks every offer twice. Once bitten, twice shy."
What does "cheque bounce" mean?

A cheque "bounces" when the bank refuses to pay it, usually because there is not enough money in the account. The person who wrote it may have to pay a fine, so always check your balance before you write a cheque.
"Bhai, I left the house key under the flower pot by the back door. Please feed the dog at 6 and lock the gate. - Didi" Where is the key?
The key is under the flower pot by the back door.
messages.think: The message says "I left the house key under the flower pot by the back door."

messages.content: A pack of 4 soaps costs 220 rupees. How much is one soap?
One soap costs 55 rupees.
what is a "bhakari"?
A bhakari is a big round container woven from bamboo and plastered with mud or cow dung, used to store grain like rice and maize. In English: a grain bin or granary basket.
"Bhai, I left the house key under the flower pot by the back door. Please feed the dog at 6 and lock the gate. - Didi" When should he feed the dog?
He should feed the dog at 6.
messages.think: The message says "Please feed the dog at 6".

messages.content: The lab says I must be "fasting" before my blood test. What does that mean?

It means you should not eat or drink anything except plain water for some hours before the test, often from the night before. Ask the lab exactly how many hours, and whether you can take your usual medicines.
Bus tickets for 3 people cost 1250 rupees each, plus 200 rupees for luggage. What is the total?
The total is 3950 rupees.
"Bhai, I left the house key under the flower pot by the back door. Please feed the dog at 6 and lock the gate. - Didi" Who wrote this message?
Didi, his elder sister, wrote the message.
what are "dhiki" and "jaato"?

A dhiki is a wooden pounder worked with the foot, used to husk rice and pound grain. A jaato is a hand mill made of two round stones; you turn the top stone to grind grain into flour. Many villages now use machines instead.
"Bhai, I left the house key under the flower pot by the back door. Please feed the dog at 6 and lock the gate. - Didi" Where is the dog?
The message does not say where the dog is. It only says to feed the dog at 6 and to lock the gate.
messages.think: The message says to feed the dog at 6, but it does not say where the dog is.

messages.content: The doctor asked me to come for a "follow-up". What is that?
A follow-up is a second visit after your first treatment, so the doctor can check how you are doing and change the treatment if needed. Take your old reports and medicines with you.
A recipe for 4 people uses 300 g of rice. How much rice is needed for 10 people?
750 g of rice is needed for 10 people.
messages.think: one person: 300 / 4 = 75 g. 10 people: 75 x 10 = 750 g.

messages.content: "Kalika Secondary School sports week: football and volleyball on Sunday and Monday, races on Tuesday, prize giving on Wednesday at 2 pm." When is the prize giving?
The prize giving is on Wednesday at 2 pm.
messages.think: The notice says "prize giving on Wednesday at 2 pm".

messages.content: what is a "goth"?
A goth is a shed for cattle or goats. It can also mean a simple shelter in the high pastures where herders stay with their animals in summer. In English: a cattle shed.
"Kalika Secondary School sports week: football and volleyball on Sunday and Monday, races on Tuesday, prize giving on Wednesday at 2 pm." On which day are the races?
The races are on Tuesday.
What is an "attested copy"?

An attested copy is a photocopy of a document that an authorised person has signed and stamped to show it matches the original. Offices and colleges often ask for attested copies of certificates. It is also called a certified copy.
A farmer plants 15 rows of cabbage with 24 plants in each row. 36 plants die. How many are left?
324 cabbage plants are left.
"Kalika Secondary School sports week: football and volleyball on Sunday and Monday, races on Tuesday, prize giving on Wednesday at 2 pm." Which games are on Monday?
Football and volleyball are on Monday.
messages.think: The notice says "football and volleyball on Sunday and Monday".

messages.content: what is a "ghum"?
A ghum is a rain shield made of bamboo strips and leaves, worn over the head and back. Farmers wear it while planting rice in the rain, because it keeps both hands free.
"Kalika Secondary School sports week: football and volleyball on Sunday and Monday, races on Tuesday, prize giving on Wednesday at 2 pm." Are there races on Monday?
No. The races are on Tuesday; Monday has football and volleyball.
messages.think: The notice says "races on Tuesday". Monday has football and volleyball.

messages.content: What should I wear to a job interview?

Wear clean, ironed, simple clothes that are a little formal, like a plain shirt with trousers, or a kurta suruwal or sari. Choose comfortable shoes and keep your hair neat. Dress for the job, but always neat and simple.
I walk 3.6 km at 4.8 km per hour. How many minutes does it take?
It takes 45 minutes.
"Dawa missed the 7 o'clock bus, so he took the 8 o'clock one. Because of a landslide, the bus reached Besisahar two hours late, at 1 pm." Which bus did Dawa take?
Dawa took the 8 o'clock bus.

messages.content: what is a "sukul"?
A sukul is a mat woven from rice straw. People spread it on the floor to sit on, especially in villages and at feasts. In English: a straw mat.
"Dawa missed the 7 o'clock bus, so he took the 8 o'clock one. Because of a landslide, the bus reached Besisahar two hours late, at 1 pm." Which bus did Dawa miss?
Dawa missed the 7 o'clock bus.
messages.think: The text says "Dawa missed the 7 o'clock bus".

messages.content: I have no work experience. Should I say "I am a fresher" in an interview?

"Fresher" is understood in South Asia, but "I am a recent graduate" sounds better everywhere. Then talk about what you do have: projects, an internship, volunteer work or skills you learned in college.
The temperature fell from 14 degrees to -3 degrees. How many degrees did it fall?
The temperature fell by 17 degrees.
messages.think: From 14 down to 0 is 14 degrees, and from 0 down to -3 is 3 more. 14 + 3 = 17.

messages.content: "Dawa missed the 7 o'clock bus, so he took the 8 o'clock one. Because of a landslide, the bus reached Besisahar two hours late, at 1 pm." Why was the bus late?
The bus was late because of a landslide.
messages.think: The text says "Because of a landslide, the bus reached Besisahar two hours late".

messages.content: what does "ukhan" mean?

An "ukhan" is a proverb: a short, old saying with a lesson, like "Ek thuki suki, saya thuki nadi": one drop of spit dries up, but a hundred make a river, meaning many people working together can do big things. In Nepali the phrase "ukhan tukka" means proverbs and sayings.
"Dawa missed the 7 o'clock bus, so he took the 8 o'clock one. Because of a landslide, the bus reached Besisahar two hours late, at 1 pm." At what time should the bus have reached Besisahar?
Without the delay, the bus should have reached Besisahar at 11 am.
messages.think: It reached at 1 pm, and that was two hours late. Two hours before 1 pm is 11 am.

messages.content: How do I ask a shop if they deliver?
"Do you deliver to (your area)?" Then: "Is there a delivery charge?" and "How long does it take?" If they say yes, give your address with a landmark and your phone number.
There is 13% VAT on a bill of 2500 rupees. What is the total with VAT?
The total with VAT is 2825 rupees.
"Stationery shop: notebook 60 rupees, pen 20 rupees, eraser 10 rupees, geometry box 250 rupees." Which item is the cheapest?
The eraser is the cheapest, at 10 rupees.
messages.think: The prices are 60, 20, 10 and 250. The smallest is 10, the eraser.

messages.content: what is a "pirka"?
A pirka is a small, low wooden seat, only a few inches high, used in the kitchen or for sitting near the fire. In English: a low stool.
"Stationery shop: notebook 60 rupees, pen 20 rupees, eraser 10 rupees, geometry box 250 rupees." Which item is the most expensive?
The geometry box is the most expensive, at 250 rupees.
messages.think: The prices are 60, 20, 10 and 250. The biggest is 250, the geometry box.

messages.content: The bus stopped for lunch. How do I ask how long we will stay?
Ask the conductor or driver: "How long will we stop here?" or "What time does the bus leave?" Then check your watch and come back a few minutes early.

what does "aama samuha" mean?

An aama samuha is a mothers' group: women of a village or tole who meet regularly, save money together and do community work like cleaning, tree planting and helping families in need. In English: a women's group or mothers' group.
"Stationery shop: notebook 60 rupees, pen 20 rupees, eraser 10 rupees, geometry box 250 rupees." How much is a pencil?

messages.content: How do I ask what is in a dish at a restaurant?
"Excuse me, what is in this dish?" or "Is this vegetarian?" If you can't eat something: "Does it have egg in it? I don't eat egg."
How many 45-minute classes fit between 10:00 and 1:00 if there is one 30-minute break?
3 classes fit, with 15 minutes to spare.
messages.think: 10:00 to 1:00 is 3 hours, which is 180 minutes. 180 - 30 = 150 minutes for classes. 45 x 3 = 135, and 150 - 135 = 15 minutes left, not enough for another class.

messages.content: "Mother: Did you eat the apples? Son: I ate one, and Sima ate two. The rest are in the fridge." How many apples did the son eat?
The son ate one apple.
what is an "aangan"?
An aangan is the open yard in front of or around a house. Families dry grain there, children play there and guests sit there in the sun. In English: a courtyard or front yard.
"Mother: Did you eat the apples? Son: I ate one, and Sima ate two. The rest are in the fridge." Who ate two apples?
Sima ate two apples.
How do I ask the hotel for a late checkout?
Ask at the reception the evening before or in the morning: "Could I check out a little later, around (time)? Is there an extra charge for that?"
I have used 25 GB of my 40 GB data. What percent have I used?
You have used 62.5% of your data.
"Mother: Did you eat the apples? Son: I ate one, and Sima ate two. The rest are in the fridge." Where are the rest of the apples?
The rest of the apples are in the fridge.
messages.think: The son says "The rest are in the fridge."

messages.content: what is a "kausi"?
A kausi is the flat roof of a house that people use like a terrace: to dry clothes and grain, grow plants in pots, or sit in the sun. In English: a flat roof or roof terrace.
"Mother: Did you eat the apples? Son: I ate one, and Sima ate two. The rest are in the fridge." How many apples did they eat in all?
They ate 3 apples in all.
messages.think: The son ate 1 and Sima ate 2. 1 + 2 = 3.

messages.content: How do I introduce two people to each other?
Say each person's name and one small detail: "Anil, this is my colleague Rita. Rita, this is my friend Anil; we were at school together." Then they can say, "Nice to meet you."
A rectangle has a perimeter of 50 m and a length of 15 m. What is its width?
The width is 10 m.
"Yesterday it rained in Pokhara all afternoon, but Kathmandu stayed dry. Both cities were cold at night." Where did it rain?
It rained in Pokhara.

messages.content: what is a "chhapro"?
A chhapro is a small, simple hut or shed, often with a roof of straw or tin, used for shelter, storing things or a small shop. In English: a hut or shed.
"Yesterday it rained in Pokhara all afternoon, but Kathmandu stayed dry. Both cities were cold at night." Did it rain in Kathmandu?
No. It did not rain in Kathmandu; it stayed dry.
How do I give directions with "opposite", "next to" and "between"?
Use a place everyone knows: "The bank is opposite the school." "The pharmacy is next to the bank." "The post office is between the bank and the hotel." "Opposite" means across the road, facing it.

The daughter is 12 and the mother is 38.
"Yesterday it rained in Pokhara all afternoon, but Kathmandu stayed dry. Both cities were cold at night." When did it rain in Pokhara?
It rained in Pokhara all afternoon.

messages.content: what does "dhara" mean?
A dhara is a water tap or spout where people fetch water. A "dhunge dhara" is an old stone water spout, often carved, like the ones in Patan and Bhaktapur.
"Yesterday it rained in Pokhara all afternoon, but Kathmandu stayed dry. Both cities were cold at night." Which city was cold at night?
Both cities, Pokhara and Kathmandu, were cold at night.
messages.think: The text says "Both cities were cold at night."

messages.content: How do I ask a shopkeeper to keep something for me until tomorrow?
"Could you keep this for me until tomorrow? I'll come back with the money." The shopkeeper may ask for a small advance, so ask: "Do you need an advance?"
A night bus leaves at 7:30 pm and arrives at 5:15 am. How long is the trip?
The trip takes 9 hours 45 minutes.
messages.think: 7:30 pm to 5:30 am is 10 hours. 5:15 am is 15 minutes before 5:30, so the trip is 9 hours 45 minutes.

messages.content: My bus leaves at 6:30. How long will the trip take?
I can't tell from the leaving time alone. Tell me when the bus arrives, or the distance and the usual speed, and I will work out the trip time.
A 40-seat bus makes 3 trips a day with 35 passengers each trip. The fare is 60 rupees. How much fare money does it collect in a day?
The bus collects 6300 rupees a day.
messages.think: The number of seats is not needed. passengers: 3 x 35 = 105. money: 105 x 60 = 6300.

messages.content: What do I say when I give someone a gift?

"This is for you. I hope you like it." When you receive one, say: "Thank you so much! That's very kind of you." Many people in English-speaking countries open a gift in front of the giver, but in Nepal it is fine to open it later.

Sita has 10000 rupees left.

His profit is 3500 rupees.
